title: Admin screens (users, roles, audit, health, flags)
body:
## Context
**Goal.** Give the owner one coherent, RBAC-gated administration area **inside the web app** — no separate admin application — from which the entire installation can be governed: who may use it, what they may reach, what happened, whether the system is healthy, and what can be switched off in a hurry.

`00-planning-brief.md` locks the shape: "Owner/admin functions (users & roles, Bybit accounts & API keys, per-account profiles, audit log, recorder/storage, system health, feature flags) are RBAC-gated screens **inside the web app** — there is NO separate admin app." `14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 locks the access rule: "All `/admin/*` routes require role `owner` **and** an admin re-auth token ≤15 min old (SCR-149). Non-owners receive 404 from the router and 403 from the API; every admin action is audited."

**Why now (R3, Sprints 16–17).** `30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1 places E42 after `E09 --> E42`, `E27 --> E42` and `E39 --> E42`, and before `E42 --> E43`. That ordering is deliberate: the admin area governs the machinery those epics build (auth and RBAC, accounts and keys, risk caps and the kill-switch), and the security-hardening epic that follows needs an administration surface to harden. Shipping it at the end of the R3 train means the "Trading on demo" release is not merely functional but **operable** — an installation somebody can actually run, supervise and investigate.

**Modules.** M19 (Auth/RBAC/Audit — the audit read side) and M21 (Admin — users, accounts, profiles, flags, health, recorder policy), per `20-architecture.md` C14 and C15.

**The three things that make this epic hard**, and which the tickets are shaped around:
1. **It concentrates privilege.** User creation, role assignment, account binding, impersonation, feature flags, maintenance mode and backup restore all live here. A defect is not a broken screen; it is a path to controlling the installation. Hence a STRIDE model two sprints before the build (E42-X01), a white-box review of the shipped code (E42-X02), and permanently-enforcing automation (E42-X03).
2. **It must work when everything else does not.** The health screen is opened precisely when the system is degraded, so `14-screens-catalogue.md` requires it to "remain responsive when the system it is reporting on is degraded (all tiles resolve independently, no tile can block another)". That is a design constraint, an implementation constraint and a chaos-test case — E42-D05, E42-S06 and E42-Q03 respectively.
3. **The audit log's credibility is a product feature.** SCR-135 requires that "no edit or delete affordance exists anywhere", that the append-only guarantee is stated on screen, and that an integrity failure is presented as a security incident rather than a retryable error. `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1 backs it with `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE`, a hash-chain trigger, serialised appends and off-box checkpoints. This epic must not weaken any of that while making it browsable.

## Scope / Deliverables
**User stories covered (ADMIN domain, `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26):**
- **US-ADMIN-001** User management (Must) — E42-S02, E42-T04, E42-T09, E42-T10
- **US-ADMIN-002** Role assignment and account binding (Must) — E42-S03, E42-T04, E42-T08, E42-T09
- **US-ADMIN-003** Risk-limit administration (Must) — E42-S03 (the administration surface; enforcement is E39)
- **US-ADMIN-004** Owner risk dashboard (Must) — E42-S01 (the SCR-120 overview half; SCR-071 itself is E39-S04)
- **US-ADMIN-005** Trade-group administration (Must) — E42-S07 (governance over E28's SCR-062)
- **US-ADMIN-006** Recorder & retention administration (Must) — E42-S07 (admin-area mounting and audit of E16's SCR-140/141)
- **US-ADMIN-007** Feature flags (Must) — E42-S05, E42-T03
- **US-ADMIN-008** Append-only audit log (Must) — E42-S04, E42-T02
- **US-ADMIN-009** Audit log search and export (Must) — E42-S04, E42-T02, E42-K01
- **US-ADMIN-011** System health screen (Must) — E42-S06, E42-T05
- **US-ADMIN-013** Manager onboarding workflow (Should) — E42-S07
- **US-ADMIN-014** Sub-account capacity awareness (Should) — E42-S02 (users-side capacity), E42-T01

### Deferred ADMIN Must stories — where they are actually built (DoR item 3/4)
Two ADMIN-domain **Must** stories are intentionally **not** built by E42. They are named here with the exact downstream tickets that carry them to closure, so E42 cannot be read as claiming full ADMIN Must coverage on its own, and so the deferral is verifiable rather than asserted:

| Story | Screen | Owning epic | Owning tickets (verified present in the backlog) | Milestone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **US-ADMIN-010** Security posture panel (Must) | **SCR-137** Admin: security centre | **E43** Security hardening & pen-test remediation | `E43-D01` (SCR-137 wireframe→hi-fi), `E43-D02` (SCR-128 key health + SCR-136 detail), `E43-S02` (machine-evaluated posture checks + the security centre), `E43-Q01` (black-box plan), `E43-Q05` (a11y audit), `E43-X06` (key-permission/RBAC grant verification) | R4 Live enablement |
| **US-ADMIN-012** Live-trading enablement gate (Must) | SCR-137 + **SCR-145** flag console | **E44** Live-enablement gating (with the attestation half in **E43**) | `E44-D01` (gate wireframe), `E44-T04` (evidence-bound flag write), `E44-S01` (gate UI on SCR-137/SCR-145), `E44-Q01` (gating test plan); `E43-S01` (enforcement + criteria/attestation half) | R4 Live enablement |

**What E42 owes them.** E42 builds the *container and the refusal*, not the gate: the `/admin/security` route is registered in the shell (`E42-S01`) and renders a placeholder that states the panel ships in R4; the flag console (`E42-S05`, `E42-T03`) renders `trading.live_enabled` **disabled with its blocking reason**, and `E42-T03` enforces the `reason` + `evidence_url` precondition (`gate_evidence_required`) that `E44-T04` later binds evidence to. No enable path exists anywhere in E42.

**Verification.** `E42-Q06` is the standing check that this deferral is honoured: it asserts, as a repeatable test rather than a planning claim, that E42 ships no enable path, and it re-confirms against the E43/E44 backlogs that the two stories are still owned there before E42 closes. Consequently **E42 alone does not satisfy ADMIN-domain Must coverage** — the domain closes at R4 with E43 and E44, and `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012 point at those epics, not at this one.

**Screens:** SCR-120 overview · SCR-121 users list · SCR-122 user detail · SCR-123 invite · SCR-124 view-as · SCR-135 audit log · SCR-136 audit event detail · SCR-143 system health · SCR-144 incident log · SCR-145 feature flags · SCR-146 backups & restore · SCR-148 maintenance mode · SCR-149 re-auth gate · SCR-154 permission denied · plus SCR-062 governance controls and the SCR-017/SCR-123 onboarding composition.

**Components:** CMP-087 AdminLayout · CMP-088 PageHeader · CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger · CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip · CMP-099 PrintExportBar · CMP-173 AuditRow · CMP-174 AuditFilterBar · CMP-178 SystemHealthTile · CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow · CMP-210 HealthChips · plus CMP-043/044/046/047/049/050/055/065/068/092/105/138/201/204 consumed.

**API:** `GET /users` · `POST /users` · `GET|PATCH|DELETE /users/{userId}` · `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` · `GET|PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` · `GET /roles` · `GET /permissions` · `GET /admin/overview` · `GET /admin/capacity` · `GET /admin/audit` · `POST /admin/audit/verify` · `POST /admin/audit/export` · `GET /admin/health` · `GET /admin/incidents` · `GET|PUT /admin/feature-flags[/{flagKey}]` · `GET|POST /admin/backups` · `POST /admin/backups/{backupId}/verify|restore` · `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`.

**WS:** the auto-subscribed `system` topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2, §15.9 `SystemUpdate`) for health, feature-flag, kill-switch and exchange-state deltas.

**DB tables:** `users` · `roles` · `permissions` · `role_permissions` · `user_roles` · `user_account_access` · `sessions` · `mfa_methods` · `feature_flags` · `feature_flag_overrides` · `settings` · `audit_log` · `audit_checkpoints` · `system_events` · `backups`.

**Child tickets:**
- Stories: E42-S01 shell/re-auth/overview · S02 users list & invite · S03 user detail, bindings & view-as · S04 audit browser · S05 flags & maintenance · S06 health, incidents & backups · S07 onboarding & governance · S08 statechart inspector screen.
- Tasks: E42-T01 overview/capacity read models · T02 audit query/verify/export · T03 flag service & push · T04 user lifecycle contract & disable cascade · T05 health/incidents/backups wiring · T06 ADRs & docs · T07 statechart inspector read API · T08 account-access grants · T09 user read/PATCH, roles & admin sessions · T10 deferred PII purge (T08–T10 split from T04 on 2026-10-15).
- Spike: E42-K01 audit query plan and index strategy at 10 M rows.
- Design: E42-D01 research · D02 wireframes & cross-screen patterns · D03/D04/D05 hi-fi · D06 a11y review & handoff · D07 design QA.
- QA: E42-Q01 test plan & fixtures · Q02 E2E suite · Q03 perf & chaos · Q04 exploratory & regression pack · Q05 a11y audit · Q06 deferred-Must coverage & no-enable-path verification.
- Security: E42-X01 STRIDE · X02 security review · X03 abuse-case & rule automation.

**Points:** **53 engineering, 19 over the roadmap's 34** (see the update below); 41 design/QA/security tracked separately; **94 total**.

> **Engineering budget note (corrected at DoR review).** The roadmap allocates E42 **34 engineering points** (`30-release-roadmap.md` §3). The seven stories, six tasks and the spike previously totalled 38 (+11.8%); they now total **34 exactly**. The four points came off tickets that are thin wrappers over infrastructure another epic already built, not off scope:
> - `E42-S01` 3→2 — the shell is route registration and guard composition over E09's elevation primitives; no new auth logic.
> - `E42-S02` 3→2 — one table plus row actions over `GET /users`, which `E42-T04` already implements.
> - `E42-S06` 3→2 — tiles over E04's aggregate health/incidents read models; the tile pattern itself comes from `E42-S01`.
> - `E42-T03` 2→1 — CRUD plus a `system` broadcast over the existing `feature_flags` table and the E09 audit writer.
>
> No deliverable, acceptance criterion or test was removed for any of the four. Design (18 pts), QA (14 pts incl. the new `E42-Q06`) and security (9 pts) carry their own points on top and are labelled so capacity can be tracked separately, per the planning brief.
>
> **Update 2026-10-15.** The "34 exactly" above no longer holds. `E42-T07` (3) and `E42-S08` (5) were added after that review, and the R2 split of `E42-T04` on #965 added `E42-T08`, `E42-T09` and `E42-T10` (3, 5 and 3, proposed by the split's author from the slice LOC). Engineering now totals 53 against the roadmap's 34, and no decision accepts the overage yet; it is item 7 of #2710, next to the open estimates. `GET /users`, which the `E42-S02` bullet credits to `E42-T04`, has no owning ticket yet (R9 on #965).

## Out of scope
- **A separate admin application** — explicitly forbidden by `00-planning-brief.md`. Everything here is RBAC-gated routes inside the same React web app.
- **Android / any mobile client** — out of scope by owner decision 2026-09-14.
- **Authentication, sessions, TOTP, the RBAC policy decision point and the audit writer** — E09. This epic consumes them and adds no new authentication logic.
- **Bybit accounts, API keys and the key vault** (SCR-125..129) — E27. Mounted in this shell, built there.
- **Per-account profiles and the trade-group definition surface** (SCR-130..133, SCR-062) — E28. This epic adds governance controls only.
- **Risk caps, lockouts, the kill-switch, SCR-071 and SCR-134** — E39. This epic administers limits per user and surfaces state.
- **Recorder, retention and storage screens** (SCR-140..142) — E16. Mounted in this shell.
- **Security centre SCR-137, posture checks and the pen-test** — E43. **Live-enablement gating** — E44. The flag console renders `trading.live_enabled` as blocked and provides no path to enable it.
- **Metrics pipeline, probes, Grafana dashboards and alert rules** — E04. This epic is the admin surface over them.
- **The backup engine, scheduler and restore executor** — ops/E45. This epic exposes and guards them.
- **Writable impersonation** — never built. View-as is read-only by design.
- **Exchanges other than Bybit USDT linear perpetuals.**

## Acceptance criteria
Epic-level outcomes, verified end-to-end rather than per child (per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2):

```gherkin
Scenario: The installation is governable by exactly one person, safely
  Given a fresh installation with one owner
  When the owner elevates into the admin area
  Then they can create and scope a manager, set that manager's limits, see what that manager did,
       observe whether the system is healthy, switch a risky feature off, and restore from a backup
  And every one of those actions is recorded in the append-only audit log with actor, target, before and after

Scenario: Non-owners cannot reach the admin area by any route
  Given a manager and a viewer
  When every /admin/* route is visited directly, deep-linked, and called as an API
  Then the router returns 404 and the API returns 403 for every one
  And each attempt is audited

Scenario: The audit log cannot be made to lie
  When the audit area is exercised through the UI, the API and a direct database session as the application role
  Then no mutation path exists at any layer
  And an injected chain break is surfaced as a critical security incident with its position

Scenario: The admin area works when the system is degraded
  Given the recorder is down, Postgres is slow and the health endpoint returns 503
  When the owner opens the admin overview and the health screen
  Then both render within their budgets with per-tile stale and error states
  And no tile blocks another, and navigation remains usable

Scenario (failure): A safety control cannot be weakened by configuration
  Given an attempt to define a feature flag that gates authentication, RBAC or audit
  Then the service refuses to start
  And no auth, RBAC or audit module contains a flag lookup

Scenario: The deferred Must stories have an owner and no back door here
  Given US-ADMIN-010 security posture and US-ADMIN-012 live-trading enablement are deferred to E43 and E44
  When the shipped admin area is searched for any path that enables live trading or asserts security posture
  Then /admin/security renders only a placeholder naming the R4 epic
  And trading.live_enabled is rendered disabled with its blocking reason on SCR-145 and cannot be written by any API call
  And E43-S02 and E44-S01 are present in their backlogs, scheduled, and traced to US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012

Scenario (edge): The last owner cannot be removed
  Given concurrent attempts to demote or disable every owner
  Then at least one owner always remains and the losing attempt returns 409
```

**Exit criteria for the epic:**
- Every Must story listed in Scope is Done with its Gherkin criteria demonstrated; the two Should stories (US-ADMIN-013, US-ADMIN-014) are Done or explicitly descoped with a record
- **ADMIN-domain Must coverage is explicitly partial at R3**: US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012 close in R4 under E43/E44 (table above). `E42-Q06` records the verification that those tickets exist, are scheduled and are unchanged, and that E42 ships no live-enable path — the epic cannot be Done without ited disposition.
- Coverage: ≥80% frontend, ≥85% backend, **≥90% on M19/M21 security-relevant modules** (`30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- STRIDE model complete with all Critical/High findings closed (`30-release-roadmap.md` §7 R3 security gate names E42 explicitly).
- a11y: axe-core green on every admin route plus a manual screen-reader pass (E42-Q05) — no internal-tool exemption.
- Perf budgets measured and met (E42-Q03): audit first page ≤2 s at 10 M rows, SCR-120 ≤800 ms incl. with a slow subsystem, health screen ≤1 % added load.
- Design QA (E42-D07) and epic QA sign-off (E42-Q04) recorded; demoed to the Owner against staging (demo).
- ADRs merged (ADR-0021 audit index strategy, ADR-0022 admin re-auth model, and the flag-safety decision); catalogue, OpenAPI and schema docs reconciled with shipped behaviour.

## Sequencing note (added at DoR review)
The three admin read models (`E42-T01` overview/capacity, `E42-T02` audit query/verify/export, `E42-T04` user lifecycle) originally sat in **Sprint 15**, ahead of the epic's own roadmap window and ahead of their upstream data owners: **E27** Accounts & key vault lands its UI stories in S15, **E28** profiles in S15-S16 and **E39** risk caps in S15-S16. Reading a table whose owning epic is still migrating it is how a read model ends up encoding a schema that changes underneath it.

They are therefore scheduled in **Sprint 16**, inside the E42 window (`30-release-roadmap.md` §3: E42 = S16-S17), with **per-ticket** `blocked_by` on the specific upstream tickets rather than epic-level edges only:

| Ticket | Sprint | Blocked by (ticket level) | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `E42-K01` audit index spike | S15 | — | Runs against the schema in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1, which E09 already ships; deliberately early so its ADR lands before `E42-T02` starts |
| `E42-T01` overview/capacity | S16 | `E09`, `E04-T04`, `E27-T01`, `E16-T07` | Capacity reads `exchange_accounts` (E27-T01 migration) and the measured disk projection from E16's `DiskBudget` (E16-T07); the aggregate health source is E04-T04 |
| `E42-T02` audit query/verify/export | S16 | `E09`, `E42-K01` | The index set is the spike's output; building the query first would mean rebuilding it |
| `E42-T04` user lifecycle | S16 | `E09` | `E27-S04` dropped on 2026-10-15 (R1 on #965): the cascade only consumes grants. Its R2 split adds `E42-T08`, `E42-T09` and `E42-T10`, each blocked by `E42-T04` |
| `E42-S03` user detail | S16 | + `E28-T02`, `E39-T02` | Profile context beside each grant (E28-T02 profile CRUD) and the limits store (E39-T02 `risk_policy` migrations) |
| `E42-S06` health/incidents/backups | S17 | + `E04-T04` | Aggregated health endpoint |
| `E42-S07` onboarding & governance | S17 | `E27-S01`, `E28-S03`, `E16-S03` | Mounts the accounts, trade-group and retention surfaces it governs |

Sprint 16 is consequently backend-first: the three tasks are expected to merge in the first half of the sprint, with `E42-S02`/`S03`/`S04` consuming them in the second. If any upstream slips, the affected task slips with it rather than being built against a provisional schema.

## Technical notes / design
**Architecture.** Two backend modules: **M19** (Auth/RBAC/Audit — this epic owns the audit *read* side; the writer and chain are E09/schema) and **M21** (Admin — `20-architecture.md` C15: "Users/roles, Bybit accounts + keys, per-account profiles, feature flags, recorder policy, system health"). The frontend is one route tree under `/admin/*` inside `apps/web`, sharing the application's design system, data layer and WS connection.

**Four cross-cutting decisions that every child ticket inherits:**

1. **Elevation model.** Owner role **plus** a server-issued 15-minute admin token. Guard order `requireAuth → requireRole('owner') → requireFreshAdminToken`. Role failure renders the **router 404** (non-disclosure); staleness renders the **SCR-149 gate** as a portal overlay, never a route swap — so an in-progress form survives, its save is held, and it resumes after elevation. The client cannot extend the TTL. Recorded as ADR-0022 (E42-T06).

2. **Everything is audited, including reading.** Every state-changing control composes **CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger**; every admin route emits `admin.area_entered`; and per SCR-136, viewing and exporting audit records are themselves audited. Enforcement is a Semgrep rule (E42-X03), not discipline.

3. **Nothing is enforced in the client.** Manager scoping on the audit query lives in the repository layer; account-access grants are server-authoritative with replace semantics; flag resolution is server-side; restore preconditions are enforced in the service. The UI renders denials, it does not create them.

4. **Independent resolution.** Both aggregate screens (SCR-120, SCR-143) are built as independent tiles over one snapshot plus the auto-subscribed `system` topic — never a page-level fetch-all. This is what lets the admin area stay usable during the incidents it exists to diagnose, and it is asserted by chaos tests rather than assumed.

**Data flow.** REST snapshot on mount → WS `system` deltas (1 000 ms throttle, auto-subscribed, un-unsubscribable per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2) → per-tile state with `lastGoodAt`. No admin screen creates a polling timer; that is how the ≤1 % added-load NFR is met structurally rather than by tuning.

**Error codes surfaced across the epic:** `stepup_required` · `forbidden` · `conflict` (last owner, restore preconditions, concurrent write) · `validation_failed` · `gate_evidence_required` · `rate_limited` · `account_scope_denied`.

## Test plan
Per `03-testing-strategy.md`, all layers apply:
- **Unit** — ≥80% frontend, ≥85% backend, ≥90% on M19/M21; ships with each story/task.
- **Contract** — schemathesis/MSW over every `/admin/*` and `/users*` path plus `SystemUpdate` frame validation.
- **Integration** — seeded Postgres incl. a 10 M-row audit dataset; stubbed subsystem services for the degraded paths.
- **E2E (Playwright)** — E42-Q02, including a **cross-session harness** (owner context + manager context) for the timing guarantees that cannot be tested any other way, and a route-enumerating guard spec that fails when a new admin route lacks a guard.
- **Perf/load** — E42-Q03: audit query at 10 M rows, export under concurrent load, overview/health render with a failing subsystem, added-load measurement.
- **Chaos** — E42-Q03: health endpoint 503, WS disconnect, Postgres latency, injected chain break, failed backup verification, flag store unreachable.
- **Security** — E42-X03: RBAC assertion matrix (route × role × elevation), automated abuse cases, Semgrep rules, authenticated ZAP scans.
- **a11y** — E42-Q05: axe-core in CI on every route/state plus two-screen-reader manual passes against a written script.
- **Exploratory** — E42-Q04: six timeboxed charters, then a standing regression pack.

## Security notes
**Classification.** PII (usernames, emails, `actor_ip`), Confidential (grants, limits, audit contents, operational state), Secret-adjacent (backup artefacts containing envelope-encrypted key material — handled, never decrypted here). No API-key material is rendered by any screen in this epic.

**Named in the R3 security gate.** `30-release-roadmap.md` §7: "STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 — all Critical/High closed; a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes."

**Principal threats and their controls:**
- *Elevation of privilege* — deny-by-default RBAC, owner-only routes, 15-minute elevation, router-404 non-disclosure, replace-semantics grants, last-owner protection under a row lock, read-only impersonation. Asserted continuously by E42-X03's route × role × elevation matrix.
- *Tampering with the audit trail* — database grants **and** a `forbid_mutation` trigger (verified independently of the application in E42-X02), hash chaining, serialised appends, off-box checkpoints, an integrity check surfaced as a critical incident.
- *Configuration as an attack surface* — the compile-time flag registry that refuses to start if a flag declares it gates auth, RBAC, audit, a risk invariant or rate limiting, plus a Semgrep rule forbidding flag lookups in those modules. This is the concrete implementation of US-ADMIN-007's "no flag may weaken a security control".
- *Information disclosure* — fingerprint-only rendering of secret-bearing diffs, server-side redaction at write time preserved through export, signed short-lived single-use download URLs, health payloads restricted to the schema's fields, and no admin-route existence disclosure to non-owners.
- *Destruction* — restore and purge require maintenance mode, typed confirmation, step-up and high-severity audit, with server-side preconditions that do not trust the UI.
- *Denial of service* — export range and rate limits, last-owner protection, step-up on maintenance mode so it cannot be used to halt trading casually.

Every ticket in this epic carries the `security` label implicitly under `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8; reviewers must block Done if a Security-engineer review comment is missing.

## Accessibility notes
WCAG 2.2 AA across all fifteen screens, with **no internal-tool exemption** (`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 states this explicitly for admin screens).

Epic-level commitments:
- Status, severity, role and outcome are always **text**, never colour alone; greyscale proofs are part of design sign-off.
- The admin tint is paired with an `aria-label="Admin area"` landmark and the page header, so the area is identifiable without colour.
- Interrupting patterns are handled deliberately: the re-auth gate is an `alertdialog` with focus trapped and returned; the countdown announces at thresholds, not per tick; the integrity-failure alert announces once then persists; live health updates are coalesced so a flapping subsystem does not flood a screen reader.
- Every sparkline has a table alternative; every diff is a labelled definition list; every typed-confirmation field states its expected value in text.
- Keyboard paths are documented pre-build (E42-D06), automated for the highest-risk flows (E42-Q02) and audited post-build with two screen readers (E42-Q05).
- Disabled-for-RBAC controls expose their reason via `aria-describedby` — **and** are enforced server-side, since an accessible explanation of a fake restriction is still a security defect.

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and the screen catalogue, all measured in E42-Q03:
- **SCR-120** overview: ≤800 ms render, never blocking on the slowest subsystem; each tile has its own timeout and error state.
- **SCR-135** audit: ≤2 s first page over 10 M entries (US-ADMIN-009 NFR), ≤400 ms filter round-trip for common combinations, 200 rows per page, keyset pagination only.
- **SCR-136**: ≤300 ms single-record fetch, lazy raw-payload expansion.
- **SCR-143** health: ≤1 % added server load (US-ADMIN-011 NFR) achieved structurally — one snapshot GET plus the already-open `system` subscription, no polling — and ≤2 ms scripting per frame.
- **SCR-144** incidents: 10k rows scrolling without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame.
- **SCR-149**: token issue ≤400 ms.
- **Propagation**: flag change visible to all users ≤10 s; maintenance broadcast ≤2 s with order blocking ≤200 ms server-side; session revocation ≤5 s.
- The audit index strategy is settled by measurement (E42-K01 → ADR-0021) before E42-T02 implements, including the write-path overhead the audit path pays on every state-changing request.

## Observability
**Audit actions added or surfaced:** `admin.area_entered` · `admin.session_elevated` · `admin.access_denied` · `admin.view_as_started|ended` (high) · `users.create|disable|enable|delete|anonymise` · `users.access_change` · `roles.grant|revoke` · `auth.session_revoked` · `auth.mfa_reset` · `audit.viewed|record_viewed|exported|integrity_check_run` · `flags.change` (high) · `maintenance.enabled|disabled` · `incident.acknowledged` · `backup.run|verified|restore|downloaded|deleted` (restore and download high) · `trade_group.enabled|disabled|renamed|reordered` · `user.onboarding_started|resumed|completed`.

**Metrics:** `cv_admin_overview_source_duration_seconds{source}` · `cv_admin_overview_render_ms` · `cv_admin_stepup_total{result}` · `cv_audit_query_duration_seconds{filter_class}` · `cv_audit_export_jobs_total{result}` · **`cv_audit_chain_verified`** (gauge; `0` pages immediately per ADR-0014) · `cv_feature_flag_changes_total{key,result}` · `cv_flag_push_latency_seconds` · `cv_maintenance_mode` · `cv_user_lifecycle_total{action,result}` · `auth_revocation_latency_seconds` (E09-S03's, reused) · `cv_incidents_open` · **`cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds`** (alerts past the schedule interval) · `cv_restore_jobs_total{result}`.

**Principle carried through every ticket:** a denial must be observable. Every 403, every failed elevation and every refused destructive action produces both an audit entry and a metric increment — E42-X03 fails the build if a denial is silent.

- [ ] Every child Story/Task/Spike/Design/QA/Security ticket is Done (100% rollup), or explicitly descoped with a Won't/Later disposition recorded here.

- [ ] Coverage rolled up: ≥80% frontend, ≥85% backend, ≥90% on M19/M21; no open P0/P1 bugs in this epic's scope.
- [ ] Docs updated to shipped reality: `14-screens-catalogue.md`, `15-component-catalogue.md`, `22-api-openapi.yaml`, `21-database-schema.md`, plus ADR-0021/0022 (E42-T06).
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on every admin route; two-screen-reader manual passes recorded (E42-Q05); all serious/critical findings closed.
- [ ] perf: E42-Q03 report published with measured values beside every budget listed above.
- [ ] security: STRIDE model finalised (E42-X01), implementation review complete (E42-X02), automation enforcing in CI (E42-X03); all Critical/High findings fixed or accepted with Owner sign-off; Security-engineer sign-off comment present.
- [ ] design: CDO sign-off on the hi-fi set; design QA (E42-D07) complete with every discrepancy fixed or filed.
- [ ] QA: epic-level regression and exploratory pass executed and recorded (E42-Q04) with a sign-off comment.

This epic consumes all of it and adds no new authentication logic. (`30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E09 --> E42`.)

title: Build the admin shell, re-auth gate and SCR-120 admin overview
body:
## Context
Every other screen in this epic lives inside one RBAC-gated shell. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 states the rule for the whole `/admin/*` band: "All `/admin/*` routes require role `owner` **and** an admin re-auth token ≤15 min old (SCR-149). Non-owners receive 404 from the router and 403 from the API; every admin action is audited." §0 of the same document repeats it as a global convention ("whole admin areas … are hidden from navigation and hard-404 for non-owners").

This story builds that shell — **CMP-087 AdminLayout** with its re-auth freshness badge — the **SCR-149** re-authentication gate as the route guard, and **SCR-120 Admin home / overview**, the landing page whose tiles link to every other admin area and which is the first thing the owner sees. It covers the navigation half of **US-ADMIN-001**, **US-ADMIN-004** and **US-ADMIN-011** (each of which names SCR-120 in `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26); the full screens behind those tiles are E42-S02/S03, E39-S04 and E42-S06.

Design is signed off in E42-D03 (Sprint 14), two sprints ahead, per the design-ahead rule in `00-planning-brief.md`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Route tree `/admin`, `/admin/users`, `/admin/users/:userId`, `/admin/audit`, `/admin/flags`, `/admin/health`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/security`, `/admin/accounts`, `/admin/profiles`, `/admin/recorder`, `/admin/risk-policy` registered in the web app router (`12-sitemap.md`), each rendered inside **CMP-087 AdminLayout**; pages owned by other epics (SCR-125 E27, SCR-130..133 E28, SCR-134 E39, SCR-140..142 E16, SCR-137 E43) mount into the same shell — this story owns only the shell contract, not those pages.
- **SCR-149 Admin re-authentication gate**: route guard that, on first entry to any `/admin/*` route when the admin token is older than 15 minutes, renders the password + TOTP dialog (CMP-043 Dialog, CMP-201 PasswordField, CMP-204 OtpInput, CMP-027 ErrorState) explaining why re-authentication is required and how long the resulting token lasts. On success admin routes unlock for 15 minutes of activity. Backed by the step-up endpoint delivered by E09; this story consumes it.
- Re-auth **freshness countdown** in the admin chrome (CMP-035 Countdown pattern) so expiry is never a surprise; expiry **during** an admin edit preserves the form's content and holds the save until re-auth succeeds (explicit requirement in the SCR-149 sign-off checklist).
- **SCR-120 Admin home / overview** at `/admin`: independent tiles for users, accounts, keys needing rotation, recorder, storage, health, flags and last backup, fed by `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` (E42-T01) plus live tiles from the WS `system` topic. Each tile resolves **independently** with its own loading, error and degraded state; no tile may block another. Components: CMP-050 Card, CMP-087 AdminLayout, CMP-088 PageHeader, CMP-138 RiskCapMeter, CMP-173 AuditRow (recent-activity tile), CMP-178 SystemHealthTile.
- Left-rail "Admin" entry (SCR-011 navigation) rendered **only** for `owner`; absent — not disabled — for manager/viewer.
- **SCR-154 Permission denied (403)** wiring for the API-level denial path (US-ADMIN-002 lists SCR-154): a manager who reaches an admin API through a stale deep link sees the 403 screen with a route back to the trading app, never a dead end.
- Analytics/audit emission: `admin.overview_viewed` (analytics) and the **audited** `admin.area_entered {route, reauthTokenAge}` on entering any admin route, plus `admin.session_elevated` on a successful gate pass.

## Out of scope
- The step-up/TOTP backend itself (E09) — consumed here.
- The contents of the screens the tiles link to (E42-S02..S07, E16, E27, E28, E39, E43).
- **The security posture panel itself (US-ADMIN-010 / SCR-137) — E43-S02.** This story registers the `/admin/security` route and renders a **placeholder card** only: title "Security centre", body "Security posture checks ship in R4 (E43)", and a link to the audit log. The route exists so the shell's navigation, RBAC guard and re-auth gate are complete and so E43 mounts into a finished container rather than editing the shell.
- "View as" impersonation (E42-S03) and the audit browser (E42-S04).
- `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` implementation (E42-T01).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Owner enters the admin area with a stale token
  Given I am signed in as owner and my admin re-auth token is 20 minutes old
  When I navigate to /admin
  Then the SCR-149 gate is shown as role="alertdialog" explaining why re-authentication is required and that the token lasts 15 minutes
  And on entering a correct password and TOTP the admin area renders
  And an audited admin.session_elevated entry exists with my actor id and the target route

Scenario: Non-owner cannot reach the admin area
  Given I am signed in as a manager
  Then no "Admin" item appears in the left rail
  And navigating directly to /admin/users renders the router 404 surface
  And any XHR the page would have made returns 403 with an audit entry recorded server-side

Scenario: Overview tiles resolve independently
  Given the recorder subsystem is unreachable and every other subsystem is healthy
  When I open /admin
  Then the recorder tile shows its own error state with a retry action
  And every other tile renders its value normally within 800 ms

Scenario (failure): Re-auth expires mid-edit
  Given I am editing a form on an admin screen and the re-auth countdown reaches zero
  When I press Save
  Then the save is held, the gate is shown, and after a successful re-auth the save proceeds with my unchanged form content

Scenario (edge): Backend degraded
  Given GET /api/v1/admin/overview returns 503
  Then the page renders the error state with the last-known values marked stale and a retry control
  And the admin shell itself, including navigation, remains usable
```

## Technical notes / design
- `AdminRouteGuard` HOC: reads `reauth_expires_at` from the session bootstrap (`GET /api/v1/me`), and on a `401`/`403` with error code `stepup_required` opens the gate rather than logging the user out. Token TTL is **server-issued**; the client never extends it.
- Guard order: `requireAuth → requireRole('owner') → requireFreshAdminToken`. Role check failure renders the router 404 (deliberate non-disclosure); token staleness renders the gate.
- Pending-save queue: the guard exposes `withFreshAdminToken(fn)`; forms call it instead of `fetch` so a mid-edit expiry re-runs the same closure after elevation. Form state lives in the page component and is never unmounted by the gate (the gate is a portal overlay, not a route swap).
- `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` → `AdminOverview` schema; each tile subscribes to its own slice and holds its own `status: idle|loading|ok|error|stale`. Tiles additionally patch from the auto-subscribed WS `system` topic (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2: "`system` is auto-subscribed … A client may not unsubscribe from it"), `kind` in `health|feature_flags|kill_switch|exchange_state`.
- Admin surface tint token `color.surface.admin-tint` (CMP-087) distinguishes the admin area from the trading app; the distinction must survive greyscale, so it is paired with the "Admin area" landmark label and the page header.
- Error codes surfaced: `stepup_required`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited` (gate brute-force protection is E09's).

## Test plan
- **Unit (Vitest + RTL)**: guard matrix (owner/manager/viewer × fresh/stale token × direct-URL/nav) — 12 cases; countdown formatting and its `aria-live` politeness; pending-save closure re-runs exactly once after elevation; tile state machine transitions incl. `ok → stale` on WS gap.
- **Contract**: MSW handlers generated from `22-api-openapi.yaml` for `/admin/overview` and `/me`; a schema-drift test fails if the response shape changes.
- **Integration**: overview page with one failing tile endpoint — asserts isolation.
- **E2E (Playwright)**: `admin-shell.spec.ts` — owner elevation happy path; manager hard-404; mid-edit expiry preserving form content; deep-link to `/admin/audit` while stale.
- **a11y**: axe-core on `/admin` and on the open gate; keyboard-only traversal of the tile grid.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/overview.ok.json`, `overview.degraded.json`, `me.owner.stale-token.json`.
- Coverage target: ≥80% lines on `apps/web/src/features/admin/shell`.

## Security notes
- Threats (`docs/plan/04-security-program.md`): **elevation of privilege** — a manager reaching admin routes by URL guessing; mitigated by server-side deny-by-default, router 404 and API 403 with an audit entry (never rely on hidden navigation). **Information disclosure** — a 403 that confirms an admin route exists; mitigated by the 404-from-router / 403-from-API split specified in `14-screens-catalogue.md` §10.
- **Session hijack / stale elevation**: the 15-minute admin token is bound server-side to the session; the client cannot extend it and never stores it outside memory.
- Data classification: the overview contains **Confidential** operational counts; no secrets, no key material, no PII beyond usernames.
- Requires the `security` label and a Security-engineer review comment (DoD cross-kind rule §8 — any ticket touching `area/auth-rbac`-adjacent RBAC enforcement).

## Accessibility notes
- Admin shell is an `aria-label="Admin area"` landmark (CMP-087 contract).
- SCR-149 gate is `role="alertdialog"` with a labelled TOTP field carrying a format hint; failures announced assertively; focus trapped in the dialog and restored to the triggering element on close.
- The re-auth countdown is text (not colour), announced politely at 5 min and 1 min only — never on every tick.
- Tiles: each is a labelled region with a heading; state is a word ("Degraded"), never colour alone; the tile grid is a single tab stop sequence in DOM order.
- Cancel from the gate returns to the non-admin app, not to a dead end (SCR-149 sign-off checklist).
- WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`; the admin tint must keep ≥4.5:1 text contrast.

## Performance notes
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-120: the overview "must render in <=800 ms and never block on the slowest subsystem"; each tile has its own 3 s timeout after which it renders an error state.
- SCR-149: token issue ≤400 ms.
- Budget from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: admin routes are non-trading surfaces — ≤2 ms scripting per frame at idle, no polling loops (live values come from the already-open `system` subscription, not from new timers).

## Observability
- Audit: `admin.area_entered {route, reauthTokenAge}`, `admin.session_elevated`, and the denial path `admin.access_denied {route, role}` (severity `warning`).
- Analytics: `admin.overview_viewed`.
- Metrics: `cv_admin_overview_render_ms` (client RUM histogram), `cv_admin_stepup_total{result}`.
- Logs: structured entry per elevation with `request_id`, correlating to the audit row.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched routes, keyboard-only pass, one manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- **E43-S02 / E43-D01** consume the `/admin/security` route this story registers (placeholder here, panel there) — US-ADMIN-010 is *not* satisfied by this ticket.

- `E42-D03` — hi-fi design for SCR-120 and the shell must be Done (design-ahead rule).
- `E42-T01` — `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` must exist for the tiles.
- `E09` — auth, sessions, TOTP and the step-up/elevation endpoint plus the RBAC policy decision point; this story consumes them and adds no new auth logic.

## Branch

title: Build SCR-121 users list and SCR-123 invite user with lifecycle actions
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-001 — User management (Must)**: "As the owner, I want to create, edit, disable and delete app users, so that I control who can reach the terminal." Its three Gherkin scenarios are non-negotiable: a created user is *pending until they redeem their invite*; disabling revokes sessions **within 5 seconds**, disarms their rules and retains their data; deleting retains audit and journal history under an **anonymised reference** and the deletion itself is audited. The NFR adds: "step-up authentication required; user list is a keyboard-navigable table with clear status text."

This story builds **SCR-121 Admin: users list** (`/admin/users`) and **SCR-123 Admin: invite user**. It also renders the sub-account/user **capacity constraint** required by the SCR-121 sign-off checklist, which is the list-side half of **US-ADMIN-014** (the accounts-side half is E27's SCR-125).

The server-side lifecycle semantics are split across E42-T04 (the disable cascade with ≤5 s session revocation), E42-T09 (re-enable through `PATCH`) and E42-T10 (the anonymised delete behind `?purge=true`) since the R2 split of 2026-10-15 on #965; this story is the surface plus its confirmations.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-121** at `/admin/users`: CMP-049 Table of users with columns username, display name, email, role, status (`invited|active|disabled`), MFA state, last seen, granted accounts count; CMP-055 FilterBar (role, status, free-text `q`); CMP-011 Tag/Chip for role and status; CMP-013 Avatar/ProfileBadge. Data: `GET /api/v1/users` (cursor + limit + `status`/`role`/`q` params) and `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity`.
- Capacity line per the sign-off checklist: users against the operative sub-account cap context (5 regular / 20 with Business KYC, from `CapacityReport`) with the assumed tier stated as a recorded fact, never inferred (US-ADMIN-014 NFR).
- Row actions, each step-up gated and wrapped in **CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger**: Edit (→ SCR-122, E42-S03), **Disable**, **Re-enable**, **Delete**, **Resend invite**, **Revoke invite**, **View as** entry point (the impersonation screen itself is E42-S03).
- **Disable** confirmation (CMP-044 ConfirmDialog) stating exactly what happens: sessions revoked within 5 s, armed rules disarmed, data retained, the user can be re-enabled.
- **Delete** confirmation: typed confirmation of the username; copy states that audit and journal history is retained under an anonymised reference and that the deletion is audited. Calls `DELETE /api/v1/users/{userId}` (soft) and, when the owner opts in, `?purge=true` for PII anonymisation after the 90-day retention window.
- Last-owner protection surfaced in the UI: the owner's own row cannot be demoted or disabled — the control is **disabled with a reason tooltip**, not hidden (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §0 RBAC rule), matching the server's `conflict` response.
- **SCR-123** invite flow: `POST /api/v1/users` with username, email, roles, `mfa_required`, and initial `account_access` grants; returns `UserWithInvite` with a one-time link valid 72 h. The link is shown once with CMP-033 CopyButton and an explicit "this link is shown once" statement; it is never re-displayed, only re-issued.
- States for both screens: loading (CMP-015 Skeleton) · populated · filtered-to-nothing (CMP-026 EmptyState per the SCR-151 pattern) · error · invite-pending · action-in-flight · optimistic-rollback on failure.
- Audit events emitted and asserted: `users.create`, `users.disable`, `users.enable`, `users.delete`, `user.invited`, `user.invite_revoked`.

## Out of scope
- SCR-122 user detail, role/account binding editing, session revocation UI, "view as" (E42-S03).
- Backend lifecycle cascade (E42-T04), re-enable (E42-T09) and anonymisation (E42-T10).
- The guided manager onboarding wizard (E42-S07) — this screen exposes the plain invite; the wizard is a separate, richer flow.
- Bybit sub-account creation (E27) and per-account profiles (E28).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Create and assign role
  Given I am the owner on /admin/users
  When I invite a user with role manager
  Then they appear in the list with status "Invited" until they redeem their invite
  And the one-time invite link is displayed once with a copy control and a statement that it will not be shown again
  And an audited users.create entry records actor, target and the assigned roles

Scenario: Disable revokes access quickly
  Given manager M has an active session and one armed rule
  When I disable M and confirm
  Then M's sessions are revoked within 5 seconds
  And M's rules are shown as disarmed
  And M's data is retained and M's row shows status "Disabled" with a Re-enable action

Scenario: Delete with history
  When I delete user M and type M's username to confirm
  Then M's audit and journal history remains, attributed to an anonymised reference
  And an audited users.delete entry exists
  And M no longer appears in the default list but appears under the "Disabled/Deleted" filter

Scenario (failure): Last owner protection
  Given I am the only owner
  Then the Disable and Delete controls on my own row are disabled with a tooltip explaining that the last owner is protected
  And issuing the request directly returns 409 conflict and is audited as a denied action

Scenario (edge): Capacity reached
  Given the recorded account tier is "regular" and 5 sub-accounts are in use
  Then the capacity line states 5 of 5 used with the assumed tier named
  And the explanation of the Business KYC path and the isolation trade-off of sharing a sub-account is shown

Scenario (failure): Step-up expired during a destructive action
  Given my admin re-auth token expires while the delete confirmation is open
  When I confirm
  Then the re-auth gate appears and, after success, the delete proceeds exactly once (idempotency key reused)
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data layer: `useUsers({cursor, limit, status, role, q})` over `GET /api/v1/users`; cursor pagination only (no offset), page size 50. Filters are server-side; the client never filters a partial page for correctness.
- Mutations use the `Idempotency-Key` header (`x-idempotency: recommended` on `POST /users`) so a retry after a step-up interruption cannot double-invite; the key is generated once per confirmation dialog instance.
- `PATCH /api/v1/users/{userId}` uses `If-Match` with the row ETag; a `412` renders "This user changed while you were editing" with a reload action rather than overwriting.
- Disable → `DELETE /api/v1/users/{userId}` (soft: `status=disabled`, sessions and grants revoked server-side). Purge → same route with `?purge=true`. Re-enable → `PATCH {status: active}`.
- Invite link handling: rendered from the `UserWithInvite` response in memory only — never written to localStorage, never logged, never included in analytics payloads.
- All destructive controls compose **CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger** with `action`, `target`, `before`, `after` so the integration test in the component catalogue's contract applies here.
- Error codes: `conflict` (last owner, duplicate username/email), `validation_failed`, `stepup_required`, `forbidden`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter/query-param mapping; ETag conflict handling; idempotency-key stability across a step-up interruption; capacity-line copy for tiers regular/business and at/below cap; last-owner control disabling; invite link never persisted (assert no storage writes).
- **Contract**: MSW from `22-api-openapi.yaml` for `/users` GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE and `/admin/capacity`; drift test.
- **Integration**: disable flow asserts the confirmation copy enumerates session revocation, rule disarming and data retention.
- **E2E (Playwright)** `admin-users.spec.ts`: invite → pending row → redeem (second browser context) → active; disable with a live second session asserting it is dropped within 5 s; delete with typed confirm; last-owner guard.
- **a11y**: axe on both screens; keyboard-only invite and delete; screen-reader pass on the table (status as text) and the typed-confirm dialog.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/users.page1.json`, `users.empty-filter.json`, `capacity.regular-at-cap.json`, `user.invite.json`.
- Coverage ≥80% on `apps/web/src/features/admin/users`.

## Security notes
- Threats: **privilege escalation** via crafted role payloads (server is authoritative; the client sends role names only from `GET /roles`); **information disclosure** of the invite link (shown once, memory-only, excluded from analytics and logs); **denial of service on the owner account** (last-owner protection server-side, 409); **spoofing** via invite-link replay (72 h TTL, single use, invalidated on revoke — enforced by E09/E42-T04).
- Data classification: usernames and emails are **PII** (`21-database-schema.md` comment on `users.email`: "PII: contact identifier; purge on account erase"); `password_hash` is never returned by the API and must never appear in a fixture.
- Every destructive action is step-up gated (`04-security-program.md` SR-025 pattern) and audited; `security` label required, Security-engineer review comment required before Done.

## Accessibility notes
- Table is keyboard-navigable with visible focus, sortable headers exposed as buttons with `aria-sort`, and **status rendered as text** ("Invited", "Active", "Disabled") — never a coloured dot alone (US-ADMIN-001 NFR).
- Destructive dialogs are `role="alertdialog"` with focus trapped, the typed-confirm field labelled, and the consequence list rendered as a `<ul>` read in full by the screen reader.
- Disabled controls carry a `title`+`aria-describedby` reason, satisfying the "disabled with a reason tooltip, not hidden" rule.
- Empty and filtered-to-nothing states follow SCR-151: heading, one sentence of cause, one action.
- Invite link region is `aria-live="polite"` with a copy button whose success is announced.

## Performance notes
- List first page ≤500 ms p95 over 200 users; cursor pagination, no client-side sorting of a partial set.
- No polling: status changes arrive over the `system`/session invalidation path already open.
- Table virtualisation is unnecessary at this scale (owner + a few managers) — explicitly not implemented; an inline comment records why, so a future reviewer does not add it speculatively.

## Observability
- Audit: `users.create`, `users.disable`, `users.enable`, `users.delete`, `user.invited`, `user.invite_revoked` — each with `before_state`/`after_state` redacted of secrets.
- Analytics: `admin.users_list_viewed {rowCount, filters}`.
- Metrics: `cv_admin_user_mutation_total{action,result}`.

- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.

- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies

Since the R2 split on #965 the anonymised delete (`?purge=true`) is E42-T10 and re-enable is E42-T09. Both sit in Sprint 19, so they are not in `blocked_by` (adding them fails SPRINT-ORDER), and the delete-with-purge and re-enable criteria cannot pass before they land. title: Build SCR-122 user detail with role/account binding, limits and SCR-124 view-as
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-002 — Role assignment and account binding (Must)** is the isolation boundary of the whole product: "bindings are the single source of truth for scoping on every API route." Its scenarios require that binding manager M to sub-account S lets M see and trade **only** S subject to S's profile; that a second binding appears in M's scope selector *and* in server-side scoping; and that **unbinding with open positions forces an explicit choice** — leave the positions (owner takes over) or flatten first.

**US-ADMIN-003 — Risk-limit administration (Must)** adds the per-manager limits surface on the same screen (SCR-122 is listed for both in `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26), with the hard rule that tightening a limit during an open position **never force-liquidates**: new entries are blocked, reduce-only remains available, and both owner and manager are informed. Each change is audited with old and new values.

**SCR-124 Admin: "view as" (read-only impersonation)** is listed under US-ADMIN-002/US-ADMIN-008 and audited at high severity (`admin.view_as_started|ended`).

The enforcement engines live elsewhere — `user_account_access` scoping in E09, per-account risk caps in **E39** (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11.1: `E39 --> E42`), profiles in **E28**. This story is the owner-facing administration surface over them and the safety semantics of changing them.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-122** at `/admin/users/:userId`: identity block; role selector (CMP-009 Select, options from `GET /api/v1/roles`); **account assignments** table with per-account permission level (`trade` / `read`) via CMP-105 AccountMultiSelect, driven by `GET|PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/account-access`; rule-authoring permission; live-trading permission per account; **risk-cap overrides** (CMP-138 RiskCapMeter showing the current measured value beside each limit); session list with per-session revoke (`GET /api/v1/me/sessions` equivalent admin view + `DELETE`); 2FA state with reset; and the user's own audit trail (a filtered embed of E42-S04's list).
- Role changes call `PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/roles`; account bindings call `PUT /api/v1/users/{userId}/account-access` (full replace semantics — the UI must send the complete grant set, and shows a change summary before saving).
- **Unbind-with-open-positions flow**: before saving a grant removal, the UI calls the positions read model for the affected account; if positions are open, a blocking choice is presented — *Leave positions (owner takes over)* or *Flatten first* — with no third silent path, and the chosen option is recorded in the audit `after_state`.
- **Limit tightening flow**: on save, if the new cap is below current exposure, an explicit notice states "No positions will be closed. New entries are blocked; reduce-only actions remain available." Both the owner's confirmation and the manager's notification are produced (the manager-facing notice is rendered by E39's CMP-117 RiskLockoutBanner, consumed here).
- **SCR-124 view-as**: entry from SCR-121/SCR-122, an unmistakable persistent banner (CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner + CMP-028 Callout) naming the impersonated user, a **read-only** mode in which every state-changing control is disabled with a reason, and an always-visible Exit control. Emits audited `admin.view_as_started` / `admin.view_as_ended` at high severity.
- All saves step-up gated and wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger; audit actions `roles.grant`, `roles.revoke`, `users.access_change`, `risk.limits_changed`, `auth.mfa_reset`, `auth.session_revoked` (vocabulary per R5 on #965).
- States: loading · populated · dirty-with-change-summary · saving · conflict (412) · error · self-edit guard (owner cannot demote themselves) · impersonating.

## Out of scope
- The risk-evaluation engine, lockout behaviour and the risk dashboard SCR-071 (E39).
- Per-account profiles SCR-130..133 (E28) — linked to from here, not edited here.
- Bybit account/key management SCR-125..129 (E27).
- Writable impersonation — explicitly never built; view-as is read-only by design.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Bind a manager to a sub-account
  Given manager M has no account grants
  When I grant M trade access to sub-account S and save with step-up
  Then M can see and trade only S, subject to S's profile
  And the change is audited with the full before and after grant sets

Scenario: Multiple bindings
  When I add a second sub-account grant for M
  Then both accounts appear in M's scope selector on next request
  And server-side scoping covers both, verified by M's own /me response

Scenario: Unbind with open positions
  Given M holds open positions on S
  When I remove M's grant for S
  Then the save is blocked until I choose explicitly: leave the positions (owner takes over) or flatten first
  And the chosen option is recorded in the audit entry

Scenario: Tighten a limit during an open position
  Given M's current exposure exceeds the new maximum position size
  When I save the tightened limit
  Then no position is closed
  And new entries for M are blocked while reduce-only actions remain available
  And both the owner and M are informed, and the change is audited with old and new values

Scenario: View-as is unmistakably read-only
  When I start "view as" for M
  Then a persistent banner names M and states the session is read-only
  And every state-changing control is disabled with a reason
  And admin.view_as_started is audited at high severity, and admin.view_as_ended on exit

Scenario (failure): Concurrent edit
  Given another owner session changed M's roles after I loaded the page
  When I save
  Then a 412 is surfaced as "This user changed while you were editing" with a reload action
  And my change is not applied silently
```

## Technical notes / design
- Grant editing is **replace-semantics**: `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` takes the full `grants` array. The UI computes an added/removed/changed diff purely for the confirmation summary; the payload is always complete.
- Revoked grants force-close the user's WS subscriptions with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), which E42-T08 delivers; E42-T04's contract slice S1 replaces the older `unsubscribed` wording in `22-api-openapi.yaml`. The UI states this in the confirmation copy so the owner knows the effect is immediate.
- Open-position check before unbinding reads the positions read model for the affected account scope; if the check itself fails, the save is blocked (fail-closed) with a retry — never assumed to be zero.
- Limit tightening posts through the E39 risk-administration endpoint; the client renders the returned "effect summary" rather than predicting it locally.
- Optimistic concurrency via `If-Match`/ETag on `PATCH /users/{userId}`.
- View-as: the server issues a **read-only impersonation context**; the client marks the whole app tree with an `impersonation` provider that disables mutations at the request layer as well as visually — defence in depth, but the server remains authoritative (any mutation attempted under impersonation is rejected and audited).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: grant diff → confirmation summary; fail-closed behaviour when the open-position check errors; tightening notice copy; ETag conflict path; impersonation provider disabling every mutation hook.
- **Contract**: `/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/roles`, `/users/{userId}/account-access`, `/roles`, `/permissions` against the OpenAPI schema.
- **Integration**: unbind-with-open-positions renders exactly two choices and no dismissal path.
- **E2E**: `admin-user-detail.spec.ts` — bind/unbind across two browser contexts asserting M's scope changes without a reload; view-as session asserting no mutation is possible and both audit entries exist; tighten-limit asserting no position closes.
- **Security test (with E42-X02)**: attempt a grant payload naming an account the owner does not administer → 403 + audit.
- **a11y**: axe; keyboard-only grant editing; screen-reader pass on the change summary and the unbind choice dialog.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/user.detail.json`, `account-access.two-grants.json`, `positions.open-on-S.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- This is the **isolation boundary between managers** — the highest-value target in the epic. Threats: **elevation of privilege** (granting oneself or another user access to an account); **tampering** (client-side grant forgery); **repudiation** (unattributed binding changes); **information disclosure** (view-as leaking another user's data without a record).
- Controls: server-side authority over every grant, step-up on save, replace-semantics with a full audit `before_state`/`after_state`, high-severity audit on impersonation start/end, fail-closed open-position check, and a Semgrep rule (E42-X03) asserting no admin mutation route is reachable without the audit decorator.
- Data classification: **Confidential** (account scope, risk limits) + **PII** (user identity). No secrets are rendered; 2FA reset never displays a secret.
- Mandatory `security` label per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 (touches RBAC and admin screens); Security-engineer review comment required.

## Accessibility notes
- Form sections use CMP-065 FormSection with a single `h1` per route (CMP-088 PageHeader contract).
- The grant table is a labelled table; permission level is a labelled radio/select per row, not an icon toggle.
- The unbind choice is `role="alertdialog"` with two clearly named buttons and no default destructive focus; Escape cancels the save rather than picking an option.
- Limit fields state their unit; the current measured value sits beside the limit as text.
- View-as banner is `role="status"` (persistent, not a one-shot alert) and its text — not colour — carries the impersonated username; the Exit control is the first tab stop on the page.

## Performance notes
- Detail page ≤700 ms p95 to interactive; the embedded audit trail loads lazily after first paint.
- Grant save round-trip ≤500 ms p95; the scope change must be observable by the affected user's next request (no client cache older than the last `grants_changed` push).
- Per US-ADMIN-003's NFR, limit evaluation on the order path stays ≤5 ms p95 — owned and benchmarked by E39; this story asserts it does not add client-side work to that path.

## Observability
- Audit: `roles.grant`, `roles.revoke`, `users.access_change`, `risk.limits_changed`, `auth.mfa_reset`, `auth.session_revoked` (R5 on #965), `admin.view_as_started`, `admin.view_as_ended` (last two `severity=high`).
- Metrics: `cv_admin_grant_change_total{result}`, `cv_admin_view_as_seconds`.
- Logs: every grant mutation logs the request id plus the grant-set hash before and after (not the raw set, which lives in the audit row).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched routes, keyboard-only pass, one manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E42-S02` — the list is the entry point and shares the mutation plumbing.
- `E42-D03` — hi-fi design for SCR-122/SCR-124.
- `E42-T04` — the lifecycle contract (slice S1) and the disable cascade semantics. Since the R2 split on #965 the routes this screen edits belong to E42-T08 (`GET|PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` and the `revoked` push) and E42-T09 (`GET /users/{userId}` with its ETag, `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` and admin sessions). Both sit in Sprint 19, after this Story's Sprint 18, so they are not in `blocked_by` (adding them fails SPRINT-ORDER). The re-point and re-sprint decision is item 4 of #2710, which also covers `GET /roles` and `GET /permissions`, still without an owning ticket (R9 on #965).
- `E28` — per-account profiles supply the profile context shown beside each grant.
- `E39` — risk caps, the limits API and the manager-facing lockout banner consumed by the tightening flow.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-user-detail` — 3 PRs: (1) detail layout + roles, (2) account bindings incl. unbind flow, (3) view-as.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-001..014)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 Admin (SCR-120..149), §11 global states (SCR-150..159)

- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md`, `ADR-0009-secrets-and-key-management.md`, `ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`

title: Build SCR-135 audit log browser and SCR-136 event detail with integrity state
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-008 — Append-only audit log (Must)** and **US-ADMIN-009 — Audit log search and export (Must)** are the accountability backbone of a self-hosted trading terminal. US-ADMIN-008's NFR is absolute: "append-only enforced at the database level (no UPDATE/DELETE grants); entries hash-chained; retained indefinitely." US-ADMIN-009's NFR sets the bar for usability: "search over 10 million entries returns the first page in ≤2 s", with manager scope enforced server-side and exports signed and themselves audited.

`docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-135 is uncompromising about the surface: "no edit or delete affordance exists anywhere — the log is append-only by design and this is stated on screen", and the integrity-failure state is "a security incident, not a UI error".

The database guarantees already exist (`21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1: `REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON audit_log`, the `audit_chain()` trigger, `audit_checkpoints`, the nightly `cv-audit-verify` job) and the writer ships with E09. This story builds the owner/viewer-facing browser over them; the query, verify and export API surface is E42-T02.

Note on role: `22-api-openapi.yaml` gives **viewers `audit:read` deliberately** — "a reviewer must be able to read the log without any write capability" — so this screen is reachable by viewer as well as owner, while US-ADMIN-009 scenario 2 requires a manager to see only their own actions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-135** at `/admin/audit`: CMP-049 Table of CMP-173 AuditRow with columns time, actor, role, action, target, environment, IP, severity, result; **CMP-174 AuditFilterBar** + CMP-047 DateRangePicker for actor, action class, subject type/id, outcome, severity, IP, date range and full-text `q`; cursor pagination at 200 rows per page; stable ordering by `id`.
- Row expansion to the **before/after diff**, rendered as a definition list with before/after labelled (a11y requirement), secrets shown as fingerprints only — never values.
- **SCR-136 Admin: audit event detail** drawer (CMP-046 Drawer): full field set (actor, role at the time, session, IP, user agent, action, target, before, after, `request_id`, environment, outcome), **correlated events** sharing the same `request_id`, links to the related order / rule version / account / user, and the raw record in a CMP-068 CopyableCodeBlock with CMP-033 CopyButton and the statement "this record cannot be edited or deleted".
- **Integrity indicator**: the page states the chain-verification status from `chain_verified` on the query response and from the on-demand `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify`; the **integrity-failure state** is a critical banner naming the position of the break ("Audit chain verification failed at <ts> — contact security") and is treated as an incident, with no retry-as-if-transient affordance.
- **Export** (CMP-099 PrintExportBar): `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export` over the current filter range, producing signed NDJSON via an async job polled through `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}`; the export itself emits `audit.exported`, and redaction is preserved in the exported payload.
- **Manager scoping** honoured and *displayed*: a manager sees only entries describing their own actions, with an explicit on-screen statement that the view is scoped — enforcement is server-side (E42-T02), the client never filters for security.
- Explicit absence of mutation: no edit, delete, or "correct this entry" control exists anywhere on either screen, and the append-only guarantee plus the retention statement are rendered as page text.
- States: loading · populated · filtered-to-nothing (SCR-151 pattern) · integrity verified · integrity failure · export in progress/failed · manager-scoped · retention notice.

## Out of scope
- The audit **writer**, the hash-chain trigger and the nightly verifier job (E09 + `21-database-schema.md`); off-box checkpoint handling is verified in E43-T10.
- Query/verify/export endpoints and their indexes (E42-T02).
- The security centre SCR-137 and its posture checks (E43).
- Journal/analytics exports (E41) — unrelated surface despite also using CMP-099.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Search the log
  Given 10 million audit entries exist
  When I filter by actor, action type, subject, severity and a time range
  Then matching entries are listed with cursor pagination and stable ordering
  And the first page returns within 2 seconds

Scenario: No mutation affordance exists
  When I inspect any row, the detail drawer and the page chrome
  Then no edit, delete or correct control is present anywhere
  And the page states that the log is append-only and that entries are retained indefinitely

Scenario: Integrity verification
  When I run the integrity check
  Then the hash chain over the selected range is verified
  And a break is reported with its position as a critical banner naming it a security incident, not a UI error

Scenario: Manager scope
  Given I am signed in as a manager
  When I open the audit log
  Then I see only entries describing my own actions, enforced server-side
  And the screen states that the view is scoped to my own actions

Scenario: Export is signed and audited
  When I export the filtered set
  Then a signed NDJSON file is produced through an async job with visible progress
  And payload redaction is preserved in the exported file
  And an audit.exported entry records the range and the requesting actor

Scenario (failure): Export job fails
  Given the export job returns status failed
  Then the failure is shown with its reason and a retry action
  And no partial file is offered for download

Scenario (edge): Secret-bearing entry
  Given an entry whose before/after state referenced key material
  Then the diff renders fingerprints only and never a secret value
```

## Technical notes / design
- Query: `GET /api/v1/admin/audit?cursor&limit&actor_user_id&action&subject_type&subject_id&outcome&severity&ip&from&to&q`; response carries `items`, `chain_verified` and `meta.next_cursor`. Offset paging is never used — ordering must stay stable while new rows append at the head.
- New rows arriving during browsing are **not** spliced into the current page; a "N new entries" affordance re-queries from the head, preserving pagination stability.
- Verify: `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify {from_id, to_id}` → `{verified, entries_checked, first_bad_id, checked_at}`. `first_bad_id` drives a deep link to that entry.
- Export: `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export {from, to, compress}` → `202 {job_id}`; poll `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}` until `succeeded`, then use `result.download_url`. Poll with backoff (1 s → 5 s), never a tight loop.
- Diff rendering: `before_state`/`after_state` are JSONB; the renderer walks keys, marks added/removed/changed, and applies a redaction allowlist so any key matching the secret patterns from `04-security-program.md` renders as a fingerprint.
- Table rows are memoised and windowed at 200 rows/page (the catalogue's stated page size) — the scripting budget for SCR-144-class tables is ≤8 ms per frame.
- Error codes: `forbidden` (no `audit:read`), `validation_failed` (bad range), `rate_limited` (export abuse guard).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: filter → query-param mapping incl. repeated `action` params; cursor advance/retreat; redaction of secret-shaped keys in the diff renderer (table-driven, ≥10 key patterns); integrity-failure banner copy and its non-retry semantics; export job polling with backoff and terminal states.
- **Contract**: `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}` against the OpenAPI document.
- **Integration**: manager-scoped response renders the scope statement; an unscoped fixture must not be renderable as if scoped (guard test).
- **E2E (Playwright)**: `admin-audit.spec.ts` — filter round-trip; row → detail drawer → correlated events by `request_id`; export to a completed job and a failed job; integrity-failure fixture rendering the critical banner.
- **Perf**: k6/Playwright-trace measurement of first-page latency against a 10 M-row seeded database (fixture generator in E42-Q03); filter round-trip ≤400 ms budget from the catalogue.
- **a11y**: axe on page and drawer; screen-reader pass on the diff definition list and the severity-as-text column.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/audit.page.json`, `audit.chain-broken.json`, `audit.manager-scoped.json`, `jobs.export.succeeded|failed.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **repudiation** (the log's whole purpose — any UI that appears to allow correction undermines it, hence zero mutation affordances); **information disclosure** (a diff leaking a secret or full PII — mitigated by fingerprint-only rendering and server-side redaction at write time); **tampering** (chain break surfaced loudly rather than swallowed); **elevation of privilege** (a manager reading others' entries — server-side scoping, asserted by an abuse-case test in E42-X03).
- Reading the audit log is itself audited (`audit.viewed`, `audit.record_viewed`, `audit.exported`) per SCR-136 — "so that reading the audit log is also on the record".
- Exported bundles carry a detached signature; the UI states that the file contains **Confidential** data and must be handled accordingly.
- Data classification: Confidential + PII (`actor_ip` is marked PII in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1).

## Accessibility notes
- Table semantics with a caption; **severity and outcome are text**, never colour alone; high-severity rows are additionally marked with a text label so they remain distinguishable in greyscale.
- Diffs render as definition lists with before/after explicitly labelled (catalogue a11y requirement); the raw record sits in a `<pre>` region with an accessible copy control.
- The integrity-failure banner is `role="alert"` announced once, then persists as static text.
- Date-range picker is fully keyboard operable with typed-date entry as an alternative to the calendar grid.
- Filtered-to-nothing state follows SCR-151: heading, cause sentence, one action (clear filters).

## Performance notes
