title: Build SCR-145 feature-flag console and SCR-148 maintenance mode
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-007 — Feature flags (Must)**: "As the owner, I want runtime feature flags, so that I can shed load or disable a risky feature without a deployment." The scenarios set three hard rules — a disabled feature disappears **for all users within 10 seconds** and the change is audited; flags controlling trading capability (live enablement, one-click, rule arming) require **step-up authentication**; and the current state of every flag, who changed it and when, is listed. The NFR closes the loophole: "flags are server-side with a client push; **no flag may weaken a security control**."

**SCR-148 Admin: maintenance mode** is listed under US-ADMIN-007 and US-ADMIN-011 and shares the same control plane: entering maintenance blocks new orders server-side within 200 ms, pauses algos, optionally keeps the recorder running, and broadcasts a notice to all sessions within 2 s — while stating explicitly that **native exchange stops remain active**.

The flag store, resolution order and kill-switch bypass already exist in the schema (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9: `feature_flags`, `feature_flag_overrides`, "Kill-switch flags (`is_killswitch`) bypass caching and are re-read every 5 s"), and the API surface is `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags` + `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`. The service behaviour is E42-T03; this story is the console.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-145** at `/admin/flags`: CMP-049 Table of **CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow** — key, human description of what the flag changes, kind (`boolean` / `percentage` / `variant`), resolved value, scope (global / per-user / per-role override), last changed by and when. Search across keys and descriptions. Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags`; writes via `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`.
- **Risky-flag grouping**: flags affecting order routing, risk enforcement or audit are grouped, visually marked and **step-up gated** on change (sign-off checklist requirement). `trading.live_enabled` renders as **disabled with the blocking reason** and a link to SCR-137 security centre — the enabling path itself belongs to E43/E44, not here.
- **Dependency acknowledgement**: turning off a flag an armed rule depends on lists the affected rules and requires acknowledgement before the write proceeds.
- **Per-flag change history** (a filtered audit query on `flags.change` for that key, reusing E42-S04's row renderer).
- "Requires reload" indicator on flags that cannot be applied live, with an explicit reload action rather than silent later application.
- **CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip** rendered on owner-visible surfaces gated by an unreleased flag, so QA can see which flag governs a screen.
- **SCR-148 maintenance mode**: page section plus `role="alertdialog"` entry modal with typed confirmation; the consequence list is rendered verbatim as a list — "New orders are blocked. Running algos are cancelled. Recording continues. Managers see a maintenance notice." — plus the explicit statement that native exchange stops remain active; a scheduled-window option with advance notice; and the manager/viewer-facing maintenance notice banner.
- Live propagation: flag and maintenance changes arrive at every client over the auto-subscribed WS `system` topic (`kind: feature_flags`), applied without a reload where possible.
- Audit: `flags.change` (step-up, high severity, with before/after), `maintenance.enabled`, `maintenance.disabled`.

## Out of scope
- Enabling `trading.live_enabled` and the evidence-bound live gate — **US-ADMIN-012 is owned by E44 (`E44-T04` evidence-bound write, `E44-S01` gate UI) with the enforcement/attestation half in `E43-S01`**. This console only renders the flag as blocked with the reason and a link to SCR-137; it contains no enable affordance, and `E42-Q06` asserts that as a test.
- The kill-switch itself (E39) — surfaced here as state, engaged from its own safety-critical surface.
- The flag-evaluation service, caching and `system` push implementation (E42-T03).
- Flag-debt hygiene CI warnings on `expires_at` (a chore in E48).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Toggle a flag
  Given the liquidation-heat estimate flag is on
  When I disable it and complete step-up
  Then the feature disappears for all connected users within 10 seconds via the system topic
  And the change is audited with before and after values and my actor id

Scenario: Safety flags require step-up
  Given a flag is classified as trading-capability affecting
  When I attempt to change it without a fresh admin token
  Then the re-auth gate appears and the write does not occur until elevation succeeds

Scenario: Flag state visibility
  Then every flag lists its current state, its human description, its scope, who changed it last and when
  And each flag exposes its own change history

Scenario: Live enablement stays blocked here
  Given the pen-test sign-off is outstanding
  Then trading.live_enabled renders disabled with the blocking reason and a link to the security centre
  And the API rejects a direct write with validation_failed / gate_evidence_required

Scenario: Maintenance mode consequences are explicit
  When I open the maintenance-mode entry dialog
  Then it is role="alertdialog" listing exactly: new orders blocked, running algos cancelled, recording continues, managers see a maintenance notice
  And it states that native exchange stops remain active
  And entry requires a typed confirmation and step-up

Scenario (failure): Flag write rejected mid-flight
  Given the server rejects the flag write with 422
  Then the toggle reverts to its server value with an inline error naming the reason
  And no optimistic state is left applied

Scenario (edge): Armed rule depends on the flag
  Given two armed rules depend on the flag being disabled
  Then the affected rules are listed and I must acknowledge before the write proceeds
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolution order is server-side and authoritative (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9): user override → role override → percentage rollout (hash of `user_id||flag_key`) → default. The console **displays** the resolved value plus the override chain; it never recomputes resolution locally for enforcement.
- `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` body: `SetFeatureFlagRequest` (`value`, `overrides`, `reason`, optional `evidence_url`). `trading.live_enabled` is special-cased server-side and fails with `validation_failed` / `gate_evidence_required` without evidence — the UI surfaces that verbatim rather than pre-validating.
- Optimistic UI is **not** used for risky flags; the toggle shows a pending state until the server confirms, because a wrongly-rendered safety flag is worse than a slow one.
- Live application: subscribe to the already-open `system` topic and apply `kind: feature_flags` payloads to the client flag store; flags marked `requires_reload` set a banner instead of mutating live state.
- Maintenance mode is itself a kill-switch-class flag (`is_killswitch = true`), so it bypasses caching and is re-read every 5 s server-side.
- Error codes: `validation_failed`, `gate_evidence_required`, `stepup_required`, `forbidden`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: override-chain rendering for boolean/percentage/variant kinds; risky-flag classification driving step-up; pending (non-optimistic) toggle state; rollback on 422; `requires_reload` banner; dependency-acknowledgement list construction.
- **Contract**: `/admin/feature-flags` GET/PUT against the OpenAPI schema incl. the `flagKey` pattern.
- **Integration**: a `system` frame with `kind: feature_flags` updates the console and the rest of the app's flag store consistently.
- **E2E**: `admin-flags.spec.ts` — two browser contexts; owner disables a flag and the second (manager) context loses the feature within 10 s; `trading.live_enabled` blocked-state assertion; maintenance entry/exit with the manager context seeing the notice within 2 s and order entry refusing.
- **a11y**: axe; toggles labelled with the flag name (not "on/off"); alertdialog behaviour for maintenance entry.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/flags.json`, `flags.live-blocked.json`, `system.flags-push.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **elevation of privilege via flags** — the NFR "no flag may weaken a security control" is enforced by a server-side allowlist of what a flag may gate (E42-T03) and asserted by a test here that no flag key in the catalogue maps to an auth/RBAC/audit control; **tampering** (client-side flag forcing — the client store is display-only for gating non-security UI, all enforcement is server-side); **repudiation** (every change audited at high severity with before/after and a required `reason`).
- Maintenance mode is a **safety** control: it must fail closed — if the write fails, the UI must never show the system as being in maintenance.
- `trading.live_enabled` is the R4 gate; this console must not provide any path to enable it. Reviewed explicitly in E42-X02.
- Data classification: Confidential operational configuration; no PII, no secrets.

## Accessibility notes
- Each toggle's accessible name is the **flag key plus its human description**, never a bare "on/off" (catalogue a11y requirement).
- Risky flags are grouped under a heading with a text label ("Trading-capability flags — changes require re-authentication"), not merely a colour band.
- Maintenance entry dialog is `role="alertdialog"`; the consequence list is a real `<ul>` so it is read in full; the typed-confirm field is labelled and its expected value stated in text.
- Blocked flags are disabled **with a reason** exposed via `aria-describedby` (RBAC/blocked-control convention from `14-screens-catalogue.md` §0).
- Flag state changes arriving over WS are announced politely once, not per-flag in a burst.

## Performance notes
- Flag change propagates to all sessions within 2 s over `system` (catalogue) and the feature is gone for all users within 10 s (US-ADMIN-007).
- Maintenance mode blocks order acceptance server-side within 200 ms and broadcasts within 2 s (SCR-148).
- The console makes no polling requests; it renders from one GET plus the existing `system` subscription.

## Observability
- Audit: `flags.change {key, before, after, reason}` (high severity, step-up), `maintenance.enabled {window, message}`, `maintenance.disabled`.
- Metrics: `cv_feature_flag_changes_total{key,result}`, `cv_flag_push_latency_ms`, `cv_maintenance_mode` gauge.
- Logs: flag writes log actor, key, before/after hash and `request_id`; maintenance transitions log the consequence set actually applied (orders blocked, algos cancelled, recorder state).

title: Build SCR-143 system health, SCR-144 incident log and SCR-146 backups/restore
body:
## Context
**US-ADMIN-011 — System health screen (Must)**: "As the owner, I want live system health, so that I can diagnose problems quickly" — WS connection states, ingest rates and lag, rate-limit budget per account, queue depths, database sizes and latency, error rates and process uptime; drill-down to recent errors and reconnects; and a degraded state that "is escalated with a text label, the affected features are named, and a remediation hint is given". The NFR bounds the cost: "health data is served from the metrics pipeline, with the screen adding ≤1 % load."

The traceability matrix maps US-ADMIN-011 to **SCR-120, SCR-143, SCR-146 and SCR-148**; SCR-120 is E42-S01 and SCR-148 is E42-S05, leaving **SCR-143 Admin: system health** and **SCR-146 Admin: backups & restore** here. **SCR-144 Admin: incident / connectivity log** is the drill-down target SCR-143's sign-off checklist requires ("link to the incident log") and is built with it. **SCR-147 exchange connectivity & rate limits** is designed and owned elsewhere (E04/E46); this story only links to it and renders its summary tile.

The metrics pipeline, health probes and the aggregated health endpoint come from **E04 Observability baseline** (`E04-T04` implements health/readiness/aggregate). This story is the admin surface over them plus the backup/restore operator flow.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **SCR-143** at `/admin/health`: per-subsystem rows (API, WS, Bybit public/private/REST plus per-UID rate-limit budget, Ingest, Engine, Recorder, DB tiers, Client FPS) as **CMP-178 SystemHealthTile** with CMP-024 Sparkline and a table alternative for every sparkline; CMP-076 ConnectionStatus; CMP-092 DegradedModeBanner; CMP-210 HealthChips in the shell. Data: `GET /api/v1/admin/health` for the snapshot plus live patches from the WS `system` topic (`kind: health | exchange_state | connection_quality`).
- Drill-down: selecting a subsystem opens its recent errors, recent reconnects and last-hour metrics.
- **Degraded/outage states** per the catalogue: each tile states what stops working and gives a remediation hint; the outage variant states what is still safe — "Native stops on the exchange are unaffected".
- The page must **remain usable while the system it reports on is degraded**: every tile resolves independently, no tile can block another, and a failed probe renders that tile's error state only.
- **SCR-144 incident / connectivity log**: cursor-paginated table (time, subsystem, severity, message, duration, resolution) over `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents`, with filters by subsystem, severity and date, open vs resolved states, an **acknowledge** action (audited) and export; long messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently. Live incidents append over `system`.
- **SCR-146** at `/admin/backups`: schedule and retention summary; per-run table (when, target, size, status, verified) from `GET /api/v1/admin/backups`; **Back up now** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups`), **Verify** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/verify`), **Download** and the **Restore wizard** (`POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/restore`) as a CMP-023-progressed stepper: choose backup → impact preview → typed confirm + step-up → progress → verification → summary.
- Restore guardrails from the catalogue: restore is blocked while any position is open unless the owner explicitly acknowledges ("You have 2 open positions. A restore does not change anything on Bybit. Continue?"); the impact preview states that trading is halted during restore, that exchange state is untouched, and that **market history is not restored from these backups**; downloading a backup containing encrypted secrets warns about handling; last-successful-backup age warning; failed-backup and failed-verification states.
- "Export diagnostics" action on SCR-143 wired to E04's secret-scanned support bundle (`E04-S02`), emitting the audited `health.diagnostics_exported`.
- Audit: `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restore` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high), `backup.deleted`, `incident.acknowledged`, `health.diagnostics_exported`.

## Out of scope
- The metrics pipeline, probes, Grafana dashboards and alert rules (E04).
- SCR-147 exchange connectivity & rate limits as a full screen (E04/E46) and SCR-142 storage & database panel (E16/E07) — both linked to, not built here.
- The backup engine, scheduler and restore executor (E45 resilience / ops) — this story consumes the admin API surface listed in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.
- Chaos scenarios proving degraded rendering (E42-Q03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Health overview
  When I open /admin/health
  Then WS connection states, ingest rates and lag, rate-limit budget per account, queue depths, database sizes and latency, error rates and process uptime are shown
  And each tile shows a number with units plus a state word, never colour alone

Scenario: Drill down
  When I select the recorder subsystem
  Then recent errors, recent reconnects and relevant metrics over the last hour are shown

Scenario: Degraded state names the impact
  Given the private WS for sub_002 is down
  Then that tile escalates with a text label, names the affected features, and gives a remediation hint
  And the page states that native exchange stops are unaffected

Scenario: The page survives the outage it reports
  Given GET /api/v1/admin/health times out and the system topic is the only live source
  Then the shell and navigation remain usable
  And each tile renders its own last-known value marked stale rather than an empty page

Scenario: Restore is gated
  Given I have 2 open positions
  When I start the restore wizard
  Then I must acknowledge that a restore does not change anything on Bybit before continuing
  And the impact preview states that trading is halted during restore and that market history is not restored
  And completion requires a typed confirmation and step-up
  And backup.restore is audited at high severity

Scenario (failure): Backup verification fails
  Given the most recent backup fails verification
  Then its row shows the failed-verification state with the reason
  And a warning states how old the last successfully verified backup is

Scenario (edge): No backups yet
  Then the empty state explains that no backup has run, names the schedule, and offers "Back up now"
```

## Technical notes / design
- Snapshot + delta: one `GET /admin/health` on mount, then patches from the auto-subscribed `system` topic at its 1 000 ms throttle (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2). No independent polling timer is created — that is what keeps the screen inside the ≤1 % load NFR.
- `SystemUpdate.components[]` (`23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9) maps 1:1 onto tiles by `name`; unknown component names render generically rather than being dropped, so a backend addition is visible before the frontend knows about it.
- Each tile is an independent subscriber with its own `status` and `lastGoodAt`; a tile older than 3× its expected cadence renders `stale` with the timestamp.
- Restore is a long-running server job with staged progress (`GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`), requires maintenance mode (SCR-148, E42-S05) and is therefore mutually exclusive with an active trading session — the wizard states this rather than discovering it at step 4.
- Downloads are served through a short-lived signed URL from the job result; the URL is never logged and never placed in analytics.
- Sparklines always ship with a table alternative behind a disclosure (a11y requirement), rendered from the same series.
- Error codes: `forbidden`, `conflict` (restore while maintenance is off), `rate_limited`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: tile state machine (`loading → ok → stale → error`) and per-tile isolation; unknown-component fallback; restore wizard step guards (open positions, maintenance mode, typed confirm); last-successful-backup age computation; sparkline↔table equivalence.
- **Contract**: `/admin/health`, `/admin/incidents`, `/admin/backups`, `/admin/backups/{id}/verify|restore`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}`.
- **Integration**: a `system` frame with a degraded component escalates only its own tile.
- **E2E**: `admin-health.spec.ts` (health render, drill-down, degraded fixture, diagnostics export) and `admin-backups.spec.ts` (backup now → verify → restore wizard happy path and the open-positions guard).
- **Chaos (with E42-Q03)**: kill the health endpoint and the WS mid-session — the page must degrade to stale values, not blank.
- **Perf**: measure the screen's added load against the ≤1 % NFR and the ≤2 ms scripting-per-frame budget with 12 tiles updating at 1 Hz.
- **a11y**: axe; keyboard traversal of tiles and the wizard stepper; screen-reader pass on progress percentages.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/health.ok.json`, `health.degraded.json`, `incidents.page.json`, `backups.list.json`, `backups.verify-failed.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **information disclosure** — a health screen is a reconnaissance surface; internal hostnames, connection strings and stack traces must never be rendered (the support bundle is secret-scanned by E04-S02, and this screen renders only the fields in the `HealthReport` schema). **Tampering/destruction** — restore is the single most destructive action in the product: typed confirm, step-up, maintenance-mode precondition, high-severity audit, and an impact preview that is accurate rather than reassuring. **Information disclosure via download** — a backup contains encrypted secrets; the download warns about handling, is step-up gated and audited at high severity.
- Data classification: operational **Confidential**; backup artefacts are **Secret-bearing** (envelope-encrypted) and are never decrypted client-side.
- `security` review requested on the restore copy specifically (SCR-146 sign-off: "restore impact copy reviewed by security") — tracked in E42-X02.

## Accessibility notes
- Each subsystem is a labelled row with a **text status**; no reliance on dot colour (catalogue a11y requirement).
- Every sparkline has an equivalent data table reachable by keyboard.
- The restore wizard is a stepper with `aria-current="step"`, and progress exposes text percentages, not just a bar.
- Incident messages expand into a detail row rather than truncating silently, so a screen reader can reach the full text.
- Degraded banners are `role="status"`; a new outage is announced once via `role="alert"` and then persists as static text.
- All figures carry units in their accessible names.

## Performance notes
- US-ADMIN-011 NFR: the screen adds ≤1 % load — enforced by consuming the existing `system` subscription and one snapshot GET, with no per-tile polling.
- SCR-143 budget: under 2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144: 10k rows scroll without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame.
- Storage figures are sampled server-side every 60 s, never computed on request (SCR-142 convention, inherited by the linked tile).
- Restore/verify are server jobs; the browser never performs the work.

## Observability
- Audit: `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restore` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high), `backup.deleted`, `incident.acknowledged`, `health.diagnostics_exported`.
- Analytics: `admin.health_viewed`, `incident.log_viewed`, `incident.exported`.
- Metrics consumed (from E04): `cv_ws_clients`, `cv_ingest_lag_ms`, `cv_rate_budget_free_pct`, `cv_db_size_bytes`, `cv_api_request_duration_seconds`. Added here: `cv_admin_health_render_ms`, `cv_backup_restore_total{result}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.
- [ ] Storybook stories for every new/changed component variant, including loading, empty, error and degraded states.
- [ ] `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` / `15-component-catalogue.md` updated if the shipped behaviour diverged from the spec.
- [ ] a11y: axe-core CI green on the touched routes, keyboard-only pass, one manual screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) recorded.
- [ ] design-qa: built screen compared against the signed-off Figma spec by a designer; discrepancies fixed or filed as `priority/*` bugs.
- [ ] security: RBAC deny-by-default verified server-side (non-owner receives 404 from the router and 403 from the API); every state-changing control wrapped in CMP-093 AuditActionTrigger and asserted to emit its audit entry.
- [ ] QA sign-off comment posted with pass/fail per scenario.
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review against staging (demo).
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded for the surface.
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E42-S01` — admin shell.
- `E42-D05` — hi-fi design for SCR-143/SCR-144/SCR-146 (building on E04-D01's system-health design language).
- `E42-T05` — the admin read-model endpoints for overview/health/incidents/backups wiring.
- `E04` — metrics pipeline, probes, aggregated health endpoint and the diagnostics support bundle.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-health` — 3 PRs: (1) SCR-143 tiles + drill-down, (2) SCR-144 incident log, (3) SCR-146 backups + restore wizard.

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 ADMIN (US-ADMIN-001..014)
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 Admin (SCR-120..149), §11 global states (SCR-150..159)
- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` CMP-087, CMP-093, CMP-095, CMP-099, CMP-173..179, CMP-210
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 ADMIN
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (`/users`, `/roles`, `/permissions`, `/admin/*`, `/me/sessions`)
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2 private topics, §15.9 `SystemUpdate`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 identity/RBAC/sessions, §3.9 settings & feature flags, §3.10 audit log
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` C14 Auth/RBAC/Audit, C15 Admin, §3.10, §3.11
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md`, `ADR-0009-secrets-and-key-management.md`, `ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register (E42, R3, S16–S17), §7 R3, §11 dependency graph

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**
1. AGENTS.md §0 (read-order) and §3 (how to pick up a ticket)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`
3. `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`

- `tests/e2e/` (Playwright) or `services/api/tests/` (pytest) as appropriate to this ticket's layer

**Interfaces you must not break**

**Commands**
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web lint`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web typecheck`
- `pnpm --filter @candleviewer/web test`
- `pnpm test:a11y`

**Branch & PR**

- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-number-for-E42-S06>`

**Done means**

- `E42-D05` — hi-fi design for SCR-143/SCR-144/SCR-146 (building on E04-D01's system-health design language).

- `E04` — metrics pipeline, probes, aggregated health endpoint and the diagnostics support bundle.); move ticket Status → Blocked; never silently work around a failing gate or a missing dependency ticket.

## Agent-delivery adaptations (owner decision 2026-09-25)
Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:
- **Architect / CDO / Security-engineer sign-off or countersignature** → the **owner's** `approved` comment on this issue, or owner merge of the PR. No other human role exists. Do not block on a missing countersignature — proceed and record "owner approval pending" in the PR.
- **Design tooling**: *Figma* → **Penpot** (`docs/design/README.md`); frames on a page named after this ticket; exports via `docs/design/_tools/penpot_export.py`. Bind only to semantic tokens in `packages/ui/tokens/`.
- **Moderated usability / participant sessions** → a documented **heuristic evaluation** (Nielsen + the trading-specific heuristics in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`), a written session protocol ready for the owner to run later, and an **owner walkthrough** checklist posted on the issue. Never fabricate participants, timings or quotes; label all findings `(heuristic)`.
- **CVD / contrast validation** → computed programmatically (WCAG contrast matrix over the token JSON; CVD simulation via a documented script), attached as artefacts.
- **Spikes**: findings go to `docs/plan/spikes/<KEY>.md` via a normal PR (branch `spike/<epic>-<slug>`); any ADR named by the spike uses the **next free number** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` (ADR-0001…0016 are taken).
- **Dependencies**: `blocked_by` now lists the concrete prerequisite tickets (not whole epics). Start when those are **merged** (In Test or Done).
- Anything that genuinely needs a human that is not the owner (external pen-test vendor, legal) stays as-is and is flagged `needs-owner` on the issue.

title: Build the manager onboarding wizard and trade-group/recorder governance
body:
## Context
Three Should/Must administration stories remain, and each is a thin governance layer over machinery another epic already owns — so they are deliberately grouped into one small story rather than three thin ones.

**US-ADMIN-013 — Manager onboarding workflow (Should)**: a guided flow through sub-account creation, the **48-hour key restriction**, key creation with 2FA, permission scoping, IP whitelisting, profile creation, limits and the invite; a blocked step must show the exact unlock time while the rest of the flow continues; leaving and returning resumes where you left off with completed steps marked. NFR: "the flow never stores a secret outside the encrypted store, and never displays one after entry." Screens: **SCR-017** (invited-user side) and **SCR-123** (invite), orchestrated here.

**US-ADMIN-005 — Trade-group administration (Must)**: central governance of fan-out targets on **SCR-062** — create, rename, reorder, enable, disable, and **set which users may use each group**; a disabled group disappears from ticket targets while existing positions opened through it remain fully manageable; a membership change during an open group trade keeps the **original membership snapshot**, shown in the trade detail. NFR: "group definitions are versioned so historical trades reference the version used." E28 builds SCR-062's definition surface; this story adds the admin governance controls (who may use it, enable/disable, version visibility).

**US-ADMIN-006 — Recorder & retention administration (Must)**: the requirement that recorder and retention settings live "in the admin section … so that data policy is managed in one place". E16 builds SCR-140/SCR-141 in full; this story mounts them inside the admin shell, guarantees the admin-area audit and step-up wrapping applies to their destructive paths, and links them from SCR-120.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Onboarding wizard** (`/admin/users/onboard`): a resumable stepper over the existing endpoints — create sub-account (E27) → 48-hour key restriction check → create key with 2FA (E27) → permission scoping (`PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`) → IP whitelisting (E27) → profile creation (E28) → limits (E39) → invite (`POST /api/v1/users`, SCR-123). Components: CMP-001, CMP-009, CMP-027, CMP-033, CMP-040, CMP-043, CMP-050, CMP-066, CMP-097, CMP-105.
- **Blocked-step behaviour**: when Bybit's 48-hour new-sub-account key restriction is active, the key step renders blocked with the **exact unlock timestamp** and the remaining steps stay available — the flow is not halted.
- **Resume**: wizard progress is persisted server-side against the in-progress user record (not in localStorage, so it survives a device change); returning shows completed steps marked and lands on the first incomplete step.
- **Trade-group governance on SCR-062**: enable/disable a group; rename and reorder; **who may use this group** (per-user allowlist); the version indicator with a link from a historical trade to the group version it used; and the disable confirmation stating that existing positions opened through the group remain fully manageable. Components CMP-041, CMP-049, CMP-055, CMP-105, CMP-123, CMP-124.
- **Recorder/retention admin integration**: SCR-140 and SCR-141 mounted at `/admin/recorder` inside CMP-087 AdminLayout; their destructive paths (purge, retention reduction) inherit the admin re-auth gate and CMP-093 audit wrapping; SCR-120's recorder and storage tiles link here; the dangerous-change preview and typed confirmation required by US-ADMIN-006 are verified to be present (implemented by E16-S03).
- Audit: `user.onboarding_started|resumed|completed`, `trade_group.enabled|disabled|renamed|reordered`, `trade_group.membership_changed`, and (verified, not re-implemented) `retention.change`, `retention.purge`.

## Out of scope
- Sub-account and API-key creation, the 48-hour restriction detection and IP whitelisting (E27).
- Per-account profile creation and the trade-group definition surface (E28).
- Risk limits (E39).
- The recorder engine, retention manager, disk budget and SCR-140/141/142 implementations (E16) — mounted, not rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Guided steps
  When I start the manager onboarding flow
  Then it walks through sub-account creation, the 48-hour key restriction, key creation with 2FA, permission scoping, IP whitelisting, profile creation, limits and the invite
  And each completed step is marked

Scenario: Blocked step does not halt the flow
  Given the 48-hour key restriction is active for the new sub-account
  Then the key step is blocked showing the exact unlock time
  And the remaining steps continue to be available

Scenario: Resume
  Given I left the flow after the profile step
  When I return, on a different device
  Then the flow resumes at the first incomplete step with earlier steps marked complete

Scenario: Disable a trade group
  Given group G is enabled and has an open group trade
  When I disable G
  Then G disappears from ticket targets
  And the existing positions opened through G remain fully manageable

Scenario: Membership change during an open trade
  Given a group trade opened through G is still open
  When I change G's membership
  Then the open trade keeps its original membership snapshot
  And the trade detail shows which group version it used

Scenario (failure): Secret never re-displayed
  Given I entered an API secret at the key step
  When I navigate back to that step
  Then the secret is not displayed, only its fingerprint and status
  And no secret value was written outside the encrypted store

Scenario (edge): Recorder purge from the admin area
  Given I open /admin/recorder with a stale admin token
  Then the re-auth gate appears before any destructive control is reachable
  And a purge shows the impact preview and requires a typed confirmation
```

## Technical notes / design
- Wizard state is a server-side record keyed by the pending user id with `steps[] {key, status, completedAt, blockedUntil}`; the client renders from it and never infers completion locally. Resume is therefore device-independent (NFR: nothing sensitive is cached client-side).
- The 48-hour restriction is reported by E27's account read model (`restricted_until`); the wizard renders that timestamp verbatim in the viewer's locale with the UTC value in the accessible name.
- Secret handling: the key secret is posted straight to E27's import endpoint and cleared from memory on step completion; the field is `autocomplete="off"`, never rendered back, and excluded from any analytics or error payload (a test asserts the redaction).
- Trade-group governance writes go through E28's group endpoints with the group **version** bumped on membership change; open group trades reference the version they were created with, so the UI reads the snapshot from the trade, not from the live group.
- Recorder mounting is routing plus layout only — no duplicate data layer. The admin guard wraps the route; E16's components are reused unchanged.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: step-state machine incl. blocked-but-not-halting; resume targeting the first incomplete step; secret-field redaction in error/analytics payloads; group disable → removal from ticket targets while open positions persist; version-snapshot rendering.
- **Contract**: the wizard's composed calls validated against the OpenAPI document for each underlying endpoint.
- **Integration**: recorder route mounted under the admin guard — a stale token blocks destructive controls.
- **E2E**: `admin-onboarding.spec.ts` — full flow with the 48-hour restriction fixture, abandon-and-resume in a fresh context, ending with a redeemable invite; `admin-trade-groups.spec.ts` — disable with an open group trade.
- **a11y**: axe on the wizard and SCR-062 governance controls; keyboard-only completion of the whole wizard; screen-reader pass on the stepper.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/admin/onboarding.partial.json`, `account.key-restricted.json`, `trade-groups.with-open-trade.json`.
- Coverage ≥80%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **key leakage** — the NFR is explicit that no secret is stored outside the encrypted store or displayed after entry; controls are direct-to-vault submission, memory clearing, redaction in logs/analytics and a regression test. **Elevation of privilege** — the wizard grants account access and limits in one flow, so every step is step-up gated and audited individually, not once at the end. **Tampering** — group membership snapshots are server-side and immutable for open trades.
- Data classification: **Secret** (API key material, handled but never rendered), **PII** (invitee email), **Confidential** (scope and limits).
- Mandatory `security` label (touches API-key handling and RBAC grants); Security-engineer review comment required.

## Accessibility notes
- The wizard is a labelled stepper with `aria-current="step"`; each step announces its status; a blocked step states *why* and *until when* in text.
- Progress is never only a graphic — completed/blocked/current are words.
- The secret field has a visible label, a format hint, and an explicit statement that it will not be shown again.
- Group governance controls are named with their scope ("Disable trade group G — removes it from ticket targets"), never icon-only.
- Reorder is operable by keyboard (move-up/move-down buttons), not drag-only.

## Performance notes
- Each wizard step's round-trip ≤500 ms p95; step transitions never re-fetch the whole flow, only the changed step.
- Mounting SCR-140/141 adds no additional data fetching beyond E16's existing hooks — asserted by a network-call count test.
- The group list is small by construction (a handful of groups); no virtualisation, with the reason recorded in a comment.

## Observability
- Audit: `user.onboarding_started|resumed|completed`, `trade_group.enabled|disabled|renamed|reordered`, `trade_group.membership_changed` (with the version before/after); verified pass-through of `recorder.*` and `retention.*` from E16.
- Analytics: `admin.onboarding_step_completed {step, durationMs}`, `admin.onboarding_abandoned {step}` — used to find steps that block owners.
- Metrics: `cv_admin_onboarding_completions_total`, `cv_trade_group_state_changes_total{action}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All Gherkin acceptance criteria covered by automated tests (unit/integration/Playwright E2E) or an executed manual QA step with a follow-up automation Task.
- [ ] Frontend coverage ≥80% on new/changed lines; CI coverage gate green.

title: Implement GET /admin/overview and /admin/capacity read models
body:
## Context
SCR-120 Admin home is specified to aggregate "in one call plus `system` for live tiles" and to "render in <=800 ms and never block on the slowest subsystem" (`14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-120 performance note). That requires a **read model** in module M21 (Admin, `20-architecture.md` C15) that fans out to each subsystem with per-source timeouts and returns partial results rather than failing whole.

`GET /api/v1/admin/capacity` is the companion the users list and accounts list need: it "projects disk exhaustion from the current recorded-symbol set and retention policy (~0.5-0.75 GB/day/symbol at 200-depth) and reports per-UID rate-budget utilisation, so the owner can see a limit approaching instead of discovering it at a rejection" — and it carries the sub-account tier used by US-ADMIN-014, which "is an explicit recorded fact, never inferred".

Both endpoints are already declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`AdminOverview`, `CapacityReport`); this task implements them interface-first.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implement `GET /api/v1/admin/overview` → `AdminOverview`: counts and headline state across users, accounts, keys nearing expiry, recorder health, storage headroom and open incidents. RBAC `admin:read`, scope none.
- Implement `GET /api/v1/admin/capacity` → `CapacityReport`: disk projection from `recorded_symbols` × `retention_policies` at the measured GB/day rate, per-UID rate-budget utilisation, and the **recorded** sub-account tier (`regular` = 5, `business_kyc` = 20) read from `settings` (scope `system`, key `accounts.subaccount_tier`) — never inferred from the observed account count.
- **Partial-result semantics**: each contributing source has its own ≤300 ms budget; a source that times out or errors yields `{status: "error", detail}` for its slice while the response still returns `200`. The response is never all-or-nothing.
- Short-TTL cache (5 s) per slice so a rapid reload does not re-fan-out; kill-switch and flag state are excluded from the cache (they are read live, matching the 5 s re-read rule for `is_killswitch` flags).
- Emit `admin.area_entered` audit rows from the admin router dependency (shared by every `/admin/*` route), carrying `{route, reauth_token_age_s}`.
- Prometheus metrics for the fan-out (per-source latency and error counters).

## Out of scope
- The health aggregation itself (`GET /admin/health`) — E04-T04; this read model consumes its summary.
- The frontend overview screen (E42-S01).
- Audit query/verify/export endpoints (E42-T02).
- Recorder/storage measurement (E16) — consumed via its existing service interface.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Overview returns within budget
  Given every subsystem is healthy
  When GET /api/v1/admin/overview is called
  Then it responds 200 within 300 ms p95 with every slice populated

Scenario: A slow subsystem does not block the response
  Given the recorder service does not respond within its 300 ms budget
  When GET /api/v1/admin/overview is called
  Then the response is still 200 within 500 ms
  And the recorder slice carries status "error" with a detail string
  And every other slice is populated

Scenario: Capacity reports the recorded tier
  Given settings key accounts.subaccount_tier is "regular"
  Then CapacityReport states a sub-account cap of 5 and names the tier as a recorded fact
  And changing the recorded tier to business_kyc reports a cap of 20 and is audited

Scenario (failure): Non-owner access
  Given a manager token without admin:read
  Then both endpoints return 403 and an audit entry is written

Scenario (edge): No recorded symbols
  Then the disk projection reports zero growth with an explicit "nothing is recorded" marker rather than a null
```

## Technical notes / design
- Module M21 (Admin) service `AdminOverviewService` fans out with `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` under a per-source `asyncio.timeout(0.3)`; exceptions are mapped to a slice-level error object, logged with the source name and `request_id`, and never propagated.
- Disk projection: `projected_bytes = Σ_symbol(measured_gb_per_day × effective_retention_days)`, with `measured_gb_per_day` taken from E16's `DiskBudget` (measured, not assumed) and falling back to the documented 0.5–0.75 GB/day/symbol band with an explicit `estimated: true` marker when no measurement exists yet.
- Rate-budget utilisation is read from the backend's own accounting (server-side counters + exchange response headers), consistent with SCR-147 — the API never queries Bybit to answer this call.
- Caching via an in-process TTL cache keyed by slice; cache entries carry `generated_at` so the client can render freshness.
- Audit dependency: a FastAPI router dependency on the `/admin` router writes `admin.area_entered`; it must be impossible to add an admin route without it (enforced by the Semgrep rule in E42-X03).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: fan-out with each source failing in turn (N cases) asserting 200 + partial; timeout mapping; projection maths incl. the estimated-fallback branch; tier resolution from settings; cache TTL and `generated_at`.
- **Contract**: response validated against `AdminOverview` / `CapacityReport` schemas from `22-api-openapi.yaml`; schemathesis run over both paths.
- **Integration**: against a seeded Postgres + stubbed recorder/health services.
- **Perf**: p95 ≤300 ms healthy, ≤500 ms with one timing-out source, measured in CI with a benchmark test.
- **Security**: RBAC matrix test (owner 200, manager 403 + audit, viewer 403, unauthenticated 401).
- Coverage ≥85% on `services/admin/overview`.

## Security notes
- Threats: **information disclosure** — the overview aggregates across every subsystem, so the response must contain no secrets, no connection strings and no key material (schema-enforced; a test asserts the serialised response matches no secret pattern). **Elevation of privilege** — `admin:read` required, deny-by-default, 403 + audit on denial.
- Data classification: Confidential operational data; the tier setting change is audited (`settings.change`).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
- p95 ≤300 ms healthy / ≤500 ms degraded (derived from SCR-120's ≤800 ms end-to-end render budget, leaving the client its share).
- Per-source budget 300 ms; total fan-out is concurrent, not sequential.
- 5 s per-slice cache bounds load under repeated reloads; the screen itself adds no polling.

## Observability
- Metrics: `cv_admin_overview_source_duration_seconds{source}`, `cv_admin_overview_source_errors_total{source}`, `cv_admin_capacity_projection_bytes`.
- Audit: `admin.area_entered {route, reauth_token_age_s}`, `settings.change` for the tier.
- Logs: one structured line per degraded slice with `source`, `reason`, `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] OpenAPI (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) / WS (`23-ws-protocol.md`) / internal schema (`24-internal-schemas.md`) deltas merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green.

- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Observability: metrics/log fields/audit actions listed below exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies

- `E04` — metrics registry and the aggregated health summary this read model consumes.

title: Implement audit query, hash-chain verify and signed export endpoints
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-009 requires search over **10 million entries** returning the first page in ≤2 s, manager scoping enforced server-side, and a **signed** export that is itself audited with redaction preserved. US-ADMIN-008 requires an integrity check that "verifies the hash chain over entries and reports any break with its position".

The table, the chain trigger, the append-only grants and the checkpoint table already exist in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1, and the writer ships with E09. What is missing — and what this task delivers — is the **read side**: `GET /admin/audit`, `POST /admin/audit/verify`, `POST /admin/audit/export` and the job plumbing behind `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}`, all declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml`.

The indexes matter more than the handlers: `ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object` and the partial `ix_audit_sev` exist, but the filter combinations the UI offers must be proven against a 10 M-row dataset rather than assumed.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/audit` with cursor pagination (keyset on `id`, never OFFSET), filters `actor_user_id`, `action[]`, `subject_type`, `subject_id`, `outcome`, `severity`, `ip`, `from`, `to`, full-text `q` over the detail payload; returns `items`, `chain_verified` for the returned slice, and `meta.next_cursor`. Permission `audit:read`.
- **Manager scoping**: when the caller is not owner/viewer-with-`audit:read`-global, the query is narrowed server-side to `actor_user_id = caller` — implemented in the repository layer so no handler can forget it, and asserted by a test that calls the repository directly.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/verify {from_id, to_id}` → `{verified, entries_checked, first_bad_id, checked_at}`; recomputes the chain in batches with a bounded memory footprint and reports the **first** divergence.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/audit/export {from, to, compress}` → `202 {job_id}`: an async job writing NDJSON plus a **detached Ed25519 signature** over the file digest (signing key held outside the database, per `audit_checkpoints.signed_by` convention); redaction applied at write time is preserved — the exporter never re-hydrates redacted fields.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}` job status for export (and reused by recorder/backup jobs).
- Full-text search support: a GIN index on the detail payload sufficient for the `q` filter, added by an Alembic migration with a documented build cost.
- Export rate limiting and a maximum range, so export cannot be used as a data-exfiltration or DoS primitive.
- Audit of the read side itself: `audit.viewed`, `audit.exported`.

## Out of scope
- The audit **writer**, the `audit_chain()` trigger, append-only grants and the nightly `cv-audit-verify` job (E09 + schema).
- Off-box checkpoint storage verification (E43-T10).
- The browser UI (E42-S04).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: First page over 10 million entries
  Given the audit_log table holds 10 million rows
  When the first page is requested with a 30-day range and an action filter
  Then the response returns within 2 seconds p95 with 200 items and a next cursor

Scenario: Stable ordering while new rows append
  Given new entries are being written during pagination
  When I page forward using the cursor
  Then no entry is skipped or duplicated across pages

Scenario: Chain verification reports the break position
  Given a row's entry_hash is corrupted in a test fixture database
  When verify is called over the containing range
  Then verified is false and first_bad_id equals the corrupted row's id

Scenario: Manager scoping is enforced in the repository
  Given a manager calls the audit query with actor_user_id set to another user
  Then only their own entries are returned
  And the attempt is recorded

Scenario: Export is signed and audited
  When an export job completes
  Then an NDJSON file and a detached signature are produced
  And the signature verifies against the published public key
  And an audit.exported entry records the range, row count and actor

Scenario (failure): Export range too large
  Given a requested range exceeding the configured maximum
  Then the call returns 422 validation_failed naming the limit
  And no job is created

Scenario (edge): No rows match
  Then the response is 200 with an empty items array, chain_verified true and no cursor
```

## Technical notes / design
- Keyset pagination: `WHERE (id < :cursor_id) AND <filters> ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT :limit`, cursor = base64 of `{"id": <int>}` (matching the example cursor in the OpenAPI document). OFFSET is forbidden — it would both drift as rows append and degrade at depth.
- Query planning: every supported filter combination is covered by an existing or newly added index; the task ships an `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` report for each of the UI's offered combinations against the 10 M-row dataset, committed under `docs/perf/`.
- `q` full-text: `GIN` on `to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(before_state::text,'') || coalesce(after_state::text,''))` plus `object_label`; documented as the only non-trivial index build in the migration.
- Verify batches 10k rows at a time, recomputing the digest with the same canonical serialisation as the trigger; a mismatch between the app-side and trigger-side canonicalisation is itself a bug — a test pins the canonical form byte-for-byte.
- Export job: streams rows with a server-side cursor, writes gzip NDJSON to the job store, computes SHA-256, signs with Ed25519 (key from the KEK-protected store, never in the database), and publishes `result.download_url` with a short-lived signed URL.
- Error codes: `forbidden`, `validation_failed`, `rate_limited`, `not_found` (unknown job).

## Test plan
- **Unit**: cursor encode/decode; filter→SQL mapping incl. repeated `action` params; scoping applied in the repository (called directly, bypassing the handler); canonical-serialisation equality with the trigger; export row redaction preserved.
- **Contract**: schemathesis over `/admin/audit`, `/admin/audit/verify`, `/admin/audit/export`, `/admin/jobs/{jobId}`.
- **Integration**: 10 M-row seeded database (generator committed, seeding documented) — latency assertions for the first page and for each offered filter combination; pagination stability under concurrent writes.
- **Security**: attempt UPDATE/DELETE on `audit_log` as `cv_app` → must fail on grants **and** on the `forbid_mutation` trigger; corrupted-chain fixture; export range-limit and rate-limit tests.
- **Perf**: k6 profile from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` for the query endpoint.
- Coverage ≥90% on the audit read module (security-relevant module, per the R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Threats: **repudiation** (the endpoint must never expose a write path — the router declares only GET/POST-verify/POST-export and the database grants deny mutation regardless); **information disclosure** (manager scoping in the repository layer; export contains Confidential + PII data, so it is signed, rate-limited, range-limited and audited); **tampering** (chain verification is the detection control; a break is a `critical` system event, not a 500).
- The signing key lives outside the database (per `audit_checkpoints` convention and ADR-0009); the service holds only the private key handle, and key rotation is documented.
- Data classification: Confidential + PII (`actor_ip`). Requires `security` label and Security-engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes

title: Implement the feature-flag service, control allowlist and system push
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-007's NFR contains the single most important constraint in this epic: "flags are server-side with a client push; **no flag may weaken a security control**." A flag system without that guarantee is a privilege-escalation mechanism with a friendly UI.

The storage model exists (`21-database-schema.md` §3.9 `feature_flags`, `feature_flag_overrides`, resolution order user → role → percentage → default, kill-switch flags bypassing cache and re-read every 5 s) and the API is declared (`GET /admin/feature-flags`, `PUT /admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}`). This task implements the service behind them, the push over the WS `system` topic, and the maintenance-mode control plane that SCR-148 drives.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/feature-flags` → resolved flags with kind, description, value, default, overrides, `updated_by`, `updated_at`. Permission `flags:read`.
- `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/{flagKey}` (`flags:write`, step-up required): validates against the flag's kind, requires a `reason`, writes `feature_flags`/`feature_flag_overrides` transactionally and emits the audited `flags.change` with before/after.
- **Security-control allowlist**: a declarative registry mapping each flag key to what it may gate, with an explicit deny list of categories (authentication, RBAC enforcement, audit writing, the native-SL invariant, withdrawal permission, rate limiting). A flag whose declared gate falls in a denied category fails **at startup**, not at write time — the system refuses to boot with an unsafe flag definition.
- `trading.live_enabled` special case: enabling requires `reason` **and** `evidence_url`; without them the call fails `validation_failed` / `gate_evidence_required` (the gate's evidence binding itself is E44-T04; this service enforces the precondition).
- **Push**: on any flag change, publish a `SystemUpdate {kind: "feature_flags", feature_flags: {...}}` frame to every connected session over the auto-subscribed `system` topic, filtered by role so a client only learns about flags it may see.
- **Maintenance mode** control plane: a kill-switch-class flag that blocks order acceptance server-side within 200 ms, cancels running algos, optionally keeps the recorder running, broadcasts the notice within 2 s, and is audited as `maintenance.enabled|disabled`.
- Flag-resolution caching with the documented exception: `is_killswitch` flags bypass the cache and are re-read every 5 s.

## Out of scope
- Enabling the live gate with its evidence record (**E44-T04**, which owns US-ADMIN-012 together with `E44-S01`) and the security centre (**E43-S02**, which owns US-ADMIN-010 / SCR-137). This task only enforces the precondition; it exposes no way to satisfy it.
- The kill-switch engine (E39) — maintenance mode is a separate, lighter control that composes with it.
- The console UI (E42-S05).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flag change reaches every client
  Given three authenticated sessions are connected
  When a boolean flag is changed
  Then all three receive a system frame of kind feature_flags within 2 seconds
  And the effective value at each client matches server-side resolution

Scenario: No flag may weaken a security control
  Given a flag definition declares that it gates RBAC enforcement
  When the service starts
  Then startup fails with a clear error naming the flag and the denied category

Scenario: Live enablement requires evidence
  When trading.live_enabled is set to true without an evidence_url
  Then the call fails 422 with gate_evidence_required
  And no write occurs and the attempt is audited

Scenario: Maintenance mode blocks orders promptly
  When maintenance mode is enabled
  Then order acceptance is rejected server-side within 200 ms
  And every session receives the maintenance notice within 2 seconds
  And native exchange stops are untouched

Scenario (failure): Flag write conflicts
  Given two owners change the same flag concurrently
  Then one write succeeds and the other returns 409 with the current value
  And both attempts are audited

Scenario (edge): Kill-switch-class flag freshness
  Given a kill-switch flag is changed directly in the database
  Then the service reflects the new value within 5 seconds without a restart
```

## Technical notes / design
- Resolution: user override → role override → percentage rollout (`hash(user_id || flag_key)`) → default, exactly as documented in `21-database-schema.md` §3.9. The resolver is a pure function with a table-driven test per branch.
- The allowlist registry is code (`flags/registry.py`), not configuration, so it is code-reviewed and cannot be edited at runtime: `FlagSpec(key, kind, description, gates=Category.UI_SURFACE|...)`. A `Category` in `{AUTH, RBAC, AUDIT, RISK_INVARIANT, RATE_LIMIT}` is rejected at import time.
- Push path: the flag service publishes to the WS hub, which fans out on the `system` topic (auto-subscribed, un-unsubscribable per `23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2); payload content is filtered by role, matching that section's "content filtered by role" note.
- Maintenance mode sets a process-wide gate checked by the order-acceptance dependency before any OMS work, so the 200 ms bound is structural rather than best-effort.
- Concurrency: flag writes take a row lock and compare `updated_at`; a mismatch returns `409` with the current value rather than last-write-wins.
- Error codes: `validation_failed`, `gate_evidence_required`, `stepup_required`, `forbidden`, `conflict`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: resolver truth table (user/role/percentage/default × boolean/percentage/variant); allowlist rejection at import for each denied category; evidence precondition; conflict detection; kill-switch cache bypass timing.
- **Contract**: `/admin/feature-flags` GET/PUT against the OpenAPI schema; `SystemUpdate` frames validated against `23-ws-protocol.md` §15.9.
- **Integration**: three connected WS clients receiving the push within 2 s; maintenance mode rejecting an order within 200 ms measured end-to-end.
- **Security**: attempt to define a flag gating auth (must fail startup); attempt a flags:write without step-up (403 `stepup_required` + audit); role-filtered push asserting a manager does not learn owner-only flag keys.
- Coverage ≥90% (security-relevant module).

## Security notes
- Threats: **elevation of privilege via configuration** — the central threat, mitigated by the compile-time allowlist and a Semgrep rule (E42-X03) forbidding flag lookups inside auth/RBAC/audit modules; **tampering** (server-side resolution only; the client store is advisory for UI, never for enforcement); **repudiation** (every change audited with actor, reason, before/after); **DoS** (maintenance mode is itself protected by step-up so it cannot be used to halt trading maliciously).
- Fail-closed rule: if the flag store is unreachable, flags resolve to their **default** values, and safety-relevant defaults are the restrictive ones.
- Data classification: Confidential configuration. Requires `security` label and Security-engineer review.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Flag resolution ≤1 ms p99 from cache; cache TTL 30 s for normal flags, bypassed for `is_killswitch` (re-read every 5 s).
- Push fan-out to all sessions within 2 s; maintenance-mode order blocking within 200 ms.
- The push carries only changed flags, not the whole set, to keep the `system` topic within its 1 000 ms throttle budget.

## Observability
- Audit: `flags.change {key, before, after, reason, evidence_url?}` (high severity), `maintenance.enabled|disabled`.
- Metrics: `cv_feature_flag_evaluations_total{key}`, `cv_feature_flag_changes_total{key,result}`, `cv_flag_push_latency_seconds`, `cv_maintenance_mode` gauge.
- Logs: startup logs the full flag registry with its declared gate categories, so an auditor can see what flags may touch.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] OpenAPI (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) / WS (`23-ws-protocol.md`) / internal schema (`24-internal-schemas.md`) deltas merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green.

- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Observability: metrics/log fields/audit actions listed below exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E09` — permission codes `flags:read`/`flags:write`, step-up enforcement and the audit writer.
- `E42-T01` — the admin router dependency that audits area entry, reused here.

## Branch
`feat/admin-screens-flags-api` — 2 PRs: (1) resolver + registry + REST, (2) push + maintenance mode.
