title: Implement user lifecycle: contract deltas and the disable cascade
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-10-15 (DoR plan and decision record on #965).** R2 split this Task: it keeps the lifecycle contract deltas and the disable cascade (plan slices S1 and S3–S7). Account-access grants moved to E42-T08, user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions to E42-T09, and the deferred purge to E42-T10. R3 rewrote the acceptance criteria. Every section below follows the decisions recorded on #965: R1–R7, accepted by main-orchestrator, and O1–O7, accepted on an interim basis subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. R8 (flags) and R9 (backlog hygiene) are not decided yet; #2710 tracks them together with this Task's estimate.

US-ADMIN-001's scenarios impose exact server-side semantics that the UI cannot fake:

- **Disable** (this Task): "their sessions are revoked **within 5 seconds**, their rules are disarmed, and their data is retained."
- **Delete** (E42-T10 since the split): "their audit and journal history is retained under an **anonymised reference**, and the deletion itself is audited."

US-ADMIN-002 adds the binding half, which E42-T08 now delivers: revoking an account grant must force-close the user's WS subscriptions for that account with a `revoked` frame (reason `account_scope_changed`, `23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), and permissions are re-checked "at subscribe time **and again on every change to the user's grants**" (`23-ws-protocol.md` §6.3). `22-api-openapi.yaml` still calls that frame `unsubscribed` on `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`; slice S1 corrects the wording (R3).

`22-api-openapi.yaml` already declares the routes, and `21-database-schema.md` §3.1 already defines `users`, `user_roles`, `user_account_access` and `sessions`. This Task lands the contract deltas for all four Tasks and implements the disable cascade behind `DELETE /users/{userId}`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Lifecycle contract deltas first (slice S1, C-6.1; #2658).** The OpenAPI and error-code changes for this Task and for E42-T08, E42-T09 and E42-T10 land here before any implementation (R4). Under O2 they include `acknowledge_unknown_positions` on `updateUser` for a change to `status: disabled`, because that `PATCH` runs this Task's cascade (E42-T09); its description names the cascade and `409 positions_unknown`, as `deleteUser`'s does.
- **`DELETE /api/v1/users/{userId}` (soft disable).** Set `status=disabled`; revoke **all** sessions; soft-revoke every account grant (`can_view=false`, `can_trade=false`, never a `DELETE`, so the freeze columns and `max_daily_loss_usd` survive: O4, C-12.5); disarm every rule the user authored; revoke the open invite of a user who is still `invited` (R6); retain all data. Emits one `users.disable` (R5).
- **Positions (O2).** The cascade never flattens positions or cancels orders, and no lifecycle action places an order; flatten-first stays a separate OMS action. The audit `after_state` records `positions_decision=leave` and `open_position_count`. While the count is unknown, the caller must send `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (AC7). The disable service enforces this, so `DELETE /users/{userId}` and E42-T09's `PATCH` to `disabled` behave alike.
- **Session revocation within 5 s.** Every session is revoked with reason `user_disabled` and recorded through B16 REVOKE, one `auth.session_revoked` per session (R5). The user's sockets then get `bye` (`user_disabled`) and close code 4403 (`23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5), so the client does not reconnect, and the next REST call from a revoked session gets 401 `unauthenticated`.
- **Fail-closed scope readers (O5, C-2.21).** The scope readers check `users.status`, so a disabled user's armed rules lose their permissions at once, before the asynchronous disarm finishes. Slice S5 adds them, before slice S6 serves the route.
- **Last-owner protection on disable.** Disabling the only remaining Owner returns 409 `conflict`, a self-target returns 403, and a disable racing a demotion can never leave the installation without an enabled Owner (one transaction under the owner lock).
- **Audit (R5, C-2.9).** Every mutation is audited write-ahead with before/after, and refused calls from a forbidden role or against oneself are audited too. If the audit writer is unavailable, the call returns 503 `audit_unavailable` and nothing changes (AC8).
- **Docs (R5, slice S4, C-15.2).** `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 adds `user_disabled` to `sessions.revoked_reason`. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 uses the user-lifecycle names that `audit/actions.py` registers instead of `user.created`, `user.disabled` and `user.role_assigned`. SCR-122's audit line in `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` names `users.access_change` instead of `user.assignment_changed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on any cascade step: the cascade enforces RBAC and audit, which no flag may gate (C-4.14). The work stays dark instead: slices S3–S5 add no route, and `DELETE /users/{userId}` stays `not_mounted` in the RBAC matrix until slice S6 serves it. This is R8's proposal on #965; it has no recorded decision yet (#2710), and C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.
- Moved by the R2 split: `?purge=true` (E42-T10); `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` (E42-T08); `PATCH /users/{userId}`, `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` and admin session listing and revocation (E42-T09).

Slices kept by this Task (from the DoR plan on #965; PR titles `feat(accounts-admin): <summary> (E42-T04)`, branches under `## Branch`):

| # | Summary | Slug | ~LOC | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | lifecycle contract deltas | `lifecycle-contract` | 320 | O1–O3, R1–R5 |
| S3 | disable store, owner lock, write-ahead audit | `lifecycle-store` | 380 | S1, #2508, O4 |
| S4 | disable service: B16 revoke, socket close | `lifecycle-service` | 360 | S3, O2, R7 |
| S5 | rule-disarm and scope adapters; fail-closed scope readers | `cascade-adapters` | 330 | S4, O5 |
| S6 | serve `DELETE /users/{userId}` | `delete-user-route` | 360 | S5, the STRIDE appendix (O1, #2729) |
| S7 | SR-029 end to end | `disable-cascade-e2e` | 280 | S6 |

The fail-closed scope readers (O5) moved from S7 to S5 in the review of #2654. Otherwise an Owner could disable a manager between the S6 and S7 merges while the manager's armed rules kept their permissions until the asynchronous disarm finished (SR-029, C-2.21). The six slices still total about 2,030 LOC.

## Out of scope
- Authentication, password hashing, TOTP and session issuance (E09).
- Rule engine internals — this task calls the disarm interface (E35) rather than reimplementing it.
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).
- The `ws` transport close semantics themselves (E10/E09) — consumed.
- Account-access grants (E42-T08); user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09); the deferred purge with its migration, anonymisation and the surrogate (E42-T10, O6) — the R2 split of 2026-10-15.
- Flattening positions or cancelling orders (O2).
- Alerts of a disabled user, which keep evaluating today: an E40 follow-up (O7).
- A user-row version counter or `grants_version` (dropped by R7).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC1 Disable revokes sessions within 5 seconds
  Given manager M has two active sessions and one armed rule
  When an owner disables M
  Then within 5 seconds on a fake clock M's next REST call gets 401 unauthenticated
  And every socket of M receives bye with reason user_disabled and closes with 4403
  And M's rule is disarmed
  And all of M's data is retained

Scenario (edge): AC5 Disable is audited once and idempotent
  Given manager M has no sessions
  When an owner disables M
  Then exactly one users.disable audit record is written
  When the owner disables M again
  Then the call returns 204, changes nothing and writes no further audit record

Scenario (failure): AC6 A self-target is refused
  When an owner disables themselves
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC6 The last owner cannot be disabled
  Given owner A is the only enabled owner
  When an owner disables A
  Then the call returns 409 conflict and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC6 A demotion racing a disable keeps an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two owners
  When a demotion of A races a disable of B
  Then at least one enabled owner remains
  And the losing call writes no audit record

Scenario (failure): AC7 Unknown positions need an explicit acknowledgement
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner disables M without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner disables M
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC2 (history retained under an anonymised reference), AC3 (grant revocation ends the subscription with `revoked`, not `unsubscribed`) and AC4 (parallel cross-demotions, exactly one wins) moved with their scope to E42-T10, E42-T08 and E42-T09 (R2). The numbering is kept so the slice plan's test names still map; AC6–AC8 also apply to the routes of those Tasks.

## Technical notes / design
- **One transaction per disable (R7).** Lock the user row, lock the owner rows as #2508 does, apply the change (status, session rows, soft revoke of grants), run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead through the hook, then commit. The audit writer is WAL-first and outside the database transaction (`audit/writer.py`), so the hook runs only after the constraints pass, and a raise from it rolls the transaction back (AC8; `test_audit_hook_raise_rolls_back`).
- **After commit (R7).** Record B16 REVOKE for each revoked session, end the user's sockets, push `user_disabled` (`ConnectionRegistry` in `ws/permissions.py`, with #2318), disarm the user's rules through B9 DISARM (slice S5) and revoke an open invite (R6). A failure in any of these steps is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- **Sockets.** End them through `ConnectionRegistry.user_disabled(user_id)` (reached as `app.state.ws_events.user_disabled`), or through `RevocationHub.revoke(session_id, "user_disabled")` per session, which sends the same `bye` and closes 4403 since #2581 merged (2026-10-15). Never end a disable with another reason: every other reason closes 4401, which tells the client to refresh its token and reconnect (comment on #965, 2026-10-15 18:59Z).
- **No version counters (R7).** A user-row counter or `grants_version` would add per-frame database reads in the WS lane. Changes are pushed through `user_disabled` and `grants_changed` plus #2318's versioned permission snapshots.
- **Last-owner protection.** Lock the owner rows inside the transaction (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`, as #2508 does); a check-then-act without the lock is exactly the race AC6 tests.
- **Fail-closed scope readers (O5, slice S5).** Add `u.status = 'active' AND u.deleted_at IS NULL` to `_PERMS` (`storage/repositories/scope_sqlalchemy.py`) and `_PERMS_SQL` (`storage/repositories/identity_sqlalchemy.py`). B9 defers DISARM while a rule is evaluating or acting (`28-statechart-catalogue.md` §B9.3), so safety rests on O4 and O5. Slice S5 adds both predicates before slice S6 serves the route. The E35 lane is told.
- **Positions (O2).** Read the open-position count before the change. `_NoPositionStore` (`app.py`) reports it as unknown, which needs the acknowledgement (AC7), as `POST /users/{userId}/mfa/reset` does.
- **Error codes** come only from `x-error-codes` in `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, no live step-up for the `users` action class), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409, last owner), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7) and `audit_unavailable` (503, AC8), which slice S1 registers (R4). `version_conflict` (412) is the stale `If-Match` of E42-T09's `PATCH /users/{userId}`, the only lifecycle route that takes `If-Match`; slice S1 documents it there.

## Test plan
Named tests per slice (from the DoR plan on #965):
- **S1:** `test_openapi_conformance`; `test_route_matrix` (new rows `not_mounted`); `error_registry_single_source`; `python scripts/generate_protocol_models.py --check`.
- **S3** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_disable_one_tx` (AC1); `test_keeps_freeze_and_cap` (O4); `test_audit_hook_raise_rolls_back`; `test_last_owner_409` (AC6); `test_concurrent_demote_and_disable_keep_owner` (AC6: 10 pairs behind #2508's lock-hold barrier; the loser gets 409 and writes no audit); `test_twice_one_audit` (AC5).
- **S4:** `test_step_order`; `test_b16_revoke_per_session`; `test_store_failure_no_post_commit`; `test_post_commit_failure_alerts`; `test_self_target_403_audited` (AC6); `test_positions_decision_never_flattens` (O2); `test_invited_revokes_invite`; `test_log_and_metrics_per_step`.
- **S5:** `test_disarms_owner_user_id_rules`; `test_refused_rule_does_not_stop_loop`; `test_idempotency_key_deterministic`; `test_scope_refresh_failure_fails_closed`; `test_disabled_user_no_rule_perms` (O5).
- **S6:** `test_guard_order_before_change`; `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_self_target_403`; `test_last_owner_409`; `test_audit_down_503` (AC8); `test_positions_unknown_409` (AC7); `test_twice_204_one_audit` (AC5); `test_purge_400_flag_off` (`?purge=true` answers 400 until E42-T10's S14 serves it; the name assumes R8's flag, which is still undecided, #2710).
- **S7:** `test_rest_401_ws_4403_within_5s` (AC1); `test_rule_disarmed_audited` (AC1); `test_data_retained` (AC1); Postgres `test_delete_route_two_sessions_one_rule` (AC1).
- The 5-second bound runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network. Until #2525 merged (2026-10-15), WS private topics were deny-all in the deployed app, so AC1 could be proven only in-process. The real backend now loads the WS principal from the store (`build_ws_principal_loader` in `app.py`), so `test_delete_route_two_sessions_one_rule` can assert the socket close against the deployed app as well.
- Coverage ≥90% (security-relevant module M19).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`. The user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before slice S6.
- Threats: **elevation of privilege** (`DELETE /users/{userId}` is `users:write`, Owner-only, step-up gated, never self-targeted, and audited); **denial of service** (disabling the last Owner would lock the installation out permanently, hence the locked last-owner check); **repudiation** (write-ahead audit, refused calls included); **tampering with risk state** (the soft revoke keeps freeze state and caps, so a disable and a later re-grant cannot unfreeze a manager, C-12.5).
- `password_hash` is never returned by this route (schema-enforced).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, session IP) + Confidential (grants). Requires `security` label and Security-engineer sign-off per DoD §8.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Session revocation observable within 5 s (US-ADMIN-001); target p95 ≤1 s through the `user_disabled` push rather than polling.
- Lifecycle mutations ≤300 ms p95 excluding the rule-disarm fan-out, which is asynchronous with its own audit.
- The last-owner lock is held for the duration of one short transaction only; contention is negligible at this user count but the lock is still correct at scale.

## Observability
- Audit (R5): one `users.disable` per disable (AC5), with before/after and the `positions_decision` and `open_position_count` fields (O2); one `auth.session_revoked` per revoked session, recorded through B16 REVOKE; refused calls from a forbidden role or against oneself (AC6). Any new action registers in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits it.
- Metrics: `cv_user_lifecycle_total{action,result}`; post-commit step failures are counted and alerted (R7). Session-close latency goes on the `auth_revocation_latency_seconds` histogram that E09-S03 specifies (`auth/metrics.py`, `docs/ops/runbooks/auth-rbac.md` §4), not on a second histogram.
- Logs: one structured line per cascade step with the step name and outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] AC1 and AC5–AC8 pass as automated tests (the 5-second bound on a fake clock); Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] Slices S1 and S3–S7 merged. S1 and S3–S6 say `Refs #965` plus `Partial: slice k of 6`; only S7 carries the closing line (R2, C-4.7).
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] Contract deltas (slice S1) merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green; the `DELETE /users/{userId}` row in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` is `executed` from S6.
- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on every slice; the STRIDE appendix (#2729) merged before S6 (O1).
- [ ] Observability: the audit actions, metrics and log fields listed under Observability exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] Docs updated in slice S4 (C-15.2): `21-database-schema.md` §3.1.4 `revoked_reason` (`user_disabled`), `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 vocabulary, and SCR-122's audit names in `14-screens-catalogue.md`.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.
- [ ] Done only after E09-X04 (#300) has run the SR-029 drill (#2494) against the merged cascade and reached Done (R1).

## Dependencies
- `E09` — sessions, MFA, RBAC policy decision point, audit writer and the WS authentication/close semantics this task drives.
- `E27-S04` was removed from `blocked_by` on 2026-10-15 (R1 on #965): the cascade only consumes grants.
- Start waiver (R1, mirroring the one on #963): E09-K02, E09-X02 and E09-X04 are waived for the start and stay required for Done. Order: the cascade merges, E09-X04 (#300) runs the SR-029 drill (#2494) and reaches Done, then this Task reaches Done.
- Before slice S3: #2508 (owner lock and write-ahead audit for role changes), which builds on #2502. Before slice S4: #2318 (versioned WS permission snapshots). Before slice S6: the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (O1, #2729). #2525, which an end-to-end proof in the deployed app needed, merged on 2026-10-15.
- E42-T08, E42-T09 and E42-T10 are blocked by this Task: they take their contract from slice S1.
- Estimate: the 3 points are capacity-driven (Sprint 15 is at its accepted +8 overage), not sized from the ~2,030 LOC of six slices. Agreeing it (C-11.1 #7) and recording the flag decision (R8, C-11.1 #13) are open in #2710.
- Dependents: E42-S02, E42-S03 and E42-X03 list only this Task, although part of what they consume moved to E42-T08–T10; their re-point and re-sprint are open in #2710. E42-X02 lists all four Tasks, and E38-S07 lists E42-T08.

## Branch
One branch per slice PR: `feat/e42-t04-lifecycle-contract` (S1, #2658), `feat/e42-t04-lifecycle-store` (S3), `feat/e42-t04-lifecycle-service` (S4), `feat/e42-t04-cascade-adapters` (S5), `feat/e42-t04-delete-user-route` (S6) and `feat/e42-t04-disable-cascade-e2e` (S7). These are the slice plan's names on #965; S1 already runs on its branch.

## References

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.2 private topics, §6.3, §9.5 mid-connection authorisation changes, §15.9 `SystemUpdate`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 identity/RBAC/sessions, §3.9 settings & feature flags, §3.10 audit log
- `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` C14 Auth/RBAC/Audit, C15 Admin, §3.10, §3.11
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0010-auth-and-rbac.md`, `ADR-0009-secrets-and-key-management.md`, `ADR-0014-observability.md`
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`, `04-security-program.md`, `05-accessibility-standard.md`, `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`
- `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3 epic register (E42, R3, S16–S17), §7 R3, §11 dependency graph

- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 (D1–D6), SR-029, SR-055; `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` U4, U24, U25
- #965 (DoR plan and decision record, 2026-10-15)

## Agent execution brief
**Read first**

Never silently work around a failing gate or a missing dependency ticket.

title: Wire the admin health, incidents and backups read models to the admin API
body:
## Context
SCR-143, SCR-144 and SCR-146 need three read models that sit between the observability/ops machinery and the admin UI: the full health report, the incident read model over `system_events`, and the backup run list with its verify/restore job surfaces. All three are declared in `22-api-openapi.yaml` (`GET /admin/health`, `GET /admin/incidents`, `GET|POST /admin/backups`, `POST /admin/backups/{backupId}/verify|restore`).

`GET /admin/health` is implemented by **E04-T04** as part of the observability baseline; `GET /admin/incidents` is described as "read-model over `system_events` at `error` and `critical` severity, grouped into incidents with first/last occurrence and affected component". This task delivers the incident grouping and the backup admin surface, and adapts the E04 health payload to the `system` WS topic's component vocabulary so the UI has one shape, not two.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /api/v1/admin/incidents?status&cursor&limit`: group `system_events` rows at `error`/`critical` into incidents keyed by `(component, signature)` with `first_seen`, `last_seen`, `count`, `status` (`open|acknowledged|resolved`), duration and resolution text; cursor-paginated.
- Incident **acknowledge** transition with an audited `incident.acknowledged`.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/backups` (list with kind/status filters), `POST /api/v1/admin/backups` (run now), `POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/verify`, `POST /api/v1/admin/backups/{backupId}/restore` — all long-running operations returning a `job_id` polled through `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` (plumbing shared with E42-T02's export).
- **Restore preconditions enforced server-side**: maintenance mode must be active; open positions require an explicit acknowledgement flag in the request; both are rejected with `conflict` rather than being trusted from the UI.
- Backup **download** issues a short-lived signed URL, audited at high severity, and never logs the URL.
- Health payload adaptation: map E04's `HealthReport` component names onto the `SystemUpdate.components[]` vocabulary so snapshot and delta agree; unknown components pass through rather than being dropped.
- Per-component staleness: each component carries `last_good_at` so the UI can mark a tile stale rather than showing a plausible but old number.

## Out of scope
- The probes, metrics registry and the health aggregation itself (E04-T04).
- The backup engine, scheduler and restore executor (ops/E45) — this task exposes and guards them.
- The UI (E42-S06).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Incidents group repeated events
  Given 40 error-severity system_events share a component and signature
  Then they appear as one incident with count 40, a first and last occurrence and status open

Scenario: Acknowledge is audited
  When an incident is acknowledged
  Then its status becomes acknowledged
  And an incident.acknowledged audit entry records the actor

Scenario: Restore refuses without maintenance mode
  Given maintenance mode is off
  When a restore is requested
  Then the call returns 409 conflict naming maintenance mode as the precondition
  And no job is created

Scenario: Restore with open positions requires acknowledgement
  Given two positions are open and maintenance mode is on
  When a restore is requested without the acknowledgement flag
  Then the call returns 409 conflict stating that open positions must be acknowledged

Scenario (failure): Backup verification fails
  Given a stored backup whose digest does not match
  When verify runs
  Then the job completes with status failed and a reason
  And the backup row records the failed verification

Scenario (edge): Health component unknown to the client
  Given the health report includes a component the UI does not know
  Then it is still returned rather than filtered out
```

## Technical notes / design
- Incident signature = stable hash of `(component, error_class, normalised_message)`; normalisation strips ids, timestamps and symbols so the same fault does not fragment into thousands of incidents.
- Grouping is a materialised read model refreshed on write (the `system_events` insert path notifies), not an on-request aggregation — the screen must not pay for the grouping.
- Restore is the most destructive operation in the product; its preconditions are enforced in the service, not the router, so any future caller inherits them.
- Job plumbing reuses `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` from E42-T02 (`kind` in `audit_export|backup|backup_verify|backup_restore|recorder_compact|recorder_purge`).
- Signed download URLs expire in 5 minutes and are single-use.
- Error codes: `conflict` (preconditions), `not_found`, `forbidden`, `rate_limited`.

## Test plan
- **Unit**: signature normalisation (table-driven, including messages differing only by id/symbol/timestamp); precondition guards; staleness computation; health component mapping incl. pass-through.
- **Contract**: all listed routes against the OpenAPI document; job status transitions.
- **Integration**: seeded `system_events` producing the expected grouping; restore precondition matrix (maintenance on/off × positions open/closed × ack flag).
- **Security**: RBAC matrix; download URL expiry and single use; audit emission for download and restore.
- Coverage ≥85%.

## Security notes
- Threats: **destruction of data** (restore) — server-side preconditions, step-up, high-severity audit; **information disclosure** (backup artefacts contain envelope-encrypted secrets — download is signed-URL, short-lived, single-use, audited, never logged); **information disclosure via incidents** (messages may contain internal detail — the read model applies the same redaction allowlist as the audit exporter).
- Data classification: operational Confidential; backup artefacts Secret-bearing.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- Incident list first page ≤400 ms p95 over 1 M `system_events` rows thanks to the materialised grouping.
- Health snapshot ≤200 ms p95 (E04 owns the probe budget; this adapter adds no I/O).
- Backup list ≤200 ms; all long operations are jobs, never synchronous requests.

## Observability
- Audit: `incident.acknowledged`, `backup.run`, `backup.verified`, `backup.restore` (high), `backup.downloaded` (high), `backup.deleted`.
- Metrics: `cv_incidents_open` gauge, `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds`, `cv_backup_verify_failures_total`, `cv_restore_jobs_total{result}`.
- Alerting: `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds` beyond the schedule interval pages per ADR-0014.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Acceptance criteria objectively verified by tests or a recorded measurement.
- [ ] Backend coverage ≥85% on new/changed lines (≥90% for audit/RBAC-touching modules per `30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).
- [ ] OpenAPI (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) / WS (`23-ws-protocol.md`) / internal schema (`24-internal-schemas.md`) deltas merged **before** implementation (interface-first, `01-sdlc-and-branching.md` §10) and contract tests green.
- [ ] Alembic migration is forward+backward tested on a seeded database; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` updated.
- [ ] security: SAST (Semgrep/Bandit/CodeQL) and SCA clean or triaged; Security engineer review comment present.
- [ ] Observability: metrics/log fields/audit actions listed below exist and are asserted in a test.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or explicit "QA capacity deviation" note).
- [ ] PR(s) merged to `main` via the merge queue with 2 approvals incl. 1 code-owner.

## Dependencies
- `E04` — health report, metrics registry, `system_events` writer.

title: Spike: audit query plan and index strategy at 10 million rows
body:
## Context
US-ADMIN-009 sets a hard NFR — "search over 10 million entries returns the first page in ≤2 s" — and SCR-135 tightens it for the common case to a ≤400 ms filter round-trip. The existing indexes (`ix_audit_time`, `ix_audit_actor`, `ix_audit_action`, `ix_audit_object`, partial `ix_audit_sev`) were designed for the write path and single-column lookups; the UI offers **combinations** (actor + action + severity + range, plus full-text `q` over JSONB), and a combination that falls back to a bitmap heap scan over 10 M rows will not meet the budget.

Committing to an index set is a schema decision with a real migration cost (a GIN index over JSONB on 10 M rows is not free to build), so it is resolved by measurement before E42-T02 implements, rather than discovered during it.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Generate a realistic 10 M-row `audit_log` dataset with the production action distribution (order actions dominating, auth events next, admin actions rare) and realistic `before_state`/`after_state` payload sizes; commit the generator.
- Measure `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` for each filter combination the SCR-135 filter bar offers (≈12 combinations), at page 1 and at deep cursor positions.
- Compare candidate index strategies: (a) existing single-column set, (b) composite `(action, event_ts DESC)` / `(actor_user_id, action, event_ts DESC)`, (c) BRIN on `event_ts` given the append-only insert order, (d) GIN over the tsvector of the detail payload for `q`, (e) a partial index for the high-severity view.
- Measure the **build cost and ongoing write overhead** of each candidate — the audit write path is on every state-changing request, so index write amplification is a production concern, not a detail.
- Decide, and record the decision plus the numbers as **ADR-0021 Audit query and index strategy** in `docs/plan/27-adrs/`.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the endpoints (E42-T02 consumes this spike's conclusion).
- Partitioning the audit table — explicitly evaluated as a question but out of scope to implement here; if the spike concludes partitioning is required, it becomes a follow-up Task.
- Changing the hash-chain design (out of bounds; the chain is a security invariant).

## Acceptance criteria
- **Timebox**: 3 days. If the budget cannot be met by indexing alone, the decision criterion is pre-agreed: recommend monthly range partitioning on `event_ts` as a follow-up Task rather than extending the spike.
- Question 1: which index set meets ≤400 ms p95 for the common filter combinations and ≤2 s for the worst (full-text over a wide range)? Answered with numbers per combination.
- Question 2: what is the write-path overhead (ms per INSERT, p50/p99) of the recommended set versus today's? Answered with a measured benchmark at the production write rate.
- Question 3: what does the GIN index cost to build on 10 M rows, and can it be built `CONCURRENTLY` inside the deployment window?
- Deliverables: benchmark script + dataset generator committed; results table; **ADR-0021** recorded with the decision (including "defer" as a valid, recorded outcome); follow-up tickets filed; `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced.
- Explicitly **not** expected to produce production-shippable code beyond the benchmark harness and the migration draft.

## Technical notes / design
- Benchmark harness: `pytest-benchmark` plus raw `psql` timings to avoid driver overhead masking plan differences; run on the reference machine described in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` with a cold and a warm buffer cache.
- Keyset pagination is assumed (OFFSET is already ruled out); deep-cursor measurements use a cursor at the 9 M-th row.
- Write overhead measured by inserting 100k rows with and without each candidate index, reporting p50/p99 per insert including the chain trigger's advisory lock.
- The canonical hash-chain trigger must remain untouched; index changes must not alter insert ordering semantics.

## Test plan
- The spike's output *is* measurement; the harness itself carries a smoke test so the numbers are reproducible by a reviewer.
- A reviewer must be able to re-run `make audit-bench` and obtain the same ranking (absolute numbers may vary by machine; the ranking must not).

## Security notes
- The generated dataset must contain **synthetic** data only — no production payloads, no real emails or IPs; the generator is reviewed for this explicitly.
- Any index over `before_state`/`after_state` must not create a new disclosure path (indexes are not readable by the app role beyond the existing table grants).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — spike, no UI.

## Performance notes
This spike exists to establish the performance facts; budgets under test are ≤400 ms common-case filter round-trip and ≤2 s worst case (US-ADMIN-009, SCR-135).

## Observability
Findings feed `cv_audit_query_duration_seconds{filter_class}` bucket boundaries chosen in E42-T02, so the dashboards are calibrated to the measured distribution rather than to guesses.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Questions answered with recorded evidence (benchmark numbers, results table, plan excerpts).
- [ ] **ADR-0021** written in `docs/plan/27-adrs/` recording the decision, including a "defer with reason" outcome if that is the conclusion.
- [ ] Follow-up tickets filed for the chosen path with the findings linked.
- [ ] Spike code promoted (benchmark harness + dataset generator) or explicitly marked throwaway.
- [ ] Findings presented at Sprint Review.
- [ ] `32-risk-register.md` updated if a new risk surfaced or one was retired.

## Dependencies
- None. Runs against a seeded database using the schema already defined in `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1; deliberately unblocked so it can precede E42-T02.

## Branch

Delivery is executed by parallel AI agents with a single human owner (`@basiltt`). Where this ticket's text assumes the original 15-person org, apply these substitutions — they are binding and satisfy the corresponding DoR/DoD items:

title: Document admin operations and record ADR-0022 on the admin re-auth model
body:
## Context
Two decisions made in this epic deserve a written record because they will be questioned later and re-litigating them from memory is expensive:

1. **The admin re-auth model** — owner-only plus a 15-minute server-issued elevation token, with router-404/API-403 non-disclosure and a pending-save queue rather than a logout on expiry. This is a deliberate trade-off between friction and blast radius, and it is not obvious.
2. **Flags may never gate a security control** — enforced at startup by a compile-time registry (E42-T03). A future engineer will want to add "just one" auth-related flag; the ADR is what stops that.

Separately, `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` and `22-api-openapi.yaml` must be reconciled with what actually shipped, per the Story/Task DoD ("docs reflect final shipped behavior … if they diverged").

- Extend the flag-safety decision into the same ADR or a short **ADR-0023 — Feature flags may not gate security controls**, whichever the Architect prefers at review; record the compile-time registry as the enforcement mechanism.

title: UX research: how an owner supervises, delegates and investigates
body:
## Context
The admin area is 14 user stories and ~15 screens serving exactly one persona in a specific state of mind: **P1 Owner wearing the P4 Admin hat** (`docs/plan/10-personas.md`). Designing it as "CRUD screens for settings" would miss what the stories actually describe — supervision under time pressure (US-ADMIN-004 "supervise at a glance"), delegation with consequences (US-ADMIN-002 unbind-with-open-positions), and investigation after something went wrong (US-ADMIN-009 "so that investigation is practical").

Those three modes want different information architectures, and choosing wrongly is expensive to undo once eight screens are built. This research ticket exists to answer that before wireframes start, in line with the design-ahead rule (`00-planning-brief.md`: design runs ≥2 sprints ahead; this runs three ahead of the S16 build).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Structured sessions with the Owner (and, where available, a manager) covering three scripted scenarios: (1) *supervise* — "a manager's account is approaching its daily loss cap, what do you do?"; (2) *delegate* — "onboard a new manager and scope them to one sub-account"; (3) *investigate* — "an order was placed that you did not expect; find out who, when and under what permissions."
- Card-sort of the admin area's information: which of users / accounts / profiles / audit / health / flags / recorder / security / backups belong together, and what the owner expects on the landing page (SCR-120) versus one click away.
- Comprehension test of the vocabulary this area forces on the user: "step-up", "re-authentication", "elevation", "impersonation / view as", "hash chain", "append-only", "kill switch", "maintenance mode", "flag". Any term the owner cannot explain back is a copy defect, not a training problem.
- Specific risk probes: does the owner understand that **disabling a user revokes sessions but retains data**? That **deleting retains anonymised history**? That **unbinding with open positions forces a choice**? That **restore does not change anything on Bybit**? Each is a place where a wrong mental model causes real loss.
- Deliverable: a research report in `docs/design/research/e42-admin.md` with findings, verbatim quotes, an IA recommendation for SCR-120's tile set and grouping, a vocabulary decision list (term → keep / replace with X), and a prioritised list of comprehension risks feeding the copy work in E42-D02/D03.

## Out of scope
- Wireframes and hi-fi (E42-D02, E42-D03, E42-D04, E42-D05).
- Research for accounts/keys (E27) and profiles (E28) — already done in their own epics; this ticket reads those reports rather than repeating them.
- Quantitative usability metrics — the population is one owner plus a few managers; this is qualitative by necessity and says so.

## Acceptance criteria
- At least three scripted sessions completed and recorded (with consent), covering supervise, delegate and investigate.
- The card-sort produces a recommended SCR-120 tile set and grouping, explicitly reconciled with the catalogue's stated tiles (users, accounts, keys needing rotation, recorder, storage, health, flags, last backup) — any deviation is argued, not silently dropped.
- Every vocabulary term listed above has a decision recorded: keep (with a one-line in-product explanation) or replace (with the replacement).
- Each of the four risk probes has a finding: understood / partially understood / misunderstood, with the copy change that follows.
- Report merged and linked from E42-D02 and E42-D03; findings that imply a change to `14-screens-catalogue.md` are filed as catalogue amendments.
- CDO (or delegate) review comment recorded.

## Technical notes / design
- Sessions are moderated, think-aloud, against a clickable low-fidelity prototype or the existing catalogue wireframes — not a blank page.
- Card sort is open, then closed against the catalogue's grouping, so both "what the owner expects" and "does the proposed grouping survive" are answered.

- At least one session includes keyboard-only operation of the prototype, so keyboard flow problems are found in research rather than in design QA.

title: Wireframe the admin area: shell, overview, users, audit, health and flags
body:
## Context
Fifteen admin screens share one shell, one re-auth model, one audit convention and one set of destructive-confirmation patterns. Wireframing them **together**, before any hi-fi work, is what prevents fifteen slightly different treatments of the same idea.

The catalogue already fixes the skeleton for each screen (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §10 contains ASCII wireframes, data sources, states, validation, a11y, performance and a per-screen sign-off checklist). This ticket turns those into structured, reviewable wireframes that resolve the cross-screen questions the catalogue leaves open: how the re-auth countdown lives in the chrome, how destructive confirmations are graded (simple confirm vs typed confirm vs typed confirm + step-up), and how a degraded subsystem is expressed consistently across SCR-120, SCR-143 and every tile.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Wireframes at low/medium fidelity for: **CMP-087 AdminLayout** shell with the re-auth freshness badge, **SCR-149** re-auth gate, **SCR-120** overview, **SCR-121** users list, **SCR-122** user detail, **SCR-123** invite, **SCR-124** view-as, **SCR-135** audit log, **SCR-136** audit event detail, **SCR-143** system health, **SCR-144** incident log, **SCR-145** feature flags, **SCR-146** backups & restore, **SCR-148** maintenance mode, **SCR-154** permission denied.
- **Cross-screen pattern decisions**, documented once and applied everywhere:
  - The **destructive-action ladder**: which actions need a plain confirm, which need a typed confirm, which need typed confirm + step-up. (The catalogue already mandates typed confirm + step-up for purge, restore, live enablement, flag changes on trading-capability flags and user deletion.)
  - The **degraded/stale expression**: one treatment for "this value is old", one for "this subsystem is down", used identically on SCR-120 tiles, SCR-143 tiles and SCR-147's summary.
  - The **audit-visibility convention**: how a screen tells the user "this action will be recorded".
  - The **re-auth interruption pattern**: gate as overlay, form content preserved, save held and resumed.
- Role variants drawn where behaviour differs: owner, manager (hard-404 / scoped audit), viewer (audit read-only).
- Every state from each screen's catalogue entry represented: loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, integrity failure, action-in-flight.
- Review with engineering (feasibility) and security (does the wireframe imply an unsafe affordance) before the hi-fi tickets start.

## Out of scope
- Hi-fi visual design and design-system contributions (E42-D03, E42-D04, E42-D05).
- Motion specification (E42-D04).
- Screens owned by other epics: SCR-125..129 (E27), SCR-130..134 (E28/E39), SCR-137 (E43), SCR-140..142 (E16), SCR-147 (E04/E46) — referenced for consistency, not redrawn.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every screen listed in Scope has a wireframe covering all of its catalogue-listed states.
- The four cross-screen pattern decisions are written down with a rationale and applied consistently — a reviewer can pick any two screens and find the same treatment of the same idea.
- The destructive-action ladder maps every destructive action in the epic to exactly one rung; no action is unclassified.
- Role variants drawn; the manager path shows the router-404, not a disabled admin nav item.
- Engineering feasibility review and security review comments recorded; any "this cannot be built as drawn" is resolved in the wireframe, not deferred to hi-fi.
- Findings from E42-D01 are visibly addressed (vocabulary decisions applied; each comprehension risk has a design response).

## Technical notes / design
- Wireframes are built from the catalogue's ASCII layouts as the starting skeleton so the design and the spec cannot silently diverge.
- Every wireframe annotates its data source (endpoint or WS topic) so engineering can see what a screen costs before it is beautiful.
- Tiles on SCR-120 and SCR-143 are annotated as **independently resolving** — the catalogue's hard requirement that no tile blocks another must be visible in the design, not assumed in code.

## Test plan
- Reviewed against each screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item; unticked items block the ticket.
- Walked through with QA (E42-Q01) so the test plan's scenarios and the wireframes' states are the same list.

## Security notes
- Security review specifically looks for: affordances that imply mutability of the audit log (there must be none), any path that could enable live trading from the flag console, impersonation that is not obviously read-only, and any screen that displays a secret.
- Wireframes must show the non-disclosure behaviour for non-owners (404, not 403-with-details) — a design that shows a helpful "you need owner access" page would be a spec violation.

## Accessibility notes
- Focus order annotated on every wireframe; the first tab stop on the view-as screen is Exit; the first tab stop in a destructive dialog is never the destructive button.
- All status expressions are text-first; the greyscale check is applied to the wireframes themselves.
- Tables annotated with their header semantics and sort affordances; sparklines annotated with their required table alternative.

## Performance notes
- Each wireframe carries its catalogue performance budget as an annotation (SCR-120 ≤800 ms, SCR-135 ≤400 ms filter round-trip, SCR-136 ≤300 ms, SCR-143 ≤2 ms scripting/frame), so designs that would require more data than the budget allows are caught here.

Each wireframe annotates the audit/analytics events it emits, taken from the catalogue's Analytics/audit lines, so the instrumentation is designed rather than retrofitted.

title: Hi-fi: admin shell, re-auth gate, SCR-120 overview, SCR-121/122/123/124 users
body:
## Context
This is the hi-fi design the Sprint 16 stories E42-S01, E42-S02 and E42-S03 consume, delivered two sprints ahead as the design-ahead rule requires ("no frontend screen work starts until its design is signed off").

It covers the shell that every admin screen inherits and the user-administration screens, which contain the epic's two most consequential interactions: **granting account access** (the isolation boundary between managers) and **unbinding with open positions** (a choice that must not have a silent third path).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi for **CMP-087 AdminLayout** including the `color.surface.admin-tint` treatment and the re-auth countdown, **SCR-149** gate, **SCR-120** overview, **SCR-121** users list, **SCR-122** user detail, **SCR-123** invite, **SCR-124** view-as, **SCR-154** permission denied.
- **Design-system contributions**: specification updates for CMP-087 (AdminLayout), CMP-088 (PageHeader in the admin context), CMP-173 (AuditRow, as used in SCR-120's recent-activity tile), CMP-178 (SystemHealthTile) and CMP-138 (RiskCapMeter in the user-detail limits context) — each contributed to `15-component-catalogue.md` with tier, props, a11y contract, tokens and the Storybook variant list, not designed ad hoc for this screen.
- All states per the catalogue: SCR-120's per-tile loading/error/degraded; SCR-121's loading/populated/filtered-to-nothing/error; SCR-122's dirty/change-summary/saving/conflict/self-edit-guard; SCR-123's invite-shown-once; SCR-124's persistent impersonation banner with every control disabled.
- **The unbind-with-open-positions dialog** drawn in full: two named choices, no dismissal that silently picks one, and copy stating the consequence of each.
- **The limit-tightening notice** drawn: "No positions will be closed. New entries are blocked; reduce-only actions remain available."
- The **capacity line** on SCR-121 with the tier stated as a recorded fact and the at-capacity variant explaining the Business KYC path and the isolation trade-off.
- Greyscale proofs for the admin tint and every status treatment.

## Out of scope
- Audit, flags and health screens (E42-D04, E42-D05).
- Motion specification (E42-D04 covers the epic's motion in one place).
- SCR-125..134 (E27/E28/E39) and SCR-137 (E43).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every screen listed has hi-fi frames for every catalogue-listed state, at 1280×800 and 2560×1440.
- Each screen's "Design sign-off acceptance checklist" from `14-screens-catalogue.md` is ticked item by item in a comment — including SCR-120's "non-owner access hard-404s (verified, not just hidden)" and SCR-149's "expiry-during-an-admin-edit case drawn (the form's content is preserved, the save is held)".
- Design-system contributions are proposed as edits to `15-component-catalogue.md` in the same PR; no new component exists only in Figma.
- The admin tint passes the greyscale check: the admin area remains distinguishable from the trading app without colour, paired with the landmark label and page header.
- Contrast ≥4.5:1 for text and ≥3:1 for UI components throughout, annotated.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status Done by the end of Sprint 14, two sprints before E42-S01 starts.

## Technical notes / design
- Built on the design-system tokens in `16-design-system-brief.md`; no one-off colours, spacing or type sizes. New tokens (e.g. `color.surface.admin-tint`) are proposed to the design system, with contrast evidence.
- Frames are annotated with the component ids they compose, so the implementer maps design → catalogue → code without interpretation.
- Data-shape annotations reference the actual schema field names (`AdminOverview`, `User`, `AccountAccessGrant`), preventing a design that implies data the API does not return.

## Test plan
- Reviewed against the wireframe pattern decisions from E42-D02 — a hi-fi screen that quietly invents a new destructive-confirmation rung fails review.
- Handed to E42-D06 for the accessibility design review and the engineering handoff pack.
- Verified against the build in E42-D07 design QA.

## Security notes
- No screen may render a secret: the invite link is shown once with an explicit statement, and API-key material never appears in these screens at all.
- The impersonation banner must be impossible to miss and impossible to confuse with a normal session; security reviews this frame specifically.
- The permission-denied treatment must not disclose the existence of admin routes to non-owners.

## Accessibility notes
- Focus order, focus-visible treatment and keyboard paths annotated for every interactive frame.
- Status and role rendered as text; the greyscale proof accompanies each status treatment.
- The re-auth gate's `role="alertdialog"` structure, its labelled TOTP field with a format hint, and its assertive failure announcement are annotated.
- Disabled-with-reason controls annotated with the reason text that becomes `aria-describedby`.
- Reviewed in depth by E42-D06 before handoff.

## Performance notes
- SCR-120's ≤800 ms budget is annotated on the frame, with the per-tile independent-resolution requirement drawn as distinct states rather than one page-level spinner.
- Designs avoid patterns that force synchronous fan-out (for example, a single combined table that cannot render until every subsystem answers).

## Observability
Frames annotate the audit and analytics events each control emits (`users.create`, `users.disable`, `admin.view_as_started`, `admin.overview_viewed`), so instrumentation is part of the spec.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Artefacts delivered in Figma at the stated fidelity, linked from this ticket and from the relevant `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` entries.
- [ ] Every state in the screen's catalogue entry drawn (loading, empty, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded, role variants, destructive-confirmation).

## Dependencies

title: Hi-fi: SCR-135/136 audit, SCR-145 flags, SCR-148 maintenance, motion spec
body:
## Context
The audit browser and the flag console are the two admin screens where a design mistake has security consequences rather than usability ones.

For the audit log, `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-135 requires that "no edit or delete affordance exists anywhere", that the append-only guarantee is stated on screen, and that the **integrity-failure state** is designed as a security incident ("Audit chain verification failed at 2026-09-10 — contact security"), not as a retryable UI error. A designer who draws a friendly "Retry" button on that state has created a misleading affordance.

For the flag console, SCR-145 requires risky flags to be "grouped, marked and step-up-gated", `trading.live_enabled` to be drawn **blocked with its reason**, and every toggle to be confirmed as emitting an audit event with before/after.

This ticket also owns the epic's **motion specification** in one place, so eight screens do not each invent their own transitions.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Hi-fi for **SCR-135** audit log (columns, filters, integrity indicator, high-severity rows distinguishable without colour, export, empty/filtered-to-nothing, retention statement), **SCR-136** audit event detail drawer (full field set, before/after diff rendering, correlated events, links to related objects, raw record with copy, "cannot be edited or deleted" statement), **SCR-145** feature flags, **SCR-148** maintenance mode.
- The **integrity-failure state** designed explicitly as an incident state: what it says, what it offers (contact security, view the break position), and what it deliberately does *not* offer (a retry that implies transience).
- The **before/after diff** visual language, including how a redacted/secret-bearing value renders (fingerprint only) — reused by SCR-136, SCR-122's change summary and SCR-145's flag history.
- **Design-system contributions**: CMP-173 AuditRow, CMP-174 AuditFilterBar, CMP-179 FeatureFlagRow, CMP-095 FeatureFlagChip, CMP-099 PrintExportBar in the audit context — contributed to `15-component-catalogue.md`.
- **Epic motion specification**: drawer open/close, row expansion, dialog entry, the re-auth gate overlay, tile state transitions (ok → stale → error), toast/banner entry. Durations, easings and the reduced-motion behaviour, sourced from `16-design-system-brief.md`'s motion tokens; nothing in the admin area may animate a status change in a way that hides the change from a reduced-motion user.
- Export progress and failure states (async job with a job id, not an instant download).

## Out of scope
- SCR-137 security centre (E43-D01) and SCR-128 key health (E43-D02).
- Health, incidents and backups (E42-D05).
- The shell and user screens (E42-D03).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every listed screen has hi-fi frames for every catalogue-listed state, including SCR-135's integrity-failure and SCR-145's blocked `trading.live_enabled`.
- Each screen's catalogue sign-off checklist is ticked item by item in a comment.
- The audit screens contain **no** mutation affordance anywhere, and the append-only guarantee plus retention statement appear as page text.
- High-severity audit rows are distinguishable in the greyscale proof.
- The diff language renders secrets as fingerprints in every frame where a secret-bearing change is shown.
- The motion spec covers every transition used in the epic, with reduced-motion alternatives, and is contributed to `16-design-system-brief.md`.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Done by end of Sprint 14 (two sprints before E42-S04's Sprint 16 build and three before E42-S05).

## Technical notes / design
- Filter-bar design accounts for cursor pagination: no page-number affordance may be drawn, because the API is keyset-based and page numbers would be a lie.
- The "N new entries" pattern is drawn rather than live-splicing rows, preserving pagination stability.
- Export is drawn as an async job with progress and a terminal success/failure, matching `POST /admin/audit/export` → `202 {job_id}`.

## Test plan
- Checked against the wireframe pattern decisions (E42-D02) and validated in design QA (E42-D07).
- The integrity-failure frame is reviewed by the Security engineer as part of E42-X02 before sign-off.

## Security notes
- Security review is a **blocking** sign-off criterion for this ticket specifically: the audit screens' credibility is a security control.
- The flag console must contain no path that enables live trading; `trading.live_enabled` is drawn permanently blocked here with a link to the security centre.
- The diff language must make it structurally impossible to render a secret value — the component takes a fingerprint, not a value.

## Accessibility notes
- Table semantics with a caption; severity and outcome as text; the diff as a definition list with before/after explicitly labelled (catalogue requirement).
- The raw-record region is a `<pre>` with an accessible copy control whose success is announced.
- The integrity-failure banner is `role="alert"` once, then static.
- Flag toggles are labelled with the flag key **and** description, never "on/off".
- Reduced-motion variants specified for every animated transition.

## Performance notes
- Frames annotate SCR-135's ≤400 ms filter round-trip and 200-rows-per-page pagination, and SCR-136's ≤300 ms single-record fetch with lazy raw-payload expansion.
- The motion spec keeps transitions ≤200 ms so they never sit in the way of an operator working quickly under pressure.

## Observability
Frames annotate `audit.viewed`, `audit.record_viewed`, `audit.exported`, `flags.change`, `maintenance.enabled|disabled` — including the fact that *reading* the audit log is itself audited, which the design must not hide.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-143/144 health and incidents, SCR-146 backups, onboarding wizard
body:
## Context
These are the operations screens: the ones the owner opens when something is wrong, plus the one destructive flow in the product that can undo the database (**restore**), plus the guided onboarding wizard that turns an eight-step delegation procedure into something repeatable.

The visual language for system health was established by **E04-D01** ("Design the system-health, incident-log and degraded-state surfaces"), which already covers SCR-143/SCR-144/SCR-147 as part of the observability baseline. This ticket **extends** that language into the admin area rather than re-inventing it, and adds the two surfaces E04 did not cover: SCR-146 backups & restore and the US-ADMIN-013 onboarding wizard.

The restore wizard's copy is a safety control: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-146 requires the impact preview to state "what a restore does and does not recover (market history is not restored from these backups)" and the sign-off explicitly requires that "restore impact copy reviewed by security".

## Scope / Deliverables
- Design pass for the E42-S08 statechart inspector screen (machine list, state diagram, event timeline, latch-acknowledge control), reusing this ticket's operations-screen visual language rather than a separate design track.
- Hi-fi for **SCR-143** system health and **SCR-144** incident log as admin-area applications of E04-D01's language (tiles with number + unit + state word, sparkline with table alternative, degraded and outage variants naming what stops working, link to the incident log, export diagnostics).
- Hi-fi for **SCR-146** backups & restore: the run table, backup-now with progress, verify, download-with-handling-warning, last-successful-backup age warning, failed-backup and failed-verification states, and the **restore wizard** as a stepper — choose backup → impact preview → typed confirm + step-up → progress → verification → summary.
- Hi-fi for the **manager onboarding wizard** (US-ADMIN-013, composing SCR-123 and SCR-017): the eight steps, the **blocked step** variant showing the exact 48-hour unlock time while the rest of the flow continues, the resume state with completed steps marked, and the secret-entry step with its "will not be shown again" statement.
- Hi-fi for the **trade-group governance** controls added to SCR-062 (enable/disable, who may use this group, reorder, version indicator) as an extension of E28's existing design, not a replacement.
- The **degraded-while-reporting-degradation** case drawn explicitly: SCR-143 when the health endpoint itself is unavailable — stale tiles with timestamps, shell and navigation still usable.
- Design-system contributions: CMP-178 SystemHealthTile (admin variants), CMP-210 HealthChips, CMP-023 Progress Bar in the wizard context, CMP-177 RecorderStatusRow reuse confirmation.

## Out of scope
- The Grafana dashboards (E04) — different audience, different medium.
- SCR-142 storage panel (E16/E07) and SCR-147 connectivity (E04/E46), linked to from SCR-143.
- The audit and flag screens (E42-D04).

## Acceptance criteria
- Every listed surface has hi-fi frames for every catalogue-listed state.
- Each screen's catalogue sign-off checklist ticked item by item, including SCR-146's "explicit statement of what a restore does and does not recover" and SCR-143's "the page works when the backend is partially down".
- The restore impact copy is reviewed and signed off by the Security engineer (blocking criterion, per the catalogue).
- The onboarding blocked-step variant shows the exact unlock time and demonstrably does not halt the flow.
- Every sparkline has its table alternative designed, not assumed.
- Continuity with E04-D01 demonstrated: a reviewer placing SCR-143 beside E04's designs sees one language, not two.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Done by end of Sprint 15, two sprints before the Sprint 17 builds (E42-S06, E42-S07).

## Technical notes / design
- Tiles are drawn as independently resolving units with their own status, matching the snapshot-plus-`system`-delta data model; no page-level spinner is drawn anywhere on SCR-143.
- The restore wizard's step 1 states the maintenance-mode precondition up front rather than failing at step 4, because the server enforces it as a `conflict`.
- The onboarding wizard's state is server-side and resumable across devices; the design reflects that ("continue on another device" is possible and shown), avoiding a local-draft metaphor the backend does not support.

## Test plan
- Validated in design QA (E42-D07) against the built screens, and in the chaos scenarios of E42-Q03 (the degraded-while-reporting case is both a design state and a test case).

## Security notes
- Restore and download are the two most dangerous controls in the epic: both are drawn with typed confirmation and step-up, and the download frame carries the secret-handling warning.
- The onboarding secret step must show that the secret is never redisplayed; the frame shows the fingerprint-and-status treatment for a revisited step.
- Health screens must not surface internal hostnames, connection strings or stack traces — the frames show only the fields the `HealthReport` schema exposes.

## Accessibility notes
- Each subsystem is a labelled row with a text status; no dot-colour reliance.
- The restore wizard and onboarding wizard are steppers with `aria-current="step"`; progress carries text percentages.
- Incident messages expand rather than truncate, so a screen reader can reach the full text.
- Reorder controls in trade-group governance are keyboard-operable buttons, not drag-only.
- Every figure carries units in its accessible name.

## Performance notes
- Frames annotate the ≤1 % added-load NFR for SCR-143 (one snapshot plus the existing `system` subscription, no polling), SCR-144's 10k-row 8 ms/frame budget, and the fact that backup/restore/verify are server jobs the browser only observes.

## Observability
Frames annotate `health.diagnostics_exported`, `incident.acknowledged`, `backup.run|verified|restore|downloaded|deleted` and the onboarding analytics events, including which are audited at high severity.

## Definition of Done

body:

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 is explicit that there is no internal-tool exemption: "a11y: default-on (WCAG 2.2 AA) for any ticket that ships or changes a UI surface, **including owner/admin screens** — there is no 'internal tool, a11y doesn't matter' exception, since owner/admin screens are inside the same web app and RBAC-gated, not absent of users with accessibility needs."

- Specific high-risk reviews: the impersonation banner (must be announced and must not be dismissible into invisibility), the integrity-failure alert (announced once, then persistent), the countdown (announced at thresholds, not every tick), and disabled-with-reason controls (`aria-describedby` text supplied by design, not invented by engineering).
- **Handoff pack** per screen: annotated redlines (spacing, type, tokens), component mapping to `15-component-catalogue.md` ids, state inventory, data-source annotations (endpoint / WS topic / schema field names), copy deck (every string, including error and empty-state copy), the a11y contract per interactive element, and the motion table.

- Design QA of the built screens (E42-D07) — this is the pre-build review; that is the post-build one.

- Reduced-motion alternatives specified for every transition.

- The keyboard paths documented here become the E2E keyboard tests in E42-Q02 and the manual screen-reader script in E42-Q05 — one list, three uses.

- The copy deck is reviewed for security accuracy: a confirmation dialog that understates a consequence is a security defect. The handoff pack carries each screen's performance budget so engineering treats it as a requirement rather than a footnote.

body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes design QA a Done gate for net-new UI: "built screen compared against design spec (spacing/tokens/type/color/states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer; discrepancies either fixed or filed as follow-up Bug with `priority/*` set."

The admin area is fifteen screens built by several engineers across two sprints from one shared pattern set. Drift is the expected failure mode — not gross deviation, but fifteen slightly different paddings, three variants of the same empty state, and a destructive dialog that quietly dropped its typed confirmation. ## Scope / Deliverables
- Screen-by-screen comparison of the built implementation against the signed-off hi-fi for: CMP-087 shell, SCR-149, SCR-120, SCR-121, SCR-122, SCR-123, SCR-124, SCR-135, SCR-136, SCR-143, SCR-144, SCR-145, SCR-146, SCR-148, SCR-154, the onboarding wizard and the SCR-062 governance controls.
- Per screen: spacing, type scale, token usage (no hard-coded colours), component fidelity to `15-component-catalogue.md`, and **every state** — not just the populated one. Empty, loading, filtered-to-nothing, error, degraded and destructive-confirmation states are where drift hides.
- **Pattern-conformance audit** against the E42-D06 pattern sheet: is every destructive action on the correct rung of the ladder? Is the degraded/stale expression identical across SCR-120, SCR-143 and SCR-144? Does every state-changing control announce that it will be recorded?
- **Copy audit** against the copy deck: every string matches, including error and empty-state copy; no engineer-authored placeholder survives.
- Motion conformance: durations, easings and reduced-motion behaviour match the motion spec.
- Cross-screen consistency sweep at both breakpoints (1280×800, 2560×1440) and in both themes if the admin area supports them.
- Discrepancy log with a disposition for each: fixed in-sprint, or filed as a Bug with `priority/*` and an owner. Nothing is left as "noted".

## Out of scope
- Functional testing (E42-Q02) and accessibility auditing (E42-Q05) — separate tickets with separate skills; this is visual and pattern conformance.
- Screens owned by other epics, even though they render inside the admin shell (E16, E27, E28, E39, E43) — each has its own design QA.
- Redesign. Findings that are design changes rather than implementation drift are filed as new design tickets, not smuggled in here.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every listed screen reviewed in every catalogue-listed state, with evidence (screenshots) attached.

- The copy audit confirms 100% match with the copy deck, or files the differences.
- Discrepancy log complete: each entry is fixed, or filed as a Bug with a priority and an owner; none are undispositioned.
- Design sign-off comment recorded on this ticket and on the epic — this is the design gate the epic's DoD requires.

## Technical notes / design
- Reviewed against a staging (demo) build at a pinned commit SHA, recorded on the ticket, so "fixed later" claims are verifiable.
- Token conformance is checked with the design-system linting where available, and by inspection where not — a hard-coded hex in the admin area is a finding, even if it matches the token's current value.

## Test plan
- Visual-regression snapshots for the admin screens are added or refreshed as part of the fixes, so the same drift cannot recur silently.
- Findings that indicate a missing test (a state nobody ever rendered) are cross-filed to E42-Q02.

## Security notes
- Security-relevant visual checks are part of the pass, not an afterthought: the impersonation banner is present and unmissable; the audit screens still contain no mutation affordance; `trading.live_enabled` still renders blocked; no screen displays a secret; typed confirmations were not downgraded to plain confirms during implementation.

## Accessibility notes
- Visual a11y conformance only (contrast, focus-visible treatment, text-not-colour status); the full audit is E42-Q05.
- Any contrast regression introduced during implementation is a finding here, with the measured value recorded.

## Performance notes
Findings that reveal a perf-driven design compromise (for example, a tile that was made page-blocking to simplify the code) are escalated rather than accepted, since SCR-120 and SCR-143 have explicit independence requirements.

## Observability
Confirms that the audit/analytics events named in the handoff pack are actually emitted by the built controls, by inspecting the events in the staging build.

- [ ] CDO (or delegate) sign-off comment recorded; ticket Status=Done ≥2 sprints before the consuming frontend story starts (design-ahead rule, `00-planning-brief.md`).

title: Write the black-box test plan and fixture set for the admin area
body:
## Context
`03-testing-strategy.md` and the Story DoR both require a black-box test plan before a story is Ready. The admin area has fourteen user stories whose acceptance criteria include timing guarantees (sessions revoked within 5 s, flags propagated within 10 s, orders blocked within 200 ms), cross-user effects (a change by the owner must be observed by a manager's session), and states that only appear when something is broken (integrity failure, degraded subsystems, failed backup verification).

None of those are testable without a deliberate fixture set. This ticket writes the plan and builds the fixtures **before** the Sprint 16 stories start, so engineering and QA are testing the same list of scenarios rather than discovering the gap at the end.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Black-box test plan and fixtures for E42-T07 (statechart inspector read API) and E42-S08 (inspector screen), including a seeded chain_trips-degraded machine fixture for the latch-acknowledge scenario.
- Black-box test plan in `docs/qa/e42-admin-test-plan.md` covering US-ADMIN-001..014 as they are implemented in this epic, structured per story group: shell & re-auth (S01), users (S02), bindings & view-as (S03), audit (S04), flags & maintenance (S05), health/incidents/backups (S06), onboarding & governance (S07).
- Every Gherkin scenario from the seven stories mapped to a test case, plus the negative and boundary cases the stories imply but do not spell out: expired token mid-action, concurrent owner edits, a manager session open while their grant is revoked, an export requested over a range that exceeds the limit, a flag changed twice in one second.
- **Cross-session scenarios** defined explicitly, since they need two browser contexts: owner disables a manager while that manager is trading; owner revokes a grant while the manager is subscribed; owner enables maintenance while a manager has the order ticket open.
- **Fixture set**: seeded users in every status (`invited`, `active`, `disabled`), grant sets covering none/one/many accounts, a 10 M-row audit dataset (sharing E42-K01's generator), a **corrupted-chain** fixture, degraded and outage health payloads, a failed-verification backup, flags in every kind (boolean/percentage/variant) including a blocked `trading.live_enabled`, and an account under the 48-hour key restriction.
- **Exploratory charters** (timeboxed, one per theme): "try to see data outside your scope as a manager", "try to make the audit log look editable", "try to reach an admin screen without elevation", "try to lose form content by letting the token expire", "try to make two tiles block each other".
- Entry/exit criteria per story group and the epic-level regression pack definition (which cases re-run every sprint thereafter).

## Out of scope
- Executing the plan (E42-Q02, Q03, Q05) and the automated suites themselves.
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — related but owned by Security; this plan references them rather than duplicating.
- Load testing of non-admin surfaces.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every Gherkin scenario across E42-S01..S07 maps to at least one numbered test case; the traceability table is part of the plan.
- Every fixture listed in Scope exists, is committed, is deterministic, and is documented with how to load it.
- The corrupted-chain fixture reproducibly makes `POST /admin/audit/verify` report the expected `first_bad_id`.
- Cross-session scenarios specify the exact timing assertion (≤5 s, ≤10 s, ≤2 s, ≤200 ms) taken from the user story or the catalogue, not invented.
- Exploratory charters are written with a timebox and a "what would make this a finding" statement each.
- Plan reviewed by the story owners and the Security engineer; sign-off recorded.

## Technical notes / design
- Fixtures are code (seed scripts), not database dumps, so they survive schema migrations; each seed is idempotent and asserts its own post-conditions.
- The 10 M-row audit dataset is generated, not stored — the generator is shared with E42-K01 so the perf spike and QA use identical data.
- Timing assertions use the server's audit timestamps where possible rather than wall-clock in the test runner, to avoid flakiness masquerading as a failure.

## Test plan
- The plan is itself reviewed against `03-testing-strategy.md`'s pyramid: each case is labelled with the layer that should own it (unit / contract / integration / E2E / perf / security / a11y), so E42-Q02 knows what to automate and what stays manual.

## Security notes
- Fixtures must contain **no** real credentials, real Bybit keys or real user data. The generator produces obviously-synthetic values, and a test asserts no fixture matches a secret pattern.
- The corrupted-chain fixture is deliberately a *test-only* artefact and must never be loadable against a non-test database; the loader refuses if the target is not a test database.

## Accessibility notes
- The plan includes the manual screen-reader script derived from E42-D06's keyboard paths, so the a11y audit (E42-Q05) executes a written procedure rather than improvising.

## Performance notes
- The plan states the measurable budgets per screen (SCR-120 ≤800 ms, SCR-135 ≤400 ms filter / ≤2 s first page at 10 M rows, SCR-136 ≤300 ms, SCR-143 ≤1 % added load) and which ticket measures each.

## Observability
- Each test case names the audit event it expects, so "the feature works" and "the feature is recorded" are verified together — the audit log is a product requirement here, not an implementation detail.
