title: Automate the admin E2E suite including cross-session and timing assertions
body:
## Context
The admin stories make promises that only a multi-context E2E test can verify: a manager's session dies within 5 s of being disabled; a flag change reaches every client within 10 s; a revoked grant force-closes a live subscription. Unit tests cannot see these, and manual testing cannot re-run them every sprint.

`03-testing-strategy.md` puts Playwright (web + Electron) at the top of the pyramid for exactly this. This ticket builds the admin suite from the plan written in E42-Q01.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Playwright specs under `tests/e2e/admin/`: `admin-shell.spec.ts`, `admin-users.spec.ts`, `admin-user-detail.spec.ts`, `admin-audit.spec.ts`, `admin-flags.spec.ts`, `admin-health.spec.ts`, `admin-backups.spec.ts`, `admin-onboarding.spec.ts`.
- **Cross-session harness**: a reusable helper that opens an owner context and a manager context against the same backend, so the effect of an owner action on a manager's live session is directly assertable. This is the piece the suite is worth building for.
- Timing assertions with the budgets from the stories: session revocation ≤5 s, flag propagation ≤10 s, maintenance broadcast ≤2 s, order blocking ≤200 ms (asserted via the API response, not the UI).
- Negative-path specs: manager hard-404 on every `/admin/*` route (parameterised over the full route list, so a newly added admin route without a guard fails the suite); stale-token deep link; 412 conflict on concurrent edit; export range rejection.
- Fixture wiring from E42-Q01, with per-spec seeding and teardown so specs are order-independent.
- CI integration: the suite runs on PRs touching `apps/web/src/features/admin` or `services/admin`, and nightly in full; flaky specs are quarantined with an owner rather than retried into green.
- Contract-test additions: schemathesis/Dredd runs over the `/admin/*` and `/users*` paths added by this epic.

## Out of scope
- Perf, load and chaos scenarios (E42-Q03).
- Accessibility audit (E42-Q05).
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — the RBAC assertion suite lives there; this suite asserts the user-visible half.
- Unit and component tests, which ship with their stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The suite proves cross-session effects
  Given an owner context and a manager context are both signed in
  When the owner disables the manager
  Then the manager's next request fails within 5 seconds
  And the assertion is on the observed time, not a fixed sleep

Scenario: Every admin route is guarded
  Given the suite enumerates the admin route list from the router
  When each route is visited by a manager
  Then every one renders the 404 surface
  And adding a new admin route without a guard fails this spec

Scenario: The suite is deterministic
  When the full admin suite runs 10 times in CI
  Then it passes 10 times with no retries
  And any spec that does not is quarantined with an owner and a ticket
```
- All specs listed in Scope exist and pass against staging (demo).
- Contract tests cover every `/admin/*` and `/users*` path added by this epic.
- CI wiring merged; the suite's runtime is under 10 minutes on the standard runner, or it is sharded.
- Traceability table posted mapping each E42-Q01 case to its automated spec (or to "manual, by design" with a reason).

## Technical notes / design
- No fixed `sleep`: timing assertions poll with a deadline and report the observed duration, so a passing test still tells you how close to the budget you are.
- The route list for the guard spec is imported from the application's router definition rather than hard-coded, which is what makes the "new route without a guard" case fail automatically.
- Each spec seeds its own data with a unique prefix and tears it down, so specs can run in parallel shards.
- The step-up gate is handled by a helper that performs a real TOTP computation against the seeded secret — never by disabling the gate for tests, which would make the suite prove nothing about the guard.

## Test plan
- The suite is its own deliverable; its quality bar is the determinism criterion above.
- Meta-test: a deliberately unguarded route added in a scratch branch must fail the guard spec — verified once and recorded, so the spec's value is demonstrated rather than assumed.

## Security notes
- Test credentials are seeded, obviously synthetic, and scoped to the test environment; the suite must never run against production (a guard asserts the target base URL is not the production host).
- The TOTP secret used in tests is generated per run, not committed.
- Specs that attempt privilege escalation belong to E42-X03; this suite asserts the legitimate paths and the visible denials.

## Accessibility notes
- Each spec includes an axe-core scan of the screens it visits, so an a11y regression fails the functional suite rather than waiting for the audit.
- The keyboard paths from E42-D06 are automated here as keyboard-only specs for the highest-risk flows (elevate, delete a user, run a restore).

## Performance notes
- The suite records the observed timings for the budgeted assertions and publishes them as CI artefacts, giving a trend rather than a pass/fail snapshot.

## Observability
- Specs assert the expected audit entries exist after each action, querying `GET /admin/audit` — so the suite verifies accountability, not just behaviour.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.
- [ ] Defects filed with repro steps, environment and `priority/*`; P0/P1 defects closed or explicitly accepted before sign-off.

- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

title: Run admin performance, load and chaos scenarios including degraded rendering
body:
## Context
Three of this epic's requirements are performance claims that will be believed unless measured: the audit log's **≤2 s first page over 10 million entries** (US-ADMIN-009), the health screen's **≤1 % added load** (US-ADMIN-011), and SCR-120's **≤800 ms render that never blocks on the slowest subsystem**.

One is a resilience claim: SCR-143 "must itself remain responsive when the system it is reporting on is degraded (all tiles resolve independently, no tile can block another)". That is precisely the property that quietly breaks during implementation, and precisely the moment it matters.

`06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `03-testing-strategy.md` require chaos/failover testing (WS disconnect, exchange 5xx, rate-limit 10018) as a first-class layer, not an afterthought.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Audit query performance**: k6 profile against the 10 M-row dataset measuring first-page latency for each filter combination the UI offers, at page 1 and at deep cursor positions; assert ≤2 s worst case and ≤400 ms for the common combinations; publish the distribution, not just the pass/fail.
- **Export under load**: concurrent export jobs plus interactive queries — the interactive path must not degrade beyond its budget while an export streams.
- **Overview and health render**: measure SCR-120's end-to-end render with all subsystems healthy and with one subsystem timing out; assert ≤800 ms in both cases and that the slow tile does not delay the others.
- **Added-load measurement**: quantify the health screen's server-side cost with the screen open versus closed, against the ≤1 % NFR, at the expected session count.
- **Chaos scenarios**:
  1. Health endpoint returns 503 while the `system` topic stays up → tiles render stale with timestamps; shell usable.
  2. WS disconnects mid-session on an admin screen → reconnect, resubscribe, no duplicated or lost incident rows.
  3. Postgres becomes slow (injected latency) → admin screens degrade with explicit stale markers rather than hanging.
  4. Audit chain break injected → the critical banner appears, the alert fires, and the screen offers no misleading retry.
  5. Backup verification fails → the age warning appears with the correct last-verified time.
  6. Flag store unreachable → flags resolve to defaults and the console says so, rather than showing stale values as current.
- Results recorded against budgets in a report under `docs/qa/` and fed into the epic's PRR evidence.

## Out of scope
- Trading-path load testing (E29/E34/E46) — different surfaces, different budgets.
- Fixing the defects found; those are filed as Bugs against the owning story.
- The chaos framework itself, if one exists from E45 — reused, not rebuilt.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Audit first page at scale
  Given 10 million audit entries
  When the first page is requested with each of the UI's filter combinations
  Then every combination returns within 2 seconds p95
  And the common combinations return within 400 ms p95
  And the full distribution is published

Scenario: One slow subsystem does not block the overview
  Given the recorder subsystem does not respond
  When the admin overview is opened
  Then it renders within 800 ms with the recorder tile in its error state
  And every other tile shows its value

Scenario: The health screen survives the outage it reports
  Given the health endpoint returns 503
  Then every tile shows its last-known value marked stale with a timestamp
  And the shell and navigation remain usable
  And no tile shows a plausible but stale number as if it were current

Scenario (failure): Chain break is unmistakable
  Given an injected audit chain break
  Then the critical banner names the break position
  And the cv_audit_chain_verified alert fires
  And no retry control implies the failure is transient

Scenario (edge): Flag store unreachable
  Then flags resolve to their defaults, safety-relevant defaults being the restrictive ones
  And the console states that values are defaults, not current
```
- All six chaos scenarios executed with results recorded; each either passes or has a filed Bug with a priority.
- Budget table published with measured values beside the required values.

## Technical notes / design
- Latency injection via a proxy/toxiproxy-style layer rather than code changes, so the system under test is the shipped build.
- The chain-break injection operates on a disposable test database only, with the loader refusing any non-test target.
- Measurements use server-side timings plus client RUM (`cv_admin_overview_render_ms`), so a fast server with a slow client is not mistaken for success.
- The ≤1 % added-load figure is measured as the delta in server CPU/request rate with N admin screens open versus none, at the expected session count — stated as a method, because the NFR is otherwise unfalsifiable.

## Test plan
- This ticket *is* the test execution; its own quality bar is reproducibility: a reviewer must be able to re-run `make admin-perf` and `make admin-chaos` and obtain the same conclusions.

## Security notes
- Chaos scenarios must not be runnable against production; the harness asserts its target environment.
- The injected chain break is a security-sensitive test artefact: its presence in any non-test environment would itself be an incident, so the fixture is clearly marked and the loader is guarded.
- Load testing the export endpoint doubles as a check that the export rate limit and range limit actually bound exfiltration.

## Accessibility notes
- The degraded and stale states exercised here are also a11y states: the audit confirms their announcements behave correctly under repeated transitions (no announcement storms when a subsystem flaps).

## Performance notes
- Budgets under test, all sourced from the plan docs: ≤2 s audit first page at 10 M rows and ≤400 ms common filter round-trip; SCR-120 ≤800 ms with and without a slow subsystem; SCR-136 ≤300 ms; SCR-143 ≤1 % added load and ≤2 ms scripting per frame; SCR-144 10k rows without exceeding 8 ms scripting per frame.

## Observability
- Verifies the alerting path end-to-end, not just the metric: `cv_audit_chain_verified == 0` must actually page, and `cv_backup_last_success_age_seconds` must fire at the configured threshold. A metric that exists but never alerts is a false sense of security.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.

- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

- `E42-T02` — the audit query endpoints and their index strategy.

title: Run exploratory charters and assemble the E42 regression pack with QA sign-off
body:
## Context
Scripted tests find what was anticipated. The admin area's most expensive failures would be the unanticipated ones: a path that leaks scope, a confirmation that can be bypassed by a keyboard shortcut, a form that loses twenty minutes of work on token expiry. `03-testing-strategy.md` therefore pairs the automated pyramid with timeboxed exploratory charters.

This ticket also assembles the **regression pack** — the subset that re-runs every sprint afterwards — and records the epic-level QA sign-off that `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 requires before the Epic can be Done ("an Epic-level regression/exploratory pass executed and recorded, not just child-ticket QA").

## Scope / Deliverables
- Exploratory charter and regression-pack entry for the E42-S08 statechart inspector screen, covering the latch-acknowledge step-up gate.
- Execute the exploratory charters defined in E42-Q01, each timeboxed to 90 minutes with a written session report:
  1. *Scope escape* — as a manager, try every route, deep link, API call and WS subscription to see data outside your grants.
  2. *Audit credibility* — try to make the audit log appear editable, incomplete, or reorderable; try to take an action that produces no entry.
  3. *Elevation bypass* — try to reach or act on an admin surface without a fresh token, including via back/forward navigation, a restored session, and a second tab.
  4. *Work loss* — try to lose form content: token expiry mid-edit, concurrent edit, navigation, reload, network drop.
  5. *Tile interference* — try to make one slow or failing tile degrade another on SCR-120 and SCR-143.
  6. *Destructive-action pressure* — try to complete a destructive action faster than the confirmation intends (double-submit, Enter-key, browser autofill of the typed confirmation).
- File every finding as a Bug with repro steps, environment, build SHA and a priority.
- **Regression pack**: select the subset of cases (automated + manual) that must re-run every sprint for the rest of the project — the RBAC denials, the audit-integrity path, the session-revocation timing, the destructive confirmations, and the flag/maintenance propagation. Document it and wire the automated portion into the nightly run.
- **Epic QA sign-off**: execute the pack against a release candidate build, record pass/fail per case, and post the sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
- Automation of newly found gaps (filed as follow-up tickets against E42-Q02 or the owning story).
- Security abuse cases (E42-X03) — charter 1 and 3 overlap deliberately; findings are cross-referenced, and the Security ticket owns the formal verdict.
- Accessibility audit (E42-Q05).

## Acceptance criteria
- All six charters executed with a written session report each (what was tried, what was found, what was not covered).
- Every finding filed as a Bug with repro steps and a priority; P0/P1 findings are closed or explicitly accepted with Owner sign-off before the epic closes.
- The regression pack is documented, its automated portion runs nightly, and its manual portion has an owner and an execution cadence.
- The epic-level QA sign-off comment is posted with pass/fail per case against a named build SHA.
- Charter 2's outcome is explicit: either "no way was found to make the audit log appear mutable or incomplete", or findings that block the epic.

## Technical notes / design
- Charters are session-based: a stated mission, a timebox, notes taken during rather than after, and an explicit list of what the session did **not** cover — that list is how the next session avoids re-treading.
- Findings are reproduced once before filing, so the Bug carries deterministic steps rather than a narrative.

## Test plan
- Each finding that reveals a missing automated case produces a follow-up ticket naming the pyramid layer that should have caught it (the Bug DoR requirement in `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §6.1).

## Security notes
- Charters 1, 2, 3 and 6 are security-relevant; findings are shared with the Security engineer immediately rather than at the end of the ticket, and any privilege-escalation or scope-leak finding is treated as P0 regardless of its apparent exploitability.
- Exploration is performed against staging (demo) with synthetic data only.

## Accessibility notes
- Charter 6 explicitly includes keyboard-driven bypass attempts (Enter-key submission, focus order permitting a destructive action before the warning is read), which is both a security and an accessibility concern.

## Performance notes
- Charter 5 is the exploratory counterpart to E42-Q03's measured tile-independence scenario; findings here often explain measurements there.

## Observability
- Charter 2 verifies that every action taken during exploration produced its expected audit entry — in practice the most effective way to find an unaudited mutation path.

title: Run the WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility audit across every admin screen
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 forbids the "internal tool" exemption explicitly for admin screens, and `05-accessibility-standard.md` sets WCAG 2.2 AA plus axe-core in CI plus **manual screen-reader passes** as the standard. axe-core catches perhaps a third of real barriers; the rest — focus management after a dialog, announcement of an alert that appears without user action, a countdown that spams a screen reader, a status conveyed only by position — need a person.

This audit covers fifteen screens with several patterns that are genuinely hard: an interrupting re-auth overlay, a persistent impersonation banner, a live-updating health grid, a long audit table with expandable diffs, and two multi-step wizards.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Automated: axe-core runs on every admin route in every major state (loading, populated, empty, error, degraded, dialog-open), wired into CI so a regression fails a PR.
- Manual screen-reader passes with **two** screen readers (NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on macOS at minimum) executing the written script from E42-D06, covering: elevate into admin; invite, disable and delete a user; bind and unbind an account with open positions; start and exit view-as; browse, expand and export the audit log; toggle a flag; enter and exit maintenance mode; run a restore; complete the onboarding wizard.
- Keyboard-only pass of the same flows: no mouse, verifying focus order, focus visibility, focus return after dialogs and drawers, no keyboard traps, and that no destructive action is reachable before its warning is read.
- Specific high-risk checks: the re-auth gate's `alertdialog` semantics and assertive failure announcement; the countdown announcing at thresholds rather than every tick; the impersonation banner announced and not silently dismissible; the integrity-failure alert announced once then persistent; live health updates not producing announcement storms; every status word-not-colour verified in greyscale; sparklines' table alternatives reachable; typed-confirmation fields labelled with their expected value stated in text.
- Contrast verification of the shipped build (not the design) for the admin tint and every state treatment.
- Zoom/reflow at 200% and 400% per WCAG 2.2, and target-size checks on the dense tables.
- Findings filed with the WCAG success criterion, severity and a remediation suggestion; report published under `docs/qa/`.

## Out of scope
- Fixing the findings (filed against the owning stories).
- The design-side a11y review (E42-D06) — done pre-build.
- Screens owned by other epics rendering inside the admin shell (E16, E27, E28, E39, E43), which have their own audits; the **shell itself** is in scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Automated checks are clean and enforced
  When axe-core runs on every admin route in every major state
  Then there are no violations at serious or critical level
  And the check is wired into CI so a regression fails the PR

Scenario: Screen-reader operability
  Given a screen-reader user follows the written script with two screen readers
  Then every flow can be completed without sighted assistance
  And every status, severity and outcome is conveyed as text

Scenario: The re-auth interruption is announced and recoverable
  Given the gate appears while I am editing a form
  Then it is announced as an alertdialog stating why and for how long
  And focus moves into it and returns to my form afterwards
  And my form content is intact

Scenario (failure): Announcement storm
  Given twelve health tiles update every second
  Then the screen reader is not flooded; updates are announced politely and coalesced

Scenario (edge): 400% zoom
  Then every admin screen reflows without horizontal scrolling and without content loss
```
- All findings filed with their WCAG criterion; no serious/critical finding is left unowned.
- The audit report is published and the epic's a11y DoD item is satisfiable from it.

## Technical notes / design
- axe-core runs against real application states driven by the Playwright suite, not against static Storybook snapshots alone — the states that fail are usually the ones only reachable through interaction.
- Announcement behaviour is verified by recording the screen-reader speech output for the high-risk flows, so a regression can be compared against a baseline rather than re-argued.
- Contrast is measured on the rendered build with a colour picker, because token values and shipped values can diverge.

## Test plan
- The manual script is versioned; each audit run records the script version and the build SHA, so results are comparable over time.
- Findings become regression cases in E42-Q04's pack where they are automatable.

## Security notes
- One overlap worth naming: a control that is disabled for RBAC reasons must expose its reason accessibly, **and** must still be enforced server-side. The audit verifies the first; E42-X03 verifies the second. Neither substitutes for the other.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket is the accessibility work; its scope is the full WCAG 2.2 AA criteria set as applied in `05-accessibility-standard.md`, not a spot check.
- Both automated and manual layers are required; passing axe alone does not satisfy this ticket.

## Performance notes
- Verifies that live-updating surfaces do not create announcement storms — an accessibility failure caused by an update cadence, which is where a11y and performance meet.

## Observability
Findings are categorised by pattern (dialogs, tables, live regions, wizards) so recurring causes are fixed in the design system rather than per screen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test artefacts committed under `tests/` (or `docs/qa/` for plans) and runnable in CI.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario in the covered stories mapped to at least one executed case; traceability table posted on the ticket.

- [ ] Flaky tests quarantined with an owner and a follow-up ticket rather than silently retried.

title: Verify deferred ADMIN Musts are owned by E43/E44 and no enable path ships
body:
## Context
The DoR review found that two ADMIN-domain **Must** stories are not built by E42: **US-ADMIN-010** Security posture panel (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26, SCR-137) and **US-ADMIN-012** Live-trading enablement gate (§26, SCR-137 + SCR-145). Both are deferred by design — US-ADMIN-010 to **E43** (`E43-D01`, `E43-S02`) and US-ADMIN-012 to **E44** (`E44-T04`, `E44-S01`, with the attestation half in `E43-S01`) — because neither can be honestly built before the R4 hardening and environment-separation work exists to back them.

A deferral is only safe if two things stay true: the downstream epic really does own the story to closure, and the deferring epic really does ship **no** partial or back-door implementation in the meantime. Both decay silently. Backlogs get re-scoped; a "temporarily disabled" toggle becomes an enabled one during a refactor. The most consequential switch in the product — live trading with real money — is exactly the wrong place to rely on a planning-document assertion.

This ticket turns the deferral into a check: an automated assertion that E42 contains no enable path, plus a recorded backlog verification before E42 closes. It is QA work, carries no product scope, and is deliberately **not** an engineering (S/T/K) ticket so it does not consume the 34-point engineering budget.

Refs: `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` §26 (US-ADMIN-007, US-ADMIN-010, US-ADMIN-012) · `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-137, SCR-145 · `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 · `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §2.2 (epic-level exit) · `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §3, §11.1.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Automated no-enable-path suite** (`tests/e2e/admin/deferred-must.spec.ts`), run in CI with the rest of the E42 pack:
  - As owner with a fresh admin token, `PUT /api/v1/admin/feature-flags/trading.live_enabled {enabled: true}` returns `403 gate_not_available` (or `validation_failed`/`gate_evidence_required` per `E42-T03`) — never `200` — with and without `reason`/`evidence_url`.
  - SCR-145 renders the `trading.live_enabled` row **disabled**, with its blocking reason visible and a link to SCR-137; the row exposes no control that can reach an enabled state by click, keyboard, or form submission.
  - `/admin/security` renders the placeholder registered by `E42-S01` — the R4 notice and nothing that claims a posture verdict.
  - A source-level assertion (Semgrep rule, contributed to `E42-X03`'s ruleset) that no E42-owned module writes `trading.live_enabled = true` and no admin component renders a posture pass/fail verdict.
- **Backlog verification record** (`docs/plan/backlog/verification/E42-deferred-must.md`), produced at epic close, stating for each of US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012: the owning epic, the owning ticket keys, their sprint and milestone, and confirmation that `18-traceability-matrix.md` §2.26 points at those epics.
- **Traceability reconciliation**: confirm rows US-ADMIN-010 and US-ADMIN-012 in `18-traceability-matrix.md` name E43/E44 (raise a docs PR if they still name E42), and that SCR-137 is listed under E43's screen set.
- Hand the record to `E42-Q04` so it is part of the epic QA sign-off packet.

## Out of scope
- Building, designing or testing the security posture panel or the live gate themselves — E43-S02, E43-Q01, E44-S01, E44-Q01.
- Judging whether E43/E44 are well specified — only that they exist, are scheduled and own the two stories.
- Any change to E42 product behaviour; if the suite fails, the fix lands on the owning story (`E42-S01`, `E42-S05`, `E42-T03`).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The live-trading flag cannot be enabled from anywhere in E42
  Given an owner with a valid session and an admin token less than 15 minutes old
  When the API is called to set trading.live_enabled to true, with and without a reason and evidence_url
  Then every call is rejected with a documented error code and no flag value changes
  And an audit entry is written for each attempt

Scenario: The deferred surfaces are visibly deferred, not half-built
  Given the owner opens SCR-145 and the /admin/security route
  Then the trading.live_enabled row is disabled with its blocking reason and a link to SCR-137
  And /admin/security shows only the R4 placeholder with no posture verdict
  And a screen reader announces the flag row as disabled with its reason, not merely as unavailable

Scenario: The downstream owners are verified before E42 closes
  Given the E43 and E44 backlogs
  When the verification record is produced
  Then US-ADMIN-010 is traced to E43-D01 and E43-S02 and US-ADMIN-012 to E44-T04 and E44-S01 with E43-S01
  And each named ticket has a sprint in the R4 window and milestone "R4 Live enablement"
  And the record is attached to the E42 QA sign-off

Scenario (failure): A downstream owner has disappeared or been descoped
  Given a re-scope has removed US-ADMIN-012 from E44 without reassigning it
  When the verification runs
  Then the check fails, E42 cannot be signed off, and the gap is escalated to the Owner as an R4 Must-coverage risk

Scenario (edge): A regression re-introduces an enable path after E42 closes
  Given a later change adds a writable control for trading.live_enabled outside E44
  When the E42 regression pack runs in CI
  Then the suite fails with the offending route or component named
```

## Technical notes / design
- The API assertions run against the seeded staging (demo) stack used by `E42-Q02`, reusing its owner and manager fixtures and its fresh-admin-token helper; no new harness.
- The UI assertions are Playwright, asserting `aria-disabled="true"` plus the presence of the `data-blocking-reason` attribute specified by `E42-S05`, rather than asserting pixels.
- The Semgrep rule is written as a deny-list pattern over `packages/web/src/features/admin/**` and `services/api/app/modules/admin/**`: any literal `trading.live_enabled` in a write position outside the E44-owned module is a finding. It ships into the ruleset maintained by `E42-X03` so it keeps running after this epic.

title: STRIDE threat model for the admin area, with abuse cases
body:
## Context
`00-planning-brief.md` and `04-security-program.md` require a STRIDE threat model per epic, and `30-release-roadmap.md` §7 names E42 explicitly in the R3 security gate: "STRIDE for E27, E29, E34, E35, E39, E42 — all Critical/High closed; a targeted abuse-case review of key handling and privilege escalation before the train closes."

E42 deserves the attention. It is the epic that concentrates privilege: user creation, role assignment, account binding, impersonation, feature flags, maintenance mode, backup restore, and the read side of the audit log. A defect here is not a bug in a screen — it is a path to controlling the installation.

This ticket runs the model **before** implementation (Sprint 14, two sprints before the build), so its findings shape the design rather than generating rework.

## Scope / Deliverables
- STRIDE decomposition of the admin area's trust boundaries: browser ↔ admin API, admin API ↔ Postgres (including the append-only grant boundary), admin API ↔ subsystem services (recorder, health, flags, backups), admin API ↔ key vault, and the elevation boundary between an authenticated session and an elevated admin session.
- Per-category analysis with concrete threats, not categories-as-checkboxes:
  - **Spoofing**: invite-link replay; TOTP replay against the re-auth gate; session fixation on elevation.
  - **Tampering**: audit-row mutation (defended by grants + trigger — verify both); flag values altered out-of-band; grant sets forged client-side; backup artefact substitution before restore.
  - **Repudiation**: an admin action producing no audit entry; an audit entry missing actor attribution; chain forking under concurrent writes.
  - **Information disclosure**: admin route existence leaking to non-owners; audit diffs leaking secrets; health screen leaking internal topology; backup download leaking key material; view-as leaking without a record.
  - **Denial of service**: removing the last owner; maintenance mode abused to halt trading; audit export used as a resource-exhaustion primitive; flag change disabling a needed control.
  - **Elevation of privilege**: reaching admin routes without elevation; a flag weakening a security control; view-as becoming writable; grant self-assignment; role escalation via a concurrent write race.
- **Abuse cases** written as executable scenarios (handed to E42-X03 for automation), each with a preconditions/steps/expected-denial shape.
- Data-classification map for the epic: which endpoint returns PII, Confidential or Secret-adjacent data, and what control protects each.
- Risk register update (`32-risk-register.md`) for anything new.
- Findings recorded with severity and disposition; Critical/High findings get remediation tickets that must be Done before the epic closes.

## Out of scope
- Executing the abuse cases (E42-X03) and the security review of the built code (E42-X02).
- The pen-test itself (E43) — this model is an input to it.
- Threat models for adjacent epics (E27 keys, E39 risk, E09 auth), referenced rather than repeated.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every STRIDE category has at least one concrete, specific threat analysed for each trust boundary; "not applicable" is argued, never left blank.
- Each threat has: likelihood, impact, existing control, residual risk, and disposition (accepted / mitigated by an existing control / requires a new ticket).
- Every Critical and High finding has a linked remediation ticket scheduled inside the R3 train.
- The abuse-case list is complete enough for E42-X03 to automate without further analysis.
- The data-classification map covers every endpoint this epic adds.
- `32-risk-register.md` updated.
- Security engineer and Architect review comments recorded; model published under `docs/security/threat-models/e42-admin.md`.

## Technical notes / design
- The model is built against the actual interfaces — the OpenAPI paths, the WS `system` topic, the Postgres grant model and the flag registry — rather than against a generic architecture diagram, so its findings are testable.
- Two structural controls get particular scrutiny because the rest of the epic leans on them: (1) the append-only enforcement (`REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE` **plus** the `forbid_mutation` trigger — belt and braces, verified independently), and (2) the flag registry's compile-time rejection of security-gating flags.

## Test plan
- Every threat with a "mitigated by an existing control" disposition names the test that proves the control works; if no such test exists, creating it is part of the disposition.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security work. Its own quality bar: a reader unfamiliar with the epic can follow the model to understand what could go wrong and why it cannot.
- Classification of the epic's data: **PII** (usernames, emails, actor IPs), **Confidential** (grants, limits, operational state, audit contents), **Secret-adjacent** (backup artefacts containing envelope-encrypted key material; never decrypted in this epic).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — analysis ticket. (Though one finding class is shared: a control disabled only visually is both an a11y and a security defect.)

## Performance notes
Denial-of-service analysis covers the audit export and query paths, feeding the range limits and rate limits implemented in E42-T02 and measured in E42-Q03.

## Observability
- The model specifies which threats are **detectable** and by what signal: `cv_audit_chain_verified`, denied-request counters, `admin.access_denied` audit entries, elevation failures. A threat with no detection signal is itself a finding.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact, and disposition (fixed / mitigated / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- [ ] Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- [ ] Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Dependencies
- `E42-D02` — the wireframes define the actual surfaces and affordances being modelled; modelling against the catalogue alone would miss resolved design decisions.

title: Security review: RBAC, elevation, audit and destructive admin paths
body:
## Context
The threat model (E42-X01) says what should be true. This ticket verifies it against the code that shipped, before the epic closes and before E43's hardening and pen-test build on top of it.

`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §8 makes this non-optional: any ticket touching RBAC, API-key handling, admin screens or order-placement paths is "always treated as `security`-labelled for DoD purposes, whether or not the label was applied at creation — reviewers must add the label and block Done if missing." This epic touches three of those four.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **White-box review** of the admin implementation against the threat model:
  - Every `/admin/*` and `/users*` route: permission declared, deny-by-default, step-up where required, audit emitted on both success and denial. Reviewed as a table, route by route, with no route unexamined.
  - The elevation model: token TTL server-issued and non-extendable by the client; elevation bound to the session; the router-404 / API-403 non-disclosure split actually implemented.
  - The audit read side: no mutation path exists; manager scoping is in the repository layer; export is signed, range-limited and rate-limited; redaction is applied at write time and preserved on export.
  - Append-only enforcement verified **independently of the application**: as `cv_app`, attempt UPDATE and DELETE on `audit_log` and confirm both the grant and the trigger refuse.
  - The flag registry: confirm the compile-time rejection of security-gating categories actually fails startup, and that no auth/RBAC/audit module reads a flag (the Semgrep rule from E42-X03 is verified, not just merged).
  - The user lifecycle: last-owner protection under concurrency (reviewed as a locking argument, not just a test); anonymisation irreversibility; grant-change propagation to live WS subscriptions (the `grants_changed` push and the `revoked` frame; R7 on #965 dropped `grants_version`).
  - Destructive paths: restore preconditions enforced server-side; backup download URL short-lived and single-use; maintenance mode step-up gated and fail-closed.
- **Copy review** of the security-relevant confirmations, as required by SCR-146's sign-off ("restore impact copy reviewed by security") and extended here to delete, unbind, purge and flag-change copy — understated consequences are findings.
- SAST/SCA results for the epic's code triaged; false positives annotated with a reason, not suppressed silently.
- Findings filed with severity; Critical/High must be closed before the epic is Done.
- Security sign-off comment on the epic.

## Out of scope
- The pen-test (E43) — this review is an input, and deliberately precedes it so the pen-testers spend their time on what a review cannot find.
- Automating the abuse cases (E42-X03).
- Remediation implementation, which lands on the owning story branches.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every admin route is accounted for
  When the review enumerates every /admin/* and /users* route
  Then each has a declared permission, deny-by-default behaviour, and an audit entry on success and on denial
  And any route missing one is a finding

Scenario: The audit log is immutable in practice, not just in intent
  Given a direct database connection as the application role
  When UPDATE and DELETE are attempted on audit_log
  Then both fail, once on grants and once on the trigger
  And the attempt is itself recorded

Scenario: No flag can weaken a security control
  Given a flag definition declaring an auth-gating category
  When the service starts
  Then startup fails
  And no auth, RBAC or audit module contains a flag lookup

Scenario: Elevation cannot be extended by the client
  When a client attempts to extend or forge the admin token TTL
  Then the server rejects it and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): A destructive path missing a precondition
  Given restore is called with maintenance mode off
  Then the service refuses regardless of what the UI sent
```
- All Critical/High findings closed or accepted with Owner sign-off before the epic closes.
- Security sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Technical notes / design
- The route table is generated from the application's router at review time rather than written by hand, so a route cannot be omitted from the review by oversight.
- The append-only check runs as a real database session with the application role, because reasoning about grants is not the same as exercising them.
- Concurrency arguments (last-owner, chain forking) are reviewed as locking proofs plus the stress tests from E42-T04 (a disable racing a demotion) and E42-T09 (parallel cross-demotions) — either alone is insufficient.

## Test plan
- Every finding produces a regression test at the appropriate layer before it is closed, so the same defect cannot return silently.
- Review conclusions that depend on a control being tested reference the specific test id.

## Security notes
- This ticket *is* the security review. Its scope is the epic's full attack surface as enumerated in E42-X01.
- Particular attention to the three controls the rest of the product trusts: the audit chain's immutability, the RBAC grant boundary between managers, and the flag registry's inability to gate security.

## Accessibility notes
- One cross-cutting check: controls that are disabled for RBAC reasons must be enforced server-side, not merely rendered disabled. A UI-only restriction is a finding here even though it looks like an accessibility nicety.

## Performance notes
Reviews the export range limit and rate limit as DoS controls, cross-checking the measured behaviour from E42-Q03.

## Observability
- Verifies that denials are observable: `admin.access_denied` entries, denied-request counters and elevation-failure metrics must exist and fire, since an undetectable denial is an undetectable attack.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact, and disposition (fixed / mitigated / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- [ ] Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- [ ] Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

title: Automate admin abuse cases, RBAC assertions and SAST/DAST rules
body:
## Context
A threat model and a security review are point-in-time artefacts. The controls they verify must keep holding through every later change — and E42's controls are exactly the ones E43, E44 and E49 will be editing around.

`00-planning-brief.md` mandates SAST (CodeQL/Semgrep/Bandit) and DAST (OWASP ZAP) as required checks. `21-database-schema.md` §3.10.1 already assumes a Semgrep rule exists for audit coverage: the list of actions that MUST be audited is described as "enforced by a Semgrep rule on the service layer". This ticket makes that real for the admin surface and turns the threat model's abuse cases into a permanently running suite.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **RBAC assertion suite**: parameterised tests over every `/admin/*` and `/users*` route × every role (owner, manager, viewer, unauthenticated) × elevation state (fresh, stale, none), asserting the expected status **and** the expected audit entry. The route list is enumerated from the router, so a newly added admin route without a guard fails the suite rather than slipping through.
- **Abuse-case automation** from E42-X01: invite-link replay; TOTP replay; grant self-assignment; role escalation under concurrent writes; last-owner removal; audit mutation attempts (API and direct database); export range and rate abuse; view-as attempting a mutation; flag write without step-up; restore without maintenance mode; backup download URL reuse after expiry.
- **Semgrep rules** (committed to the repo's rule set):
  1. Every admin service mutation function is wrapped by the audit decorator — a mutation without it fails CI.
  2. No flag lookup inside `auth`, `rbac` or `audit` modules.
  3. No route under the admin router lacking an explicit permission declaration.
  4. No logging statement that can receive an invite link, a backup download URL, an API secret or a TOTP code.
- **ZAP (DAST)** profile covering the admin surface against staging: authenticated scans as manager and as viewer, asserting no admin endpoint is reachable; plus the standard injection/headers/CSP checks for the admin routes.
- CI wiring: the RBAC suite and Semgrep rules run on every PR touching admin code; ZAP runs nightly against staging.

## Out of scope
- The threat model (E42-X01) and the manual review (E42-X02).
- Fixing findings, which land on the owning stories.
- Repo-wide SAST/DAST baseline configuration (E03/E43) — this ticket adds admin-specific rules to it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The RBAC matrix is exhaustive and self-maintaining
  Given the route list is enumerated from the application router
  When the suite runs
  Then every route is asserted for every role and elevation state
  And adding an admin route without a permission declaration fails the suite

Scenario: Audit coverage is enforced by a rule, not by discipline
  Given an admin mutation function without the audit decorator
  When Semgrep runs in CI
  Then the build fails naming the function

Scenario: Abuse cases are permanently asserted
  When the abuse-case suite runs
  Then every case from the threat model is exercised
  And each is denied with the expected status and produces the expected audit entry

Scenario (failure): A secret reaches a log statement
  Given code that logs a value derived from an invite link or a backup download URL
  Then Semgrep fails the build

Scenario (edge): ZAP authenticated as a manager
  Then no /admin/* endpoint returns anything other than 403
  And every attempt appears in the audit log
```
- All suites and rules merged and running in CI with the stated triggers.
- A deliberately-broken branch demonstrates each rule firing (recorded once, so the rules' value is proven rather than assumed).

## Technical notes / design
- The RBAC suite asserts on the audit entry as well as the status code, because a silent 403 is only half a control — the roadmap's rule is "Non-owners receive 404 from the router and 403 from the API; **every admin action is audited**".
- Semgrep rules are written with test cases (positive and negative) in the rule directory, so a rule that stops matching after a refactor is itself caught.
- The ZAP profile uses authenticated sessions for manager and viewer roles; an unauthenticated-only scan would miss the entire privilege-escalation surface.
- The concurrency abuse cases (role escalation, last-owner removal) run N parallel attempts and assert exactly one success — a single-threaded test would pass against broken code.

## Test plan
- Meta-testing is part of the deliverable: each Semgrep rule ships with a failing fixture, and the RBAC suite is demonstrated to fail against an unguarded route.

## Security notes
- This ticket converts one-time assurance into continuous assurance; its value is entirely in the rules being **enforcing** (build-failing) rather than advisory.
- Test credentials are synthetic and environment-scoped; the suite refuses to run against a production base URL.
- Findings from the automated suites are triaged like any security finding: severity, disposition, remediation ticket.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — automated security tooling.

## Performance notes
- The RBAC suite is parameterised over many combinations; it is sharded and runs in under 5 minutes, because a slow security gate gets bypassed.

## Observability
- Asserts the observability of denials: every denied request must produce both an audit entry and a metric increment. The suite fails if a denial is silent.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Findings recorded with STRIDE category, likelihood/impact, and disposition (fixed / mitigated / accepted-risk with Owner sign-off).
- [ ] Every Critical/High finding has a linked remediation ticket that is Done before the epic closes.
- [ ] Controls traced to `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` requirement ids.
- [ ] Automated checks (Semgrep rules, ZAP rules, RBAC assertion tests) merged and running in CI, not just documented.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off comment posted on this ticket and on the epic.

## Dependencies
- `E42-X01` — supplies the abuse cases to automate.
- `E42-T04` — the lifecycle contract (slice S1), the disable cascade and last-owner protection on disable. The grant (E42-T08) and role-change (E42-T09) routes that the grant self-assignment and concurrent role-escalation cases exercise moved out of E42-T04 in the R2 split on #965 and sit in Sprint 19. They are not in `blocked_by` because this Task is in Sprint 16 (adding them fails SPRINT-ORDER), so those cases cannot pass before they land. The re-point and re-sprint decision is item 4 of #2710.

## Branch
`chore/admin-screens-security-automation` — 2 PRs: (1) RBAC + abuse-case suites, (2) Semgrep rules + ZAP profile.

title: Statechart inspector read API: machines, config, chain_trips, dropped_receipts, deferred depth, Stately export
body:
## Context
Every catalogue lifecycle is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` (ADR-0016 Accepted). A restored machine with `chain_trips > 0` is admitted degraded and stays latched until an operator acknowledges it in the admin inspector (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4, the `chain_trips` latch note). This task is the read API that inspector needs: it never queries a live `Interpreter` on the hot path (MUSTNOT-03) - it reads the `CvAuditPlugin` write-ahead `machine_events` table and the persisted snapshot, both landed by `E50-T60`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `GET /admin/statecharts` - list live machines by kind (`machine_key`), current published state/enum, `machine_hash`, and `chain_trips`/`dropped_receipts`/deferred-depth counters, sourced from the persisted snapshot and the `CvMetricsPlugin` `cv_machine_*` gauges (E50-T60), never from a live interpreter call.
- `GET /admin/statecharts/{machine_key}` - context summary (redacted per the same rules as the WS topic in `E17-T08`), full config, and current configuration path.
- `GET /admin/statecharts/{machine_key}/export` - the Stately-compatible JSON export for the chart registered under that `machine_hash` (from `statechart/registry.py`), so the admin screen can render the same diagram Stately would.
- Per-entity RBAC identical in shape to `E17-T08`'s topic authorisation (owner/account scope), reusing the same permission check rather than a bespoke one.

## Out of scope
- The latch-acknowledge write path and the inspector UI itself - **E42-S08**.
- The live-update WS topic - **E17-T08**; this is the point-in-time/list read model.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: List live machines
  Given several B1-B20 machines are running
  When I call GET /admin/statecharts
  Then I see one row per machine with kind, state, machine_hash, chain_trips and dropped_receipts

Scenario: No hot-path interpreter query
  Given the read API serves a request
  Then it is answered from the persisted snapshot and machine_events, with no call into a live Interpreter instance

Scenario: Stately export matches the registered chart
  Given a machine_hash registered in statechart/registry.py
  When I call the export endpoint
  Then the returned JSON round-trips through the same Stately schema used to author the chart
```

This is a pure read model over `CvAuditPlugin`'s write-ahead `machine_events` rows plus the quiescent snapshot store (`statechart/persistence.py`); it does not import `xstate_statemachine` directly (`CV-LINT-IMPORT` applies) and does not hold or construct an `Interpreter`. Built directly on the library via the factory/registry/plugin surface: no hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

## Test plan

## Security notes
Context summaries are redacted the same way as the `E17-T08` topic payloads; the export endpoint reveals chart structure only, never live secrets/context values.

## Performance notes
Read-model only; no interpreter construction cost on the request path.

Reuses `cv_machine_*` families from `E50-T60`.

Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2; `tests/xstate_contract` gate green.

title: Build the admin statechart inspector screen: machine list, state diagram, event timeline, latch acknowledge
body:
## Context
Every catalogue lifecycle is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` (ADR-0016 Accepted). Operators need one screen to see it: which machines are running, what state each is in, its transition history, and - critically - the place to acknowledge a `chain_trips`-latched machine so it can rejoin the order path (`29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4, the `chain_trips` latch note).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Machine list view sourced from `E42-T07`'s `GET /admin/statecharts`: kind, current state, `machine_hash`, `chain_trips`, `dropped_receipts`, deferred depth; degraded rows (`chain_trips > 0`) visually distinct and filterable.
- State diagram rendered from the Stately-compatible JSON export (`E42-T07` export endpoint), with the current state highlighted.
- Event timeline from `machine_events` (the `CvAuditPlugin` write-ahead audit trail, E50-T60): transitions, guard refusals, dropped-receipt events, in chronological order per machine.
- **Latch-acknowledge action**: an operator control that clears a `chain_trips` latch, gated by step-up re-auth (`E09-S04`'s elevation, action class `killswitch`-equivalent severity) and written to the audit trail with actor, machine, and prior `chain_trips` count.

## Out of scope
- The read API itself and RBAC on it - **E42-T07**.
- Any change to how `chain_trips` is incremented or to the degraded-admission behaviour - that is the B-chart/gateway logic (`statechart/gateway.py`), not this screen.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: See a degraded machine
  Given a machine restored with chain_trips > 0
  When I open the inspector
  Then it is listed as degraded with its chain_trips and dropped_receipts counts visible

Scenario: Acknowledge a latch
  Given I am viewing a degraded machine
  When I acknowledge it with step-up re-auth
  Then the latch clears, the machine resumes serving order-path commands, and the acknowledgement is audited with my identity

Scenario: Acknowledge without elevation is refused
  Given I have not completed step-up recently
  When I attempt to acknowledge a latch
  Then the server refuses it and I am prompted for step-up

Scenario: State diagram matches the running chart
  Given a machine of a given machine_hash
  When I view its diagram
  Then it matches the Stately export for that hash and highlights the current state
```

## Technical notes / design
The screen consumes `E42-T07`'s read API for the list/detail/export and `E17-T08`'s `machines.{entity}.state` topic for live updates while the screen is open; it never opens a bespoke polling loop against the interpreter. The acknowledge action calls a dedicated admin write route (paired with `E42-T07`) that is itself gated by the E09-S04 step-up elevation and goes through `statechart/gateway.py` (`cv_re_mint`-style payload-only wrapper, CV-C68 containment) rather than touching the interpreter directly. Built directly on the library via the factory/registry/plugin/gateway surface: no hand-rolled state machine, no enum+transition table, no shim, no dual-runtime.

## Test plan
Unit: degraded-row filter, diagram highlight logic. Contract: acknowledge route against `22-api-openapi.yaml`, step-up gate enforced. Integration: end-to-end latch-and-acknowledge against a machine seeded with `chain_trips > 0`. E2E: list -> detail -> diagram -> timeline -> acknowledge with step-up, refusal without step-up. a11y: axe-core plus a manual pass on the diagram and timeline (non-visual equivalents for state/edges).

## Security notes
The acknowledge action is a dangerous action per the `E09-S04` permission registry (`is_dangerous`); it is audited at high severity with actor, machine, and prior `chain_trips` count, and it never reveals context values not already redacted by the read API.

## Accessibility notes
The state diagram and event timeline provide a non-visual equivalent (a text list of states/edges and a table for the timeline) so the screen is usable without the rendered diagram; the acknowledge control has an explicit accessible name naming the machine, not a generic "Confirm".

## Performance notes
Diagram and timeline are read from the E42-T07 API; live updates ride the existing `E17-T08` topic rather than a per-screen poll.

## Observability
`cv_machine_latch_acknowledged_total`, reusing the `cv_machine_*` families from `E50-T60`.

## Definition of Done
Per `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2; Security engineer sign-off on the acknowledge gate; design-qa and QA sign-off absorbed into E42-D05/E42-Q04 per the plan's one-line Scope additions.

## Dependencies

`docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4 (chain_trips latch), §4d; `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md`; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md`.

title: Implement account-access grants: soft revoke and revoked-frame push
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner items it relies on (O2, O4) are accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S8–S9: the account-access grant set behind `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access`.

US-ADMIN-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) requires that revoking an account grant force-closes the user's WS subscriptions for that account, and `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §9.5 re-evaluates authorisation on every change to a user's account grants. The frame is `revoked` with reason `account_scope_changed`, not `unsubscribed` (§9.5). E42-T04's contract slice S1 corrects the OpenAPI wording on this route and adds its 403 for a self-target (R3, R4).

Grant removal is a soft revoke (O4): `can_view=false, can_trade=false`, never a `DELETE`, so the freeze columns and `max_daily_loss_usd` survive (`services/api/candleviewer/db/models.py`). Delete-then-regrant would silently unfreeze a frozen manager without `risk.unfreeze_manager` (C-12.5).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S8 account-access store** (`feat(accounts-admin): account-access store (E42-T08)`, branch `feat/e42-t08-access-store`, ~340 LOC):
  - Replace a user's grant set in one transaction, with a write-ahead `users.access_change` audit record (R5).
  - Removed grants become soft revokes (O4); an unknown account rolls the whole change back.
  - A grant change on a user who is not `active` returns 409.
  - A disable racing a replacement leaves no live grant.
  - Onboarding's `_BOUND` reader (`storage/repositories/onboarding_sqlalchemy.py`), the one reader that does not filter on `can_view`, ignores revoked grants.
- **S9 serve GET/PUT account-access** (`feat(accounts-admin): serve GET/PUT account-access (E42-T08)`, branch `feat/e42-t08-access-route`, ~360 LOC):
  - `GET` and `PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` per the contract from E42-T04 slice S1: Owner-only and deny by default; `PUT` is step-up gated for the `users` action class (`04-security-program.md` §7.2.1: step-up for write).
  - After commit, push `grants_changed` (`ws/permissions.py`, with #2318) so every affected subscription ends with `revoked` (`account_scope_changed`) within 2 s and a resubscribe gets `account_scope_denied`.
  - Self-target → 403; unknown account → 404; audit unavailable → 503 `audit_unavailable`.
  - Removing the user's last grant while their open-position count is unknown needs `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (O2). The change records `positions_decision=leave` and the open-position count; it never flattens positions or cancels orders.
  - The route's row in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` flips to `executed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on grant revocation or its `revoked` push, which enforce RBAC (C-4.14). S8 adds no route, and `GET|PUT /users/{userId}/account-access` stay `not_mounted` in the RBAC matrix until S9 serves them. This follows R8's proposal on #965, which has no recorded decision yet (#2710); C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas, the disable cascade and `DELETE /users/{userId}` (E42-T04).
- User read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09); the deferred purge (E42-T10).
- Flattening positions or cancelling orders on unbind (O2): flatten-first stays a separate OMS action.
- Version counters such as `grants_version` (dropped by R7).
- The grant editor UI (E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC3 Grant revocation ends the subscription with a revoked frame
  Given manager M is subscribed to positions for account S
  When an owner revokes M's grant for S
  Then within 2 seconds on a fake clock the subscription is terminated with a revoked frame whose reason is account_scope_changed, not unsubscribed
  And a resubscribe attempt for S fails with account_scope_denied

Scenario: Soft revoke keeps the freeze state and the cap
  Given M's grant for account S is frozen and carries a max_daily_loss_usd cap
  When the grant is revoked and later granted again
  Then the freeze state and the cap are unchanged

Scenario (failure): Self-target is refused
  When an owner changes their own account access
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): An unknown account rolls the change back
  When the replacement grant set names an account that does not exist
  Then the call returns 404 and no grant changes

Scenario (failure): The user is not active
  Given M is invited, locked or disabled
  When an owner replaces M's grants
  Then the call returns 409 and no grant changes

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls GET or PUT /users/{userId}/account-access
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC7 Last grant with unknown positions
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner removes M's last grant without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner replaces M's grants
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC3 moved here with its scope, and AC7 and AC8 apply to this route as well.

## Technical notes / design
- One transaction (R7): lock the user row, apply the replacement set as soft revokes and upserts, run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead, then commit. The audit writer is WAL-first and outside the database transaction (`audit/writer.py`), so the record is written only after the constraints pass. After commit, push `grants_changed`; a failure there is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- No `grants_version` counter (R7): it would add per-frame database reads in the WS lane. Pushes go through `grants_changed` plus #2318's versioned permission snapshots.
- Every other grant reader already filters on `can_view` (`storage/repositories/identity_sqlalchemy.py`, `rules/scope_state.py`); S8 fixes onboarding's `_BOUND`.
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, a `PUT` without a live step-up), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7), and `audit_unavailable` (503), which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4). The route takes no `If-Match`, so `version_conflict` (412) does not apply.
- Until #2525 merged (2026-10-15), WS private topics were deny-all in the deployed app, so AC3 could be proven only in-process. The real backend now loads the WS principal from the store (`build_ws_principal_loader` in `app.py`), so AC3 can be proven end to end there as well.

## Test plan
- **S8** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_replace_write_ahead_audit`; `test_keeps_freeze_and_cap`; IDOR `test_unknown_account_rolls_back`; `test_non_active_user_409`; `test_disable_vs_replace_race_no_live_grant`; `test_onboarding_ignores_revoked`.
- **S9:** `test_revoked_frame_within_2s` (AC3); `test_resubscribe_scope_denied` (AC3); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_self_target_403`; `test_stepup_and_audit_503` (AC8); `test_unknown_account_404`; `test_last_grant_needs_ack` (AC7).
- The 2-second bound runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`. The user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and therefore before S9.
- Elevation of privilege: grant mutation is Owner-only, step-up gated, cannot target the acting user, and is audited (SR-055).
- Tampering with risk state: soft revoke keeps freeze state and caps, so revoking and re-granting cannot unfreeze a manager (C-12.5).
- IDOR: an unknown or foreign account rolls the whole change back.
- Data classification: grants are Confidential.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task. The grant editor UI is E42-S03.

## Performance notes
- A grant change completes within 300 ms p95, excluding the post-commit push.
- The `revoked` frame reaches affected subscriptions within 2 s (AC3).

## Observability
- Audit: `users.access_change` with before and after, registered in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits it (R5).
- Post-commit push failures are counted and alerted (R7).
- Logs: one structured line per step with its outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] Both slices merged; S8 says `Refs #2648` plus `Partial: slice 1 of 2`, and S9 carries the closing line for #2648.
- [ ] Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules; RBAC matrix row `executed`.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on both slices.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E42-T04` — its slice S1 lands the contract first (C-6.1), and S9 builds on its route slice S6.
- #2318 (versioned WS permission snapshots) before S9. #2525, which an end-to-end proof in the deployed app needed, merged on 2026-10-15.
- Feeds E38-S07 (an eligibility field on this route), which lists this Task in `blocked_by`, and E42-S03 (user detail with role and account binding), which does not yet (#2710, item 4).
- Open in #2710: this Task's estimate, an author proposal sized from the slice LOC (C-11.1 #7), and the flag record (R8).

`feat/e42-t08-access-store` (S8), then `feat/e42-t08-access-route` (S9).

- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-002

- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.3, §9.5
