title: Implement user read/PATCH, role changes under owner lock and admin sessions
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner item it relies on (O3) is accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S10–S12: the user read model with an ETag, `PATCH /users/{userId}`, role and status changes under the owner lock, and the admin view of a target user's sessions.

US-ADMIN-001 and US-ADMIN-002 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) need last-owner protection: at least one enabled Owner must always exist (SR-055; `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D6), enforced in one transaction under a lock so two concurrent demotions cannot both succeed. C-12.2 makes TOTP mandatory for every user, so `mfa_required: false` is refused (O3). R4 adds the admin session routes and a `getUser` ETag to the contract in E42-T04 slice S1, and R6 fixes the status rules.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S10 GET user with an ETag; PATCH name and MFA flag** (`feat(accounts-admin): GET user with ETag and PATCH name and MFA flag (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-get-patch-user`, ~330 LOC):
  - `GET /users/{userId}` returns an ETag that changes when the user's roles change.
  - `PATCH /users/{userId}` honours `If-Match`; a stale ETag gets 412.
  - `mfa_required: false` gets 400 `validation_failed` for every target role (O3).
  - `password_hash` is never returned.
  - Owner-only, step-up for the `users` action class, audited; audit unavailable gets 503 `audit_unavailable`.
- **S11 status and roles under the owner lock** (`feat(accounts-admin): PATCH status and roles under the owner lock (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-patch-status-roles`, ~360 LOC):
  - `PATCH` changes status only between `active` and `disabled`; `invited` or `locked` gets 400 (R6).
  - Status changes and `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` take the owner lock from #2508, so of two parallel cross-demotions exactly one wins and the other gets 409 `conflict`, in each of 10 rounds (AC4).
  - A `PATCH` disable racing a demotion keeps at least one enabled Owner (AC6).
  - A `PATCH` to `disabled` calls E42-T04's disable service, so it runs the whole cascade (sessions through B16, sockets with 4403, rules, grants, an open invite) rather than only changing the status column (SR-029). While the open-position count is unknown it needs `acknowledge_unknown_positions=true`, otherwise 409 `positions_unknown` (O2, AC7), exactly as `DELETE /users/{userId}` does; E42-T04 slice S1 adds the parameter to `updateUser`.
  - Enabling a user never restores their grants or sessions (R6).
- **S12 admin user sessions** (`feat(accounts-admin): admin user sessions (E42-T09)`, branch `feat/e42-t09-admin-sessions`, ~300 LOC):
  - `GET /users/{userId}/sessions` and `DELETE /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}` (R4): step-up for the `users` action class; a session that belongs to another user gets 404.
  - No token material in any response.
  - Each revoked session writes one `auth.session_revoked` record ahead of the change, by recording B16 REVOKE as `reset_totp` does (R5).
  - The revoked session's socket closes with 4401 within 5 s.
- Each route's row in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` flips to `executed`.
- **Flag (C-4.13, C-4.14).** No runtime flag on the owner lock, step-up or audit (C-4.14). `GET` and `PATCH /users/{userId}` stay `not_mounted` until S10 serves them, and the admin session routes until S12. Still open: what S10's `PATCH` answers to a `status` change before S11 lands. Both follow R8 on #965, which has no recorded decision yet (#2710); C-11.1 #13 needs one before this Task is marked Ready.

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas and the disable cascade (E42-T04); grants (E42-T08); the deferred purge, including cancelling a pending purge on re-enable (E42-T10).
- `GET /users`, `/roles` and `/permissions` list routes (R9 on #965 proposes a separate ticket; not yet decided).
- Self-service sessions (`/me/sessions`, E09).
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario (failure): AC4 Parallel cross-demotions leave an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two enabled owners
  When A's session demotes B to manager while B's session demotes A, in parallel
  Then exactly one of the two requests succeeds and the other returns 409 conflict
  And at least one enabled owner remains
  And the same holds in each of 10 rounds, every round starting again from two enabled owners

Scenario (failure): AC6 A disable racing a demotion keeps an owner
  Given owners A and B are the only two owners
  When a demotion of A races a PATCH that disables B
  Then at least one enabled owner remains
  And the losing call writes no audit record

Scenario: A PATCH disable runs the whole disable cascade
  Given manager M has an active session, an open socket and an armed rule
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with status disabled and acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the outcome is the same as for DELETE /users/{userId}: M's next REST call gets 401, every socket of M receives bye with reason user_disabled and closes with 4403, and M's rule is disarmed
  And exactly one users.disable record is written

Scenario (failure): AC7 A PATCH disable with unknown positions needs the acknowledgement
  Given M's open-position count is unknown
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with status disabled and without acknowledge_unknown_positions=true
  Then the call returns 409 positions_unknown and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): MFA cannot be switched off
  When an owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with mfa_required false
  Then the call returns 400 validation_failed whatever the target's role

Scenario (failure): A stale ETag is refused
  Given an owner read user M and holds M's ETag
  And M's roles changed since
  When the owner sends PATCH /users/{userId} with that ETag in If-Match
  Then the call returns 412 and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): Only active and disabled are settable
  When an owner sets M's status to invited or locked
  Then the call returns 400 and nothing changes

Scenario (edge): Re-enabling restores nothing
  Given M was disabled, losing M's grants and sessions
  When an owner re-enables M
  Then M is active with no grants and no sessions restored

Scenario: The owner revokes one of M's sessions
  Given manager M has two sessions
  When an owner deletes one of them through DELETE /users/{userId}/sessions/{sessionId}
  Then one auth.session_revoked record is written before the change
  And that session's socket closes with 4401 within 5 seconds on a fake clock
  And M's other session is untouched and no response carries token material

Scenario (failure): A session of another user is not found
  When an owner deletes a session id that belongs to a user other than {userId}
  Then the call returns 404 and nothing changes

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls any route of this Task
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario (failure): AC8 Audit unavailable
  Given the audit writer is unavailable
  When an owner sends any mutation of this Task
  Then the call returns 503 audit_unavailable and nothing changes
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC4 moved here with its scope, and AC6, AC7 and AC8 apply to these routes as well (AC7 to a `PATCH` to `disabled`). AC4 runs as 10 rounds of one cross-demotion pair, so every outcome is fixed. A repeat of a demotion that already took effect is a state-based no-op that succeeds and changes nothing, as the shipped `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` route and E42-T04's AC5 treat a repeat.

## Technical notes / design
- One transaction per mutation (R7): lock the user row, lock the owner rows as #2508 does, apply the change, run `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE`, write the audit record ahead, then commit. After commit, end sockets and record B16 transitions; a failure there is counted and alerted, never rolled back.
- The ETag covers the fields `GET /users/{userId}` returns, roles included, so a role change makes an earlier ETag stale.
- `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` keeps its shipped `{id, roles}` body, which E42-T04 slice S1 documents (R4).
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`: `validation_failed` (400), `unauthenticated` (401), `forbidden` (403), `step_up_required` (403, a mutation without a live step-up), `not_found` (404), `conflict` (409), `positions_unknown` (409, AC7), `version_conflict` (412, a stale `If-Match`), and `audit_unavailable` (503), which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4).

## Test plan
- **S10:** `test_etag_tracks_roles`; `test_no_password_hash`; `test_stale_if_match_412`; `test_mfa_required_false_400` (O3); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_step_up_and_audit_503` (AC8).
- **S11** (Postgres, `@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_ten_parallel_demotions_one_wins` (AC4); `test_patch_disable_vs_demote_keeps_owner` (AC6); property test `test_owner_always_remains`; `test_enable_no_regrant`; `test_invited_or_locked_400`; `test_patch_disable_runs_disable_cascade`; `test_patch_disable_positions_unknown_409` (AC7).
- **S12:** `test_no_token_material`; IDOR `test_other_users_session_404`; `test_revoked_audit_ahead`; `test_audit_down_503` (AC8); `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; `test_socket_4401_within_5s`.
- Time-bound assertions run on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`; the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and so before these routes.
- Elevation of privilege: role and status changes are Owner-only, step-up gated, cannot target the acting user, and are audited (SR-055).
- Denial of service: removing the last Owner would lock the installation out, hence the locked owner check (§5.7 D6).
- Information disclosure: no token material or `password_hash` in any response. A session id that belongs to a user other than `{userId}` answers 404, so one user's sessions cannot be reached through another user's path (IDOR).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, session IP); Confidential (roles).

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task. The admin UI is E42-S02 and E42-S03.

## Performance notes
- Mutations complete within 300 ms p95; the owner lock is held for one short transaction.
- A revoked session's socket closes within 5 s.

## Observability
- Audit: `users.enable` (R5), `users.disable` for a `PATCH` disable, `roles.grant` and `roles.revoke`, and one `auth.session_revoked` per revoked session, all with before and after where they apply. New actions register in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits them.
- Post-commit step failures are counted and alerted (R7).
- Logs: one structured line per step with its outcome, correlated by `request_id`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] All three slices merged; S10 and S11 say `Refs #2649` plus `Partial: slice k of 3`, and S12 carries the closing line for #2649.
- [ ] Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules; RBAC matrix rows `executed`.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on every slice.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E42-T04` — its slice S1 lands the contract first (C-6.1), and S10 and S12 build on its route slice S6.
- #2508 (owner lock and write-ahead audit for role changes) before S11.
- Feeds E42-S02 and E42-S03; neither is a `blocked_by` edge yet (#2710).
- E42-T10's S14 lands after S11 and adds the purge cancel to S11's enable path.
- Open in #2710: this Task's estimate, an author proposal sized from the slice LOC (C-11.1 #7), and the flag record (R8).

## Branch
`feat/e42-t09-get-patch-user` (S10), `feat/e42-t09-patch-status-roles` (S11), `feat/e42-t09-admin-sessions` (S12).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-001, US-ADMIN-002
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/roles`, `/users/{userId}/sessions`, `/me/sessions`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 (`users`, `user_roles`, `sessions`)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7, SR-055
- `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` U4, U24, U25
- `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` B16 (session REVOKE)
- #965 (DoR plan and decision record, 2026-10-15)


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. The DoR plan and decision record on #965 (2026-10-15): O3, R2–R7
2. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/users/{userId}`, `/users/{userId}/roles` and `/users/{userId}/sessions`, as amended by E42-T04 slice S1
3. `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 and SR-055
4. `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` B16

**Repo paths to create/modify**

- `services/api/candleviewer/storage/repositories/` (`users_sqlalchemy.py`, `sessions_sqlalchemy.py`)
- `services/api/candleviewer/auth/` (session revocation through B16, as `reset_totp` does)
- `services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py` (register `users.enable`)

- The `PUT /users/{userId}/roles` `{id, roles}` body as shipped
- The B16 session contract (`machines/B16.session.machine.json`); revoke only through its REVOKE event

**Commands**
- `ruff check .` (from `services/api/`)
- `black --check .` (from `services/api/`)
- `mypy --strict .` (from `services/api/`)
- `lint-imports` (from `services/api/`)
- `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85` (from `services/api/`)
- `pytest -m integration` (from `services/api/`, needs the docker compose stack)

**Branch & PR**
- Branches: `feat/e42-t09-get-patch-user`, `feat/e42-t09-patch-status-roles`, `feat/e42-t09-admin-sessions`

title: Implement deferred PII purge: purge columns, anonymisation reaper, ?purge=true
body:
## Context
Split from E42-T04 (#965) on 2026-10-15 by R2 of the DoR plan on #965, accepted by the orchestrator; the owner item it relies on (O6) is accepted on an interim basis, subject to owner veto on #2701, which continues #1778 (now closed) and lists #965 O1–O7 among the interim decisions open to veto. This Task owns plan slices S2, S13 and S14: deferred PII anonymisation after a user is deleted with `?purge=true`.

US-ADMIN-001 (`docs/plan/11-user-stories.md`) requires that a deleted user's "audit and journal history is retained under an anonymised reference, and the deletion itself is audited". O6 fixes how:
- The surrogate is `deleted-user-` followed by the first 12 hex characters of SHA-256(`cv-user-surrogate:` + user id); the email becomes `<surrogate>@deleted.invalid`.
- `display_name` and `last_login_ip`, and the `ip`, `user_agent`, `device_label` and `tailscale_node` of the user's sessions, are nulled. Main has no session reaper (`storage/retention/schedule.py`), so this Task's reaper does it.
- Two nullable columns, `users.purge_after` and `users.anonymised_at`, carry the schedule.
- Audit rows keep the name they were written with: `auth.login` stores the typed identifier and invites store the username, and audit is never updated (C-5.7, C-12.8). Lifecycle audit records therefore carry ids, status and roles only.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §12 is corrected to match.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **S2 users purge columns** (`feat(accounts-admin): users purge columns (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-users-purge-columns`, ~150 LOC): one Alembic revision adding nullable `users.purge_after` and `users.anonymised_at`. Additive and reversible (C-5.1, C-5.2); exactly one revision, re-parented onto the head current when it lands (C-5.3): #2516 merged `0023_replay_sessions` on 2026-10-15, and #2614 (open) claims 0024; round trip on an empty and a seeded database (C-5.5).
- **S13 anonymisation reaper** (`feat(accounts-admin): anonymisation reaper (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-purge-reaper`, ~350 LOC): anonymises only users whose `purge_after` has passed, in bounded batches; writes `users.anonymise` ahead of each user (R5); sets `anonymised_at`; never updates an audit row.
- **S14 `DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true`** (`feat(accounts-admin): DELETE user with purge (E42-T10)`, branch `feat/e42-t10-purge-route`, ~300 LOC): on top of E42-T04's disable, schedules `purge_after` 90 days out and writes `users.delete` ahead (R5). Re-enabling the user before `purge_after` cancels the pending purge (R6): S14 adds that step to the enable path of E42-T09's S11. Owner-only, step-up for the `users` action class, audited.
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`: §3.1 gains the two columns and §12 the anonymisation rules (O6).
- **Flag: open.** R8 on #965 proposes a `users_purge_enabled` Settings field, default off, gating only `?purge=true` until S14; it has no recorded decision yet (#2710). Record one before S14 starts and before this Task is marked Ready (C-11.1 #13). No flag gates any step of the disable cascade (C-4.14).

## Out of scope
- The contract deltas, the disable cascade and `DELETE /users/{userId}` without `purge` (E42-T04).
- Grants (E42-T08); user read/PATCH, role changes and admin sessions (E42-T09).
- Rewriting or redacting audit rows (C-5.7, C-12.8).
- Journal anonymisation: the journal is not on main yet, so it is covered by foreign-key retention only.
- The admin UI (E42-S02, E42-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: AC2 History is retained under an anonymised reference
  Given manager M was deleted with purge
  When purge_after passes on a fake clock and the reaper runs
  Then M's username is the surrogate and M's email is <surrogate>@deleted.invalid
  And M's display name, last login IP, and every session's IP, user agent, device label and Tailscale node are null
  And every audit row about M is byte-identical to before
  And M's journal history stays attached through foreign-key retention only

Scenario: Deletion and anonymisation are audited ahead
  When an owner deletes M with purge
  Then a users.delete record is written before the change
  And the reaper writes users.anonymise before it anonymises M

Scenario: The surrogate is stable and not derived from PII
  When the surrogate for a user id is computed on separate runs
  Then it is identical every time
  And it depends on the user id alone, never on the email, username or any IP

Scenario (edge): Only expired purges run
  Given M's purge_after is in the future
  When the reaper runs
  Then M is unchanged

Scenario (edge): Re-enabling cancels a pending purge
  Given M was deleted with purge and purge_after has not passed
  When an owner re-enables M
  Then purge_after is cleared and the reaper never anonymises M

Scenario (failure): Forbidden role
  When a manager or a viewer calls DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true
  Then the call returns 403 and the attempt is audited

Scenario: The migration round-trips
  When the purge-columns revision is upgraded, downgraded and upgraded again on an empty and on a seeded database
  Then every step succeeds and the downgrade removes only the two new columns
```
AC numbers follow the rewritten criteria of E42-T04 (R3): AC2 moved here with its scope.

## Technical notes / design
- The surrogate is deterministic but not reversible from PII: the hash input is a fixed domain prefix plus the user id, so historical joins still group by user while nothing about the email or name is recoverable.
- The reaper runs off the request path under the retention scheduler, takes bounded batches, and holds each user's anonymisation and its `users.anonymise` record in one transaction.
- `users.delete` and `users.anonymise` register in `audit/actions.py` in the PR that first emits them (R5).
- Error codes come only from `x-error-codes` in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, plus `audit_unavailable`, which E42-T04 slice S1 registers (R4).

## Test plan
- **S2:** `test_<rev>_adds_nullable_columns`; `test_<rev>_downgrade_only_new_columns`; upgrade, downgrade and upgrade on an empty and a seeded database. `<rev>` is the revision number the slice takes at the head when it lands, as the migration tests name themselves.
- **S13:** property tests `test_surrogate_stable` and `test_surrogate_not_from_pii`; Postgres (`@pytest.mark.integration`): `test_only_past_purge_after`, `test_audit_byte_identical` (AC2), `test_nulls_session_pii`, `test_batch_bounded`, `test_users_anonymise_ahead`.
- **S14** (Postgres): `test_history_under_surrogate_after_90d` (AC2); `test_users_delete_ahead`; `test_reenable_cancels_purge`; `test_forbidden_manager_viewer_audited`; if R8 adds a flag, a test that it is removed.
- The 90-day window runs on a fake clock; no sleeps and no network (C-13.5).
- Coverage of at least 90% on the touched audit- and RBAC-relevant modules (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` R4 coverage rule).

## Security notes
- Interim threat model (O1): `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7 D1–D6 plus U4, U24 and U25 in `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md`; the user-lifecycle STRIDE appendix (#2729) merges before E42-T04's route slice S6, and so before S14.
- Information disclosure: the surrogate must not be reversible from PII; PII columns are nulled, never copied elsewhere.
- Repudiation: deletion and anonymisation are audited ahead; audit rows are never updated (C-5.7, C-12.8).
- Data classification: PII (`users.email`, `users.display_name`, `users.last_login_ip`, the session columns above, `audit_log.actor_ip`). The migration also needs the CODEOWNERS of `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/`.

## Accessibility notes
N/A — backend task.

## Performance notes
- The reaper processes bounded batches off the request path.
- `DELETE /users/{userId}?purge=true` completes within 300 ms p95.

## Observability
- Audit: `users.delete` and `users.anonymise`, registered in the PR that first emits each (R5).
- Logs: one structured line per reaper batch with its count and outcome, correlated by `request_id` for the route.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every scenario above passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- [ ] All three slices merged; S2 and S13 say `Refs #2650` plus `Partial: slice k of 3`, and S14 carries the closing line for #2650.
- [ ] Migration round trip on an empty and a seeded database attached to S2; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 and §12 updated.
- [ ] The R8 flag decision recorded and applied before S14.
- [ ] Security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals on every slice.
- [ ] QA sign-off recorded (or an explicit QA capacity deviation note).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by: E42-T04` — its slice S1 lands the contract first (C-6.1); S13 builds on its disable store (S3) and S14 on its route slice (S6).
- The migration-head rule: one revision, re-parented if another lands first (#2516 merged 0023; #2614 claims 0024).
- R8 on #965 (the purge flag) before S14.
- S14 lands after E42-T09's S11, whose enable path (`PATCH` to `active`) it extends to cancel a pending purge (`test_reenable_cancels_purge`). The dependency is per slice, so it is not a task-level `blocked_by`.
- Open in #2710: this Task's estimate, an author proposal sized from the slice LOC (C-11.1 #7), and the R8 flag record.

## Branch
`feat/e42-t10-users-purge-columns` (S2), `feat/e42-t10-purge-reaper` (S13), `feat/e42-t10-purge-route` (S14).

## References
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-ADMIN-001
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `DELETE /users/{userId}`
- `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 (`users`, `sessions`), §3.10 (audit log), §12 (PII classification)
- `docs/plan/04-security-program.md` §5.7
- `docs/security/threat-models/e09-auth-rbac.md` U24
- #965 (DoR plan and decision record, 2026-10-15)


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. The DoR plan and decision record on #965 (2026-10-15): O6, R2–R8
2. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §3.1 and §12
3. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `DELETE /users/{userId}`, as amended by E42-T04 slice S1

- `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/versions/` (one new revision)
- `services/api/candleviewer/db/models.py` (the two columns)
- `services/api/candleviewer/storage/retention/` (the anonymisation reaper)
- `services/api/candleviewer/api/users.py` (`?purge=true`)
- `services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py` (register `users.delete` and `users.anonymise`)

- `services/api/tests/` (unit, property, integration and migration tests)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- REST paths: `/users`, `/users/{userId}`
- `audit_log` rows: never updated (C-5.7)
- Every applied migration: never edited (C-5.4)

**Commands**
- `ruff check .` (from `services/api/`)

- `pytest -m integration` (from `services/api/`, needs the docker compose stack)
- `alembic upgrade head` / `alembic downgrade -1` (from `services/api/`)

**Branch & PR**

- PR titles: `feat(accounts-admin): <slice summary> (E42-T10)`
- PR description: S2 and S13 `Refs #2650` plus `Partial: slice k of 3`; S14 carries the closing line for #2650
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend @CandleViewer/security @CandleViewer/architecture
- Labels: type/feature, area/accounts-admin, priority/p0, security, qa

**Done means**
- Every scenario in this ticket passes as an automated test; Postgres cases run as `@pytest.mark.integration`.
- All three slices merged with security-reviewer and code-reviewer approvals; the migration round trip is attached.

**Do NOT**
- Update, redact or delete any audit row (C-5.7, C-12.8).
- Derive the surrogate from the email, username or any IP.
- Add more than one migration, or edit an applied one (C-5.3, C-5.4).
- Gate any disable-cascade step behind a flag (C-4.14).
- Implement anything listed under this ticket's Out of scope.

**If blocked**
- Comment on #2650 in the BLOCKER format of `.claude/rules/70-multi-agent.md` §5, naming the blocking key (E42-T04, the R8 decision, a migration-head conflict, the STRIDE appendix #2729), and move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not work around a failing gate or widen scope.
